reviews.summary: `nerva chat -z "prompt"` runs one turn non-interactively and puts only the final assistant text on stdout — whole escape sequences and C0/C1 control bytes stripped, newlines and tabs kept — with every other word on stderr. The prompt resolves the way `nerva send`'s body does (argument, else `-f PATH` where `-` is stdin, else piped stdin) and a terminal is never read, by either spelling: `-f /dev/tty` is refused rather than blocking forever. A prompt over the hub's own 4,096-character `ChatRequest` bound is a usage error before the request, not an HTTP 422 a script reads as a failed turn. The ladder is stated in `--help`: 0 answered · 1 the turn did not complete · 2 usage · 3 no hub · 4 not authorised · 130 interrupted; Ctrl-C returns 130 with one stderr line instead of an uncaught traceback that could spill a partial answer. **The governance clause is implemented against Hermes, not after it:** no flag auto-approves, a turn that queues an action stays queued, and the verb exits 1 naming the pending id to decide with `nerva approvals`; a test asserts the one-shot path issues no decision call at all. For a queued action the verdict no longer rests on the reply text. The hub reports what the turn queued: `ChatResponse.pending_approvals` on `POST /chat`, and the same list on `/chat/stream`'s end event. A per-turn collector (`agents/core/turn_approvals.py`) gathers the ids at the gated Tool-RPC enqueue, and they are still reported when the turn raised after queuing. Any reported id makes `-z` exit 1 with the id on stderr, whatever the reply says, so a model that writes a plausible answer around a queued action does not exit 0. The reply text is a second detector, for stops that queue nothing and for a hub that reports no ids. It is matched by containment over the sanitised text, so the deterministic `[athena]: …` join that the synthesis pass falls back to still matches. The table holds the approval reply, the busy/compaction/continuation refusals, the no-local-model reply, the hub's two failure replies, the five tool-loop stops and a prefix rule for the stop built with an f-string. A drift test imports the ten runtime constants and asserts each is matched both verbatim and wrapped. Sanitising happens before the verdict, so a reply of pure control bytes is an incomplete turn rather than exit 0 and a blank line. `--usage-file PATH` writes `nerva.chat.usage.v1` atomically on every path including the interrupt, cleans up its temp file when a write fails, survives a field it cannot encode (a warning, never a crash after the answer is already out), says so when given an empty path, and refuses to call a turn completed while naming an approval it left queued. A hub that reports `pending_approvals` in a shape this version cannot read is told so, rather than the string being exploded into one fabricated id per character. 51 tests in tests/test_nerva_oneshot.py; the hub-side report is pinned by tests/test_turn_pending_approvals.py.
reviews.remaining: Two parts of the row are open. (1) THE SPEND HALF IS A SCHEMA OF NULLS. The hub cannot attribute one turn's cost. `AgentConfig.model` defaults to `google/gemma-4-31b-a4b` and none of the 18 agents in `agents/_system/agents.yaml` declares a model, so `cost_tracker` meters every turn at the default price row and reports $0.00; an id it does not know is priced from the `default` row with no `priced` flag. `estimated_cost_usd`, the token counts, `api_calls`, `model` and `provider` are therefore `null` with `cost_basis: "unavailable"` rather than measured zeros, and a test pins that they never become numbers. (2) A STOP THAT QUEUES NOTHING IS STILL JUDGED BY TEXT, AND ON A LIVE HUB THAT TEXT IS USUALLY REWRITTEN. The hub reports ids only for approvals queued through the gated Tool-RPC path. The tool loop's own stops are recognised only by containment over the reply. A turn routed to a specialist is not handed back verbatim: the orchestrator sends it through synthesis (`was_synthesized = len(responses) > 1 or "jarvis" not in responses`). With a `jarvis` agent and a router loaded, `jarvis.synthesize` rewrites it through a model; only the fallbacks (no `jarvis` agent, no router, a failed synthesis call) produce the `[athena]: …` join that containment survives. So a specialist's tool-loop stop can come back reworded and exit 0. The table also has no entry for `THINKING_EXHAUSTED_REPLY` (agents.core.llm.base): a comment in the table names it, but no row follows. A reasoning model that spent its whole budget thinking is therefore printed as the answer with exit 0. Also open: `POST /chat` returns no trace, invocation or session id, so `session_id` is echoed only when the caller supplied one; `-z` does not silence hub-side logging; there is no `--output-format` beyond the existing `--json`; a piped body is read whole up to the bound rather than streamed; and `os.replace` onto a symlinked `--usage-file` path replaces the link with a regular file instead of writing through it.

reviews.summary: `nerva doctor` rulează `scripts/doctor.py` fără să schimbe nimic, cu un motiv numit pentru fiecare verificare, `--json` și `--smoke`. Are cinci verificări obligatorii (python, venv, locks_in_sync, bind_is_loopback, data_root_writable) și nouă consultative (runtimes, readyz, runtime_resolves, voice din H613, config_sources, smoke și, din H501, host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords, container_storage; scripts/doctor.py:111-113). Iese cu 1 doar când pică una obligatorie; o consultativă care pică e `warn`. Din HEQ lot 1 (H242), `runtime_resolves` verifică dacă ruta pe care o ia un turn Jarvis chiar se rezolvă la un model utilizabil, nu doar dacă răspunde un runtime. Citește verdictul strict al hub-ului, blocul `model` din `GET /api/onboarding/command-center` (același select_backend, fără generare), cu un singur credențial local: `JARVIS_USER_TOKEN`, altfel `JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN`, pe care îl trimite doar unui hub de pe această mașină, decis după adresă, nu după ortografie (scripts/doctor.py:346, scripts/doctor.py:393-400). E `ok` doar pe `ready: true` care numește ruta, providerul și modelul. Altfel dă motivul numit (`configured_not_resident`, `route_unselected`, `needs_token`, `malformed_reply` …), iar fără un hub gata e `skip`. `readyz` și această citire folosesc aceeași adresă de hub ca `nerva status` (`NERVA_HUB_URL`, altfel `JARVIS_HOST`/`JARVIS_PORT`; o adresă wildcard e apelată prin loopback). Din H273, `config_sources` arată, informativ, din ce strat vine fiecare cheie de configurare (mediul procesului > `.env`-ul repo-ului > `.env`-ul din data home) și ce valori din `.env` sunt acoperite de un strat de mai sus — doar nume, niciodată o valoare. `nerva status` arată același verdict pe o linie `runnable:`, separat de vechiul `model_state`, afișat acum „resident”. Alte diagnostice sunt verbe separate: `nerva desktop status` (ce îi lipsește host-ului pentru operatorul desktop), `nerva security audit` (vulnerabilități cunoscute, prin OSV) și `nerva extensions doctor`.
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc jumătățile de reparare și de operare ale rândului: nu există `--fix` (reparări numite, în tier reversibil, cu tot ce atinge credențiale sau postura pus în coada de aprobare), `--live` (rulare continuă) sau `--ack ADVISORY_ID`. Lipsesc și verificările cerute pentru o instalare deja configurată: accesibilitatea serverelor MCP, token-urile canalelor, postura kernel/flag-uri, integritatea lanțului de audit și credențialele/conectivitatea fiecărui provider configurat. `runtime_resolves` judecă doar ruta pe care o ia acum un turn Jarvis, iar o rută cloud trece pe decizia de disponibilitate a routerului, fără un apel care să verifice credențialul la provider.

reviews.remaining: Randul cere orice platforma configurata. Nerva expune doar canalele direct-send (telegram, web, voice, ntfy), iar web nu e gata cat timp niciun client nu e conectat la el: HUD-ul nu conecteaza unul, asa ca `nerva send --list` si /api/channels/targets il arata ca nepregatit, cu motivul (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:88). Slack si Discord sunt reply-only prin brokerul channel.reply si nu pot fi adresate de `send`; email-ul e exclus deliberat, ca mailul inbound neincrezut sa nu capete efect SMTP.

reviews.summary: `nerva security audit` inventariază distribuțiile interpretorului curent și pinurile Python exacte ale descriptorilor de extensie numiți, întreabă OSV.dev prin `PluginHTTPClient` (rezoluție DNS pinată, ancorele TLS ale owner-ului, breaker; querybatch în loturi de 1000 cu paginare urmărită + un detaliu per advisory; pleacă doar perechi nume+versiune, anunțate pe stderr), unește oglinzile GHSA/PYSEC ale aceluiași CVE într-o singură constatare cu cea mai mare severitate declarată, numește fix-ul din intervalul care conține versiunea instalată și iese 0/1/5. Un advisory fără severitate declarată pică orice prag; o bază de date de neatins, un lot rămas paginat după 20 de pagini sau un audit care nu se încheie înseamnă exit 5 și nicio afirmație. O distribuție cu metadate nedecodabile e sărită și numită; textul advisory-urilor e curățat de caractere de control înainte de terminal. MCP (comenzi stdio configurate de owner) e listat ca neauditat, cu motivul. Probat live: 48 distribuții curate; un pin `requests 2.19.0` dă 5 constatări după unirea a 5 oglinzi PYSEC. Recenzie adversarială independentă: nouă defecte, toate remediate în același PR.
reviews.remaining: Suprafața MCP nu e auditată: comenzile stdio (`npx …`, `uvx …`) din configurația persistată nu sunt rezolvate la pachete și versiuni. Descriptorii de extensie trebuie numiți pe linia de comandă; catalogul pachetelor achiziționate e pe partea hub-ului și nu e citit offline. Nu există `nerva security` implicit (cli-d.security-default) și nici `--skip-venv/--skip-plugins/--skip-mcp`. Vectorii CVSS nu sunt scorați: un advisory doar cu vector rămâne `unknown` și pică orice prag dacă nu se unește cu un frate GHSA evaluat. Pragul implicit `--fail-on low` e deliberat mai strict decât `critical` din Hermes. Nu există setare de proxy pentru operator (H281). Din procesul CLI nu există mediere kernel și registrul de egress nu persistă. Scara de ieșire e cea Nerva (0/1/2/5), nu 0/1/2 din Hermes. Fără probă pe o mașină fără proxy transparent.

reviews.summary: The port-conflict diagnostic, plus one stale line of evidence corrected. `serve.py` gains `probe_bind(host, port)`, called from `main()` after the posture guards and before uvicorn binds: a taken port prints the exact address, the command that identifies the holder (`nerva status`) and the way out (`JARVIS_PORT`), then exits **12**; `EACCES` exits **13**, and since #1177 that arm branches on the port number instead of asserting a cause it cannot know — below 1024 it names the privileged-port rule (root or `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`; move `JARVIS_PORT` above 1024), at or above 1024 it says outright that this is *not* the privileged-port rule and root/Administrator will not help, then points at the reservations that actually produce it (Windows `netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange tcp`, whose Hyper-V/WSL blocks routinely cover the shipped default 8080; an SELinux `name_bind` denial on Linux) plus `JARVIS_PORT`. Both codes are deliberately distinct from uvicorn's `STARTUP_FAILURE` (3), which it uses for *every* startup failure — that collision was the actual defect, because a supervisor could not tell "the port is taken" from "the lifespan crashed". The probe is a **diagnostic, not a lock**: it binds and closes, reserves nothing, and any `OSError` outside the two named arms is swallowed, so an unexpected probe failure can never turn a boot that would have worked into a refusal. The socket **constructor sits inside the guarded region** too — a first cut that built it above the `try` turned `JARVIS_HOST=::1` on a box with no IPv6 stack into an 8-frame traceback + exit 1 in place of uvicorn's one-line error + exit 3, the diagnostic making the boot worse than no diagnostic. It also mirrors asyncio's own flags rather than stricter ones: `SO_REUSEADDR` on POSIX, because `uvicorn.Server.startup` binds through `loop.create_server` where asyncio sets it, so a probe without it would refuse a port merely holding a TIME_WAIT connection from the instance the owner just stopped — a boot uvicorn would have completed; and `IPV6_V6ONLY` on an AF_INET6 probe, so an IPv4 listener on the same port cannot turn a working v6 boot into exit 12. **The frozen 2026-09-07 evidence was stale on one point**: it recorded "no --status", but `nerva status` has existed since the unified CLI (the `status` verb in `agents/cli/nerva.py`). 13 `test_probe_bind_*` functions, 16 collected cases (the IPv6-conflict case skips on a box with no IPv6 stack). Both exit codes are asserted **by execution** rather than by reading the branch — the sub-1024 `EACCES` arm runs in a child dropped to an unprivileged uid with `setpriv`, because pytest runs as root here and a sub-1024 bind simply succeeds; the high-port `EACCES` arm is driven through a stubbed `bind()` that answers `EACCES`, parametrised over 1024/8080/49152/65535, because its real reproduction is a Windows excluded port range that cannot be staged on Linux, and a sibling test pins that port 80 still gets the privileged-port sentence. ENV-122 in `docs/test-manual/01-environment-and-boot.md` moves from a message-quality finding to an asserted string plus exit code.
reviews.remaining: Hermes's row is start, check **and stop**, and the stop half is entirely absent: no `stop` verb, no pidfile, no ready file. The row cites `hermes dashboard --status/--stop` plus backend ready sentinels and a ready file (06-cli-f.md, 16 entries); Nerva has `nerva status`, which reads the HTTP surface and so cannot report a hub that is starting or wedged before the port opens, and Ctrl-C. Hermes also signals the conflict as a machine-readable `BACKEND_PORT_IN_USE`, where this slice signals it as an exit code and an English sentence — enough for a supervisor, not enough for a caller parsing a status stream. Not delivered either: `--isolated`, `--skip-build`, `--no-open`, the SSH session-token file and owner-nonce, or the interactive auth-setup prompt. **One known limit, in the safe direction:** the probe picks a single address family from the host string while uvicorn binds every address `getaddrinfo` returns, so a dual-stack name like `localhost` is probed on v4 only and can miss a conflict held on the v6 address — it misses silently, and uvicorn then reports it exactly as it does today. The Windows half of the `SO_REUSEADDR` choice is read off asyncio's `reuse_address = os.name == "posix"` line and has never been executed here; that test skips off POSIX and the docstring says so.

reviews.summary: Drumul de la instalare la prima apăsare există acum. `nerva desktop status` citește faptele tri-state ale sondei de gazdă și le redă ca o cale ordonată — sesiune grafică, bibliotecile driverului, granturile de sistem, elevare — cu prima piedică numită explicit; `nerva desktop grant <pas>` deschide panoul unde owner-ul acordă permisiunea și nu acordă nimic el însuși. Un fapt pe care sonda nu l-a putut stabili se redă `unknown`, niciodată `ready`. Tabelul de deschidere e o constantă de modul, verificată prin identitate, deci seam-ul nu poate deveni o cale de lansat orice.
reviews.remaining: Rândul cere și jumătatea de instalare pe care Nerva o rezolvă altfel: Hermes are `computer-use install` care aduce și repară un binar cua străin, plus `status` și `doctor` separate. Nerva își construiește propriile drivere, deci nu există binar de adus — dar nu există nici instalarea dependențelor opționale dintr-o comandă (pywinauto/uiautomation/pyobjc/PyGObject rămân în sarcina owner-ului), nici un `doctor` dedicat operatorului, nici o suprafață în HUD pentru aceeași cale. NEVERIFICAT pe hardware: containerul e headless, deci calea a fost probată doar pe sonde sintetice — niciun panou de sistem real nu a fost deschis și niciun grant real nu a fost observat schimbându-se.

reviews.summary: `nerva prompt-size` există și raportează costul fix per apel, pe componente, cel mai mare primul — offline, fără hub, fără backend, fără nicio cerere: citește personele de pe disc și cere registrului specurile pe care oricum le declară. Exact asta îl face utilizabil pentru întrebarea la care răspunde („cât plătesc înainte să înceapă conversația") pe o cutie unde hub-ul nici măcar nu rulează. `agents/core/prompt_size.py` sparge costul în: câte o linie per persoană de agent găsită pe disc, câte una per unealtă — costată ca **JSON-ul care chiar traversează sârma**, nu ca numele ei, fiindcă un `input_schema` stufos poate cântări cât o persoană întreagă — indexul de skill-uri randat exact cum îl randează `build_prompt`, și schela de tură pe care fiecare cerere o plătește. Numărul pe care raportul îl scoate în față e **podeaua per apel**, nu suma: cele 18 persoane sunt listate separat fiindcă o cerere reală trimite una singură, a agentului rutat. Prima versiune a raportului aduna toate cele 18 și anunța 71,8 % dintr-o fereastră de 32k, când o cerere reală plătește ~6,5 % — un număr greșit e mai rău decât niciun număr, așa că podeaua per apel e ce se citește primul și un test o fixează. Fără agent numit se folosește persoana cea mai grea, deci cifra e cazul realist cel mai prost, nu unul măgulitor; un agent inexistent nu e taxat tăcut pe seama altcuiva. Raportul spune despre el însuși că cifrele sunt estimări din aceeași funcție pe care o folosește bugetul la runtime, și trimite la H673 pentru singura măsurătoare exactă — cea raportată de provider. Ieșire text tabelară sau `--json`.
reviews.remaining: Rândul Hermes cere și componente pe care Nerva nu le are separate azi: „cele trei tiere de prompt" și „user profile" nu există ca blocuri distincte în asamblarea promptului (`Agent.build_prompt` are soul + skills + agent memory + schelă), iar `<available_skills>` e un index Hermes; echivalentul livrat e blocul `Available skills:`. Memoria nu e costată: e per sesiune și variabilă, nu cost fix, iar a o raporta ca „fix" ar fi exact tipul de cifră greșită pe care livrarea asta o evită. Schemele de unelte sunt raportate doar când i se dau: verbul nu bootează un registru, iar pe o cutie fără hub secțiunea lipsește și raportul **spune** că lipsește, în loc s-o raporteze ca zero. Cost per toolset (grupat) nu e implementat, doar per unealtă. Neverificat pe serviciu real: nicio cerere nu a fost trimisă — cifrele sunt estimări comparabile cu bugetul intern, nu contorul unui provider.

reviews.summary: A message that arrives while a turn runs on the same session waits for that session's turn lease (`Orchestrator.turn_lease`, agents/core/orchestrator.py:1711, taken by `_channel_turn` at agents/core/orchestrator.py:1648 and by the web /chat path at agents/web.py:1257). After `_TURN_LEASE_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (180 s, agents/core/orchestrator.py:263) it gets the single busy string `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:265) and no second turn starts on that transcript (tests/test_turn_lease.py:72, tests/test_turn_lease.py:118). `/pause` and `/stop` are owner-only (ADMIN tier) slash commands that engage the e-stop (agents/core/commands.py:410, agents/core/commands.py:411). They say plainly that work already in flight finishes (agents/core/commands.py:240, tests/test_slash_commands.py:124). Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability.
reviews.remaining: No busy-input semantics. A mid-turn message cannot redirect or interrupt the running turn. There is no explicit FIFO `/queue`, no `/steer` into the running turn and no configurable mode between these with downgrades. `/stop` is not a hard kill: it engages the e-stop but does not cancel the running turn or unlock the session. It is also dispatched inside `handle_input` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1973), so it waits behind the same lease. While a turn holds the lease past the wait bound, `/stop` itself is answered with `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` (named at agents/core/orchestrator.py:3742). There is one busy string, not a set of acks saying whether a message was queued, steered or interrupted. None of the protective demotions exist (running subagent, in-flight compression, photo burst, very fast follow-up merged as the same intent). The lease is the only slot reservation; there is no pending-agent sentinel. `SlashCommand` (agents/core/commands.py:61) carries no `busy_policy`.

reviews.summary: Turns are serialized per resolved session. `Orchestrator.turn_lease` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1711) holds one asyncio.Lock per key, and `_lease_key` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1701) follows `_resolve_session`'s order, so the lease names the session the turn will actually use rather than the routing key. It is taken by channel turns (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1648) and the web /chat path (agents/web.py:1257), and it is re-entrant within one turn. After 180 s a waiting message is answered `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` instead of starting (tests/test_turn_lease.py:72, tests/test_turn_lease.py:118, tests/test_turn_lease.py:104). The lease table is capped at 1024 entries and prunes unlocked locks when full (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1730, tests/test_turn_lease.py:163). The `_active_session` ContextVar (agents/core/orchestrator.py:305) keeps concurrent turns from reading or writing each other's session (tests/test_concurrent_session_isolation.py:93). reviews.remaining: No run generation lets a late callback from an abandoned turn detect that it no longer owns the session. The only compare-and-set is the checkpoint-clock commit of a compaction (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4052), and it guards a summary, not turn ownership. There is no active-session slot claimed before the first await and no `max_concurrent_sessions` cap: turns on different sessions run concurrently without bound (tests/test_turn_lease.py:88). No watchdog evicts a session whose turn is wedged: its lease stays held until the turn ends, and later messages only get the busy reply. There is no eviction of an in-memory slot whose durable routing row ended, and no single per-session `SessionState` object with explicit lifetimes. There is no per-session warm agent cache and no memory-pressure eviction. Agents are process-wide: every session shares `orchestrator.agents`, which the compaction-boundary persona refresh walks as a whole (agents/core/orchestrator.py:446).

reviews.summary: Channel conversations are designed to be forever-sessions. Orchestrator.channel_handler derives a deterministic key per channel identity with build_session_key (agents/core/channels/session.py:68, called at agents/core/orchestrator.py:1538) and resumes that same session on every turn (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1550). conversation_clock (agents/core/conversation_clock.py) only tells a long-lived session today's date. There is no reset policy, no idle or daily expiry, no reset-trigger phrase and no stall watcher: reset_policy, session_reset, idle_reset and stall-watcher terms have no matches under agents/. The only adjacent mechanism is disk retention. The H262 lifecycle sweep (run_sweep, agents/core/lifecycle_sweep.py:213) deletes archived, unpinned chats whose last activity is older than retention.conversation_ttl_days, backup first; an hourly, interval-gated job (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:184) runs it, and it deletes only when retention.enabled is on (off by default) and a person approved the horizon. It does not evict the in-memory session, so it ages records out, the analogue of session_store_max_age_days, but does not reset live context. Tests tests/test_retention.py and tests/test_channel_sessions.py pass. reviews.remaining:
1. Reset policy: idle-minutes and daily-at-hour resets, overridable per session type (dm/group/thread) and per channel, applied by rotating the channel session to a fresh id while keeping the old transcript.
2. Reset triggers: configurable texts (e.g. /new, /reset) intercepted in channel_handler before a turn runs; they start a fresh session and acknowledge it.
3. Expiry watcher: a scheduled job that applies the idle/daily policies and drops stale _channel_sessions entries.
4. Stall watcher: track inbound receipt against last turn progress per session and notify the owner once when a message has been pending past a threshold with no progress.
5. Tests for each.

reviews.remaining: The reduced set the row accepted beyond streaming is absent: no long-running 'still working, N min' message on a chat channel while a slow turn runs (`TURN_BUSY_REPLY` only answers a second message sent while a turn holds the session); no `tool_progress: log` per-turn append-only record of which tools ran; no quiet/show-tools level with a tool-progress message and its cleanup after the final answer, and no `/verbose`-style chat command to switch it (the slash-command registry has help, status, sessions, pause, stop, resume, jobs, remind and voice); no typing indicator on an ordinary text turn; no single RO/EN reply-string catalog: the decision-inbox cards still hardcode Romanian labels (`✅ Aprob`, `❌ Resping`) while channel notes and slash-command replies are English. Neither Slack nor Discord implements an edit call — no `begin_stream`, Slack posts only through `chat_postMessage`, Discord has no message PATCH — although both descriptors declare `supports_edit=True`, so the edit path is missing as well as the approval contract below. Slack and Discord replies are not streamed until one edit stream can be approved as a single `channel.reply` decision (H104). The missing typing indicator on an ordinary text turn is counted once, under H683's acknowledge-at-ingest gap.

reviews.summary: Un mesaj vocal pe Telegram e transcris înainte să-l vadă agentul — echivalentul lui `stt_enabled` din Hermes. `InboundVoiceReader` întreabă poarta înainte de descărcare, mărginește octeții, îi trimite prin `BytesIO` direct la decodor (vorbirea nu atinge discul) și transformă fiecare eșec într-un motiv numit; santinelele motorului nu ajung niciodată la model ca vorbire. Transcriptul circulă ca o tură obișnuită, nu în gard: sunt chiar cuvintele expeditorului, iar protecția reală e filtrul de halucinații (H530). Jumătatea rostită: `/voice off|voice|always` e mod per conversație (`voice_mode.py`, magazie JSON `canal:chat`, implicit off, setat de chat pentru chat), `stt_echo_transcripts` e setarea `voice.stt_echo_transcripts` (o linie de serviciu „am auzit: …” înaintea răspunsului, niciodată rostită), iar `spoken_reply.py` transformă textul livrat într-o notă vocală peste motorul TTS al gazdei — doar proza (fără cod, linkuri, marcaje), tăiată la o limită de propoziție, fișierul șters după citire, nimic din text în log. Cârligul stă unde textul chiar ajunge (`send()` și `finish()` al draftului în flux), deci modul nu poate livra ca audio ce ruterul n-ar fi livrat ca text; orice eșec costă nota vocală, niciodată textul; un 400 pe `sendVoice` reîncearcă o dată ca `sendAudio`. `/voice` numește motorul care ar vorbi și spune „cloud” când e edge-tts. Reevaluarea inițială a raportat 15/15 mutanți uciși; numărul nu a fost reprodus la recitirea din 2026-09-22.
reviews.remaining: Consumatorul TTS în flux care începe să rostească propozițiile terminate cât timp modelul încă generează (nota vocală se sintetizează după răspunsul complet). Intrarea/ieșirea dintr-un canal de voce pe Discord e sărită deliberat de rândul original (funcție de comunitate, nu de asistent). Doar Telegram: pe Slack/Discord replica trece prin brokerul `channel.reply`, fără audio. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun mesaj vocal Telegram adevărat, niciun model Whisper încărcat, niciun `sendVoice` real — Telegram acceptă `.mp3` ca mesaj vocal după documentație, iar căderea pe `sendAudio` e plasa pentru cazul în care nu.

reviews.summary: Telegram photos are read, not only recognised. `classify` (agents/core/channels/inbound_media.py) recognises the ten attachment kinds in `RECOGNISED_KINDS` and turns a missing file handle, a declared size above the 20 MB bot ceiling or an unreadable kind into a named reason, so the sender gets one plain line from `describe` instead of silence. `InboundImageReader` (agents/core/channels/media_reader.py) describes a photo through a proven-local VLM and hands the description to the turn as data, never as instructions. Locality follows the `screen_locator` rule: `is_local` derives only from `resolve_vlm_config().is_local`, `TelegramChannel._read_image` asks `refusal()` before any download, and `_backend_call` checks again against the `VLMBackend` built for the URL it will actually post to, so a non-loopback VLM receives no bytes. `_download_file` bounds the transfer by the bytes that actually arrive, not by the sender-chosen `file_size`, and `_safe_file_path` rejects any `getFile` path that is not Telegram-shaped before it enters the bot-token URL. The description is folded to one line, capped and wrapped in the Wave 5a `fence_tool_result` fence, deliberately without the `spotlight` datamark, which would replace spaces with '▁' and blind the gateway's `detect_injection`; a photo with '<<END UNTRUSTED>>' written on it cannot close its own fence. The caption never reaches the describer: it travels separately as the sender's question. The turn goes through the normal door, so `Gateway._inbound_meta` marks it `inbound:telegram` and runs the detector over exactly what the model reads. Voice notes are read on the other path: a transcript is the sender's own words and travels unfenced as an ordinary turn (`inbound_voice`, row H071). `ChannelDescriptor` separates `recognises_media` from `reads_media` with the subset invariant checked at construction, and `READABLE_KINDS` is exactly {photo, voice}.
reviews.remaining: Only photos and voice notes, only on Telegram. Not delivered: reading audio files, video, video notes, animations, documents and stickers (recognised, answered with 'reading … is not wired up yet'); a disk cache under a media directory so vision tools can open a local path (bytes stay in memory for one call); location and venue pins (recognised as `location`, deliberately not echoed, not read); caching of media from observed group messages and from replied-to messages; media ingestion on WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Google Chat and email (those adapters pass text only). Documented limitation, not solved: taint cannot be tracked through the model; what travels is the coarse fact that the turn read untrusted material, and the channel's `inbound` origin is what keeps an action derived from a photo in approval. `mark_turn_recall_tainted()` is not called here because it would be a no-op (escalate-only over an already untrusted origin). UNVERIFIED on real services: the suite is hermetic; no real Telegram message received, no local VLM actually called, `getFile` and the download exercised only against a fake client.

ChannelDescriptor (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:28) declares each adapter's dialect, max_message_length and supports_edit (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:35). render_outbound (agents/core/channels/render.py:259) re-renders and chunks the reply per dialect after the model has answered. _begin_channel_draft (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1659) streams edits only when the owner-wide channels.streaming_replies setting is on (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1667) and the adapter declares supports_edit (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1674). reviews.summary: A burst of messages is one turn. agents/core/channels/batching.py holds the rules. Coalescer (agents/core/channels/batching.py:70) holds turn pieces per (conversation, sender) and merges them in arrival order, joined by newlines, into one turn. Each piece extends the batch window of WINDOW_SECONDS 0.35 (Hermes' _busy_text_debounce_seconds), never past HARD_CAP_SECONDS 1.0 from the first piece (Hermes' hard cap; deadline at agents/core/channels/batching.py:97). A batch of MAX_PARTS 32 pieces flushes at once. JARVIS_INBOUND_BATCH_MS and JARVIS_INBOUND_BATCH_MAX_MS set the window and cap for every channel (configured(), agents/core/channels/batching.py:127); a window of 0 turns batching off. Telegram's poll loop (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:530) hands each update to _handle_update (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:577). It queues what the update reads as: a text fragment, or what an attachment was read as (a photo's description, a voice note's transcript, its caption). So a client-split long message, an album (one update per photo) and a photo followed by its question each become one turn (_queue_turn, agents/core/channels/telegram.py:800). While pieces are held, the loop polls getUpdates with timeout 0 instead of the 25 s long poll (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1157), so the batch flushes when its window closes. A button tap or an observed group message first flushes what was said before it, and stop() waits for the cancelled poll task, then hands what is held to the chat lanes, which get LANE_DRAIN_BUDGET (2 s) to finish (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:346); a failed getUpdates also hands over what is held before its 3 s back-off. A slash command is never merged: what the sender said before it goes first, then the command alone, at once (is_command, agents/core/channels/batching.py:52, CommandRegistry.parse; Telegram's _queue_turn and AsyncBatcher.submit), so /stop after a message still engages the e-stop. The voice mark is keyed by (chat, sender), so another group member's older batch cannot take it, and only the running turn takes it: a reply sent in that turn's context while it runs (_RUNNING_TURN, agents/core/channels/telegram.py:91; _after_reply, agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1053). A send from outside that context never takes it (a digest or an outbound notice sent from outside it, another chat's turn, a task an earlier turn left running). One exception is stated at _RUNNING_TURN: once a turn has added an APScheduler job, a job the scheduler fires in that turn's context before the turn ends, and that sends to the turn's chat (the daily digest, in the owner chat), can take the mark. A service line (an unreadable-attachment notice, a transcript echo, a pairing reply, a reason acknowledgement) is sent with voice=False: it is never spoken and never takes the mark. A reply the decision inbox claims as a rejection's reason (H487) is not batched. The poll loop decides with the side-effect-free decision_reason_pending (AutonomyCoordinator.would_consume_reason_reply); a claimed reply, or any fresh text reply in a chat a reason prompt is still being posted to, first hands over what that chat held and is then handled in the chat's lane, where a reply the inbox turns down, or one whose hook fails, is handled as an ordinary message (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:611-639). Its received_at stamp comes from decision_reason_clock, read once per getUpdates page as the page comes back: never later than when that page came back, moved back by Telegram's date for the reply but never before the previous page came back, and after a page cut short by an error the next page keeps the earlier bound (_page_received and _reason_arrival, agents/core/channels/telegram.py:682, :690). The inbox judges the reason window by that stamp, not by when the lane reaches the reply; with no clock, or a failing one, the reply is judged when it runs. Discord and Slack, whose messages arrive as events, use AsyncBatcher (agents/core/channels/batching.py:145). It flushes each batch from its own timer and delivers batches for one key one at a time, under a per-key lock, in order, with at most MAX_PENDING (16) batches on their way and the caller held past that. Slack uses 1, so its one dispatcher waits on a running turn as before batching and its 128-slot ingress queue stays the only buffer. A key's lock is dropped once nothing holds or waits on it. Discord keys by channel and author (agents/core/channels/discord.py:88); Slack keys by channel, member and thread, and with batching off still returns the handler's answer (agents/core/channels/slack.py:365). A stopping Discord or Slack channel discards held pieces and cancels every batch on its way (a timer, a batch waiting behind its key's running turn, and that running turn); a piece or command still waiting for room or for its key is dropped when it wakes, as Slack's shutdown already discards its undelivered event queue. The merged text is what the gateway receives, so its prompt-injection scan runs on the whole message. The gateway scans it with quarantine.detect_injection_normalized (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:176): the raw text plus copies with whitespace collapsed and format characters stripped, hits unioned, so a payload split across pieces, lines or by a zero-width space is caught. Per-chat order is kept: a flush hands the merged turn over before anything later from that chat is processed. tests/test_h117_message_batching.py (60 cases) covers the coalescer (defaults, order, empty pieces, window, cap, wait on the earliest batch, full batch, off) and the Telegram loop: one poll, across polls within the window, after the window, the hard cap, senders and chats kept apart, a photo and its question, an album, a button tap, an observed message, stop, a full batch, batching off, the voice mark, the environment knobs, and the getUpdates timeout. It also covers AsyncBatcher (window, cap, one at a time, off with its answer, full batch with its timer cancelled, an empty batch, drain and discard, a failing delivery logged), Discord and Slack bursts, their stop, and a split injection payload caught in the merged turn. The per-message tests of the Telegram, Discord and Slack channels run with batching off, since they test each message on its own. tests/test_h117_reason_replies.py (79 cases) covers the reason replies with batching on: an ordinary reply still batched, a claimed one behind what its chat said before it and behind a tap read before it, a declined or failing hook handling it as a message, the page stamp and its bounds (Telegram's date, the previous page, a page cut short, a hostile date, a failing or missing clock) and service lines never spoken; tests/test_h487_telegram_reasons.py (34) and tests/test_telegram_voice_reply.py (32) cover the inbox's side and the voice mark left to the running turn. The review round added stop through stop(), a failing poll, command barriers (Telegram and AsyncBatcher), the group voice mark, a zero-width split, lock pruning, the discard of waiting and running batches, a command waiting at discard, the pending bound, and Slack's shutdown and backpressure. There are 61 mutants: 59 killed and 2 equivalent (returning or breaking on a batch that is already gone; a delay of exactly zero); the review round's 18 mutants: 17 killed and 1 equivalent (collapsing whitespace before detect_injection_normalized, which already scans a collapsed copy).

reviews.summary: The hub's own log is readable from the UI. GET /api/admin/logs (agents/core/routers/admin.py:657) is admin-only and read-only; it reads off the event loop and answers a refused filter with 400, its reason and no-store. Behind it, agents/core/log_tail.py reads the file the hub's own setup_logging actually opened, or reports the error it met (FILE_LOG_STATE, agents/core/log.py:19; _writer_state, agents/core/log_tail.py:95), falling back to the configuration for a process that never set logging up ($JARVIS_LOG_FILE, else data_path('logs','jarvis.log') with system.log_to_file: configured_log, agents/core/log_tail.py:86). It lists only that file and its rotations named with ASCII digits, and only regular files by lstat, so a link, a pipe or a directory is never listed (list_files, agents/core/log_tail.py:114; _listed, agents/core/log_tail.py:105); a file is chosen by one of those names, and it is opened without following a link or blocking and checked to be a regular file (_read_window, agents/core/log_tail.py:197). The read is bounded: at most the last 4 MiB, read in one go and closed before parsing, at most 500 records, each at most 8,000 characters (read_path, agents/core/log_tail.py:279). Lines are grouped into records by the log format's header, so a traceback stays with its error: a record over the limit keeps its header and its newest lines behind a "[… N lines not shown]" marker, so the error line is always there; lines above the first header read (a record whose header rotated away, a file not in the log format) are records of their own, beyond the window too. Filters: File, a minimum Level (WARNING shows WARNING, ERROR and CRITICAL; a line with no level is not shown under a floor), a Component (a logger and its children) and Lines (1-500), decided on the record as written, so only returned records are redacted. Redaction runs on every returned field, each line whole before anything is cut, so a secret is never split into a visible half: the H495 secret scanner, an assignment rule for names ending like a credential (`SMTP_PASS=`, `?token=`, `password:`), and the known values of the process's secret-named environment variables and encrypted settings, so it masks at least what /api/admin/env masks (_Redactor, agents/core/log_tail.py:159; _known_secret_values, agents/core/log_tail.py:137); when the scanner cannot be loaded nothing is shown, with a note (_redactor, agents/core/log_tail.py:181; _record, agents/core/log_tail.py:251). Terminal escape sequences, C0 and C1 controls and bidirectional overrides are removed (_clean, agents/core/log_tail.py:190). The answer carries the components seen (redacted), the bytes scanned and whether only part of the file was read, and an honest note: file logging off and how to turn it on, a file the hub could not open at start, no file yet, or a file that may no longer be written (read_log, agents/core/log_tail.py:327). The HUD's Logs panel (frontend/src/panels/logs.tsx:54, registered in the Console's Observe group) has the File / Level / Component / Lines filters, colours records by level (ERROR/CRITICAL red, WARNING amber, DEBUG dim), shows them newest first as text, never markup, auto-refreshes every 5 s while switched on and the page is visible, skipping a tick while a read is in flight and stopping on a refused credential, shows LIVE only while the hub writes its file, shows no old records after a refused filter (and goes back to the current log when a rotation is gone), and names the admin token on a 401 or 403. `nerva logs -n N` (cmd_logs, agents/cli/nerva.py:1333) reads the same bounded, redacted tail (N counts records), says when only part was read, and refuses cleanly on an unreadable file or a missing redactor. tests/test_log_tail.py (33 cases) covers the resolution and the off state, rotations and refused names, records and tracebacks, the caps, the level floor and component children, the byte budget, a partial last line, bytes that are not UTF-8, control characters, redaction (current file, rotation, traceback line, filtered fields), the route and the CLI; tests/test_h145b_log_review.py (32) covers the first review: a secret across the cut (four offsets, and in a continuation line), a long traceback keeping its error line, links and a link swapped in after listing, a pipe, secret-named environment values and credential assignments (and ordinary numbers left alone), a redactor that cannot load (route and CLI), C1 and bidi controls, filtering before redaction, the writer's error and its path, setup_logging's record, no file yet, plain lines beyond the window, the 4 MiB budget, level-less lines under a floor, component redaction, the CLI's records, window note and -n 0, rotation names, a directory and the 400's no-store; frontend/src/test/logs-panel.test.tsx (14) covers the registration, the query, the admin read, order and colours, each filter, the 5 s auto-refresh, a tick skipped in flight, a hidden page, stale records after a refusal, LIVE only while writing, the off note, no match and a partial read, 401 and 403, a kept component and text-only rendering. The first review (two majors: a secret split by the cut came back in part, and a long traceback lost its error line; ten minors; nine nits) is answered; the feature's 29 mutants were caught but one equivalent, and this round's 26, all but one equivalent (the regular-file check after open, which lseek or read also enforces), two after their cases were added (a pipe, the partial first line). Test manual: PNB-169, PNB-170; the API sweep lists the route. Adapted from Hermes: one log file and its rotations instead of six named files, since the hub writes one log; the level is a floor rather than an exact match. Known limits: a record forged by a multi-line message that contains a header-shaped line is shown as its own record (a property of the log format). Complete base evidence pins and unchanged text anchors verified; existing capability/status preserved. Claim-specific source inspection is recorded in the bounded image source review. Other CLI command handlers, settings/job flag semantics, session/approval dispatch and command-tree structure are unchanged. reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 in five rounds. The first round shipped with H200 (critic note 7). After an adversarial review reopened it, the second round added the receiver switch, an event list and a prompt template. After a second review, the third added where a delivery goes (Hermes' Deliver to and deliver only), a description and a receiver switch that fails closed. A third review (review-H153c) found that as shipped, Deliver to reached none of the owner's channels, and the fourth round made a real send reach each offered channel, tested through the real path down to the channel adapter. A fourth review (review-H153d) found that the fourth round's plain-text rendering let one delivery freeze the hub, and rewrote the sender's file names and addresses; the fifth round sends the text as written, bounds every renderer, and fixes the review's minors. A fifth review (review-H153e) found no major; its three minors (inline code spans still quadratic in two renderers, first-read waiters holding worker threads, eight unpinned behaviours) and six nits are fixed.

Backend CRUD is admin-guarded, and the store serves every change without a restart:
- GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE /api/webhooks (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:175, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:181, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:194, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:221) list, create, update and delete hooks.
- A create that carries a field it does not know (Hermes' skills, deliver_chat_id) is refused with 422, never silently dropped (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:87).
- WebhookStore.create (agents/core/webhooks.py:486) mints a token and, when signed, an HMAC signing secret. Both are returned once, and every list masks them (agents/core/webhooks.py:635). A save that fails undoes the change in memory.

(1) The receiver card (Hermes' platform-level toggle). The setting webhooks.receiver_enabled is a declared toggle, on by default. It is written through the audited PUT /api/admin/settings/webhooks, and the audit row ends with the value (receiver_enabled=false). A reseed is audited too (agents/core/routers/admin.py:455). When the switch is off, the trigger refuses every delivery with 503. It checks before the body is read and again after authentication, so a switch that lands while a sender streams its body stops that delivery (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:239).
- It fails closed (agents/core/webhooks.py:251):
  - only a literal true is on, and a missing row is the declared default;
  - when the settings store cannot be read, settings_db.read_setting raises instead of answering the default (agents/core/settings_db.py:676), so the last state read or written stays in force;
  - a receiver never read is refused with "the webhook receiver's state cannot be read".
- It is read off the event loop, and by one caller at a time: while a read runs, every other caller gets the last state at once. A caller with no state known yet (the first read after a start) waits for that read, at most two seconds, so a burst that arrives while it runs is answered, and a read slower than that is still refused, closed. The router waits on the event loop (agents/core/webhooks.py:377): who reads is decided on the loop, only the read runs on a worker thread, and a waiter holds none, so a burst on a slow fresh receiver leaves the default executor free (review-H153e MINOR-2). A caller from a thread waits in it, at most four at once (RECEIVER_FIRST_READ_WAITERS, agents/core/webhooks.py:247); any other is refused, closed. A write, a reset or another store wakes the waiters. A state is used for a second before the store is read again. A read that a write, a reset, a reseed or another store overtook while it ran is dropped, a failed one included. A write in this process is seen at once; one from another process (nerva config set) within the second.
- The admin routes keep working, and hooks keep their credentials.
- The panel's receiver row shows on, off, or "not read" with the reason:
  - a failed re-read drops the last state instead of showing it;
  - an answer is shown unless a newer one already is, so an earlier read never overwrites a newer one and a poller slower than its interval still sees each answer (frontend/src/panel-kit.tsx:20);
  - ↻ re-reads it;
  - a stored value that is not true or false is shown as off;
  - a store with no row yet, which the hub answers with its own 404 naming the category, shows the hub's default, "on · not stored", and can be switched off, because the write creates the row (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:197); any other 404 (a proxy's) is a failed read.
- Interop and the /v1 panel show every hook as refused while the switch is off.

(2) The New-subscription modal: name, description, agent or workflow target, target id, HMAC signing (the secret, shown once), an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only. Create is last in the tab order (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:389).
- Events: up to 32 printable names of 1 to 64 characters, no comma, stored stripped and kept once each, ignoring ASCII case (agents/core/webhooks.py:137).
  - The delivery's event comes from the sender's header (X-GitHub-Event, X-Gitlab-Event, X-Event-Key, X-Event-Type, X-Webhook-Event), else from the payload's event or type (agents/core/webhooks.py:121). It is bounded when read but never cut to the 64-character limit, so a longer name matches no subscription.
  - A hook with a list runs only the deliveries whose event is on it. Every other delivery is answered 202 with the reason, never run, and counted as skipped (agents/core/webhooks.py:605). That includes a delivery that names no event, and a list a hand edit broke (null, not a list, an item that is not a name).
- Template: {a.b.0} reads the JSON payload by key and list index, {event} is the event, {payload} the whole body, and {payload.x} a payload key the template reserves (agents/core/webhooks.py:173).
  - Nothing else is read. A missing value is empty, a string is used as is and anything else as JSON.
  - The work is bounded by the caps (agents/core/webhooks.py:157): each path is read once per render, a value is encoded only up to 4,000 characters, and substitution stops at 16,000.
  - A template that renders nothing is skipped, not run. So is an untemplated delivery with no text, which gets its own reason.
- A body over 5 MiB is refused with 413 before it is read whole (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:236).

(3) Deliver to and deliver only (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:355, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:367).
- deliver is log (the default: the reply stays in the sender's response and the session) or one of the owner's own channels that something receives: telegram, voice or ntfy (agents/core/webhooks.py:70). Names are matched exactly.
- web is refused by name: nothing in the hub connects a client to the web channel, so a push there would never arrive. /api/channels/targets and nerva send --list say the same: web is not ready while no client is connected (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:88).
- The reply, or a workflow's last step, goes through send_to_target and ChannelManager.send to the owner's own destination (Telegram's owner chat). send_to_target writes an IntentLog row per send. The text is labelled "Webhook <name> - <event>", and each channel carries the label its own way:
  - ntfy gets it as its title, folded to printable ASCII and cut to 120 characters;
  - telegram and voice get it on the first line.
- The text goes as written: nothing is rendered and nothing is rewritten, so a file name, an address and a Markdown link arrive as the sender wrote them, and a link shows its address. What hides or reorders text is dropped: every format and control character but a newline, a tab, a zero-width joiner and non-joiner (the bidi controls and marks, zero-width spaces, word joiners, invisible operators, the soft hyphen, the BOM, the TAG plane), and the characters that render blank (the Hangul fillers, the grapheme joiner, the Mongolian selectors, the blank braille pattern); a subdivision flag emoji stays (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:313; review-H153e NIT-1). A lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:339). Telegram sends it with no parse mode, no link preview and no voice note, and ntfy unrendered (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:208, agents/core/channels/telegram.py:432, agents/core/channels/ntfy.py:137). Voice speaks it without the markup. A longer text is cut at 4,000 characters with a note that says where the rest is (the session for a reply, nowhere for deliver-only text).
- Nothing on the push path renders, so a delivery costs linear time in its text: one long line cannot hold the event loop. The renderers the rest of the hub uses bound every marker span (a link, bold, italic, a heading line), and put inline code spans back in one pass (agents/core/channels/render.py:52; review-H153e MINOR-1), so one long line costs linear time there too, and a span past the bound is left as written (agents/core/channels/render.py:40).
- The hook is read again after the turn. If it was deleted or switched off, or the receiver was switched off or cannot be read, nothing is pushed and the hook says why; a hook moved to another destination is pushed there, labelled with its name as it is then.
- Quiet hours (ambient.quiet_hours_start/end, 22 to 7 by default, hours taken modulo 24, the jobs' own reading, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:276) keep every push off the phone and the speaker. An hour setting that is not a number (an infinity, NaN, text) keeps its default, for the jobs too (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:82). The push is noted on the hook, not held for the morning as a job's message is.
- A hook makes at most 30 push attempts an hour (agents/core/webhooks.py:422, per process). An attempt the channel refused counts, and the panel says so; a push held by quiet hours spends none. A push over it is noted, not sent.
- deliver_only skips the agent: the rendered text goes straight to the destination, and no turn runs. It needs a channel: deliver-only with the log is refused on create and on PATCH, with the reason (agents/core/webhooks.py:101). A record from before that rule can still be switched off, and its delivery says the text was dropped.
- A workflow delivers its last step's output, or nothing when the run failed or its last step returned an error, never an earlier step's output (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:440). The last step is the last to run, in the pipeline's batch order, not the last listed, and a run that stopped early delivers the last step that ran (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:416). An output the router cannot read is recorded, and nothing is pushed.
- Each delivery's outcome (channel, ok, reason, time) is kept on the hook and shown in its detail pane, and the response carries it too. Every exit after a call is counted is recorded, a missing or invalid workflow and a failed turn included (agents/core/webhooks.py:695).
- A delivery that fails is recorded and answered 200. Every answer is encodable whatever the sender or a step put in it: a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD, a NaN or an infinity null, and anything else JSON cannot carry (a date, bytes, a set, an object) its text (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:465), so a delivery is never a 500 after its push. A workflow hook answers with ok, the steps that ran and the delivery, never the run's context, which holds the sender's text and every step's output. A failed turn itself still answers 500, so the sender's retry runs it again.

(4) The subscriptions list with per-route enable/disable and delete. PATCH /api/webhooks/{hook_id} (agents/core/webhooks.py:553) takes any of enabled (a strict boolean), events, prompt, deliver, deliver_only and description, and changes them in place. It refuses:
- null (and its schema advertises none);
- an empty body;
- an unknown field;
- a destination the create would refuse.

The schema names the four destinations as an enum. A hook switched off keeps its token and secret. The trigger refuses it with 403 after authentication, from the live record, before the event filter.

Each row has an on/off switch, an HMAC or token badge, an event-count badge, the destination (none for the log) and delete with an inline confirmation. The detail pane shows the description, the calls, the skipped deliveries, where the result goes, how a push goes (on a hook that pushes) and how the last delivery went. It edits all of them and opens at the hook's own destination. After a save focus returns to the hook's row, or to the create form when the hook is gone. The legacy /v1 panel lists, creates and deletes through adminFetch, and shows the receiver as the hub reads it and each destination (agents/web/static/tools.js:441).

(5) The restart banners. Nerva needs no restart for either kind of change: the receiver switch is a setting read at most a second old, and hook CRUD is served live.

Audit: create, switch, update and delete each write a SecurityEvent (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:143). It names:
- the hook id;
- the target as a JSON string;
- the event list;
- the template's length (never its text);
- the destination and deliver only;
- the signed and enabled flags.

It never records the token or secret. A switch alone is recorded as enable or disable; any other change is an update. The receiver switch is audited by the settings route, with its value, and a choice setting's value is in its row (a toggle, a select, a number, a slider). A nerva config set from the shell writes no audit row (H378).

Deliveries: an agent-target delivery goes through handle_input(channel="webhook"). origin_for_channel (agents/core/action_origin.py:36) classifies that channel as inbound, so the payload is tainted and the kernel's GRANT->QUEUE escalation applies. A workflow target runs its pipeline (agents/core/routers/workflows.py:37) under the inbound action origin. The sender waits for the push as well as the turn. A retried delivery that carries an Idempotency-Key is not run again; it gets the first outcome back (H659, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:552). One without a key runs again.

Until now the history was a side record: a commit or rollback in the Prompts panel changed a JSON file while the agent kept its old persona. agents/core/soul_edit.py holds the one path an edit takes, apply_soul (:152). (1) Refusals. An agent the hub has not loaded is refused (404; agent_folder, :100, returns an enumerated folder name in the id alphabet, so no request value reaches a path). So is text over MAX_SOUL_BYTES (256 KiB of UTF-8, :40; 413), safe mode (:171; 409, because overlays are not read there, H275) and a persona the H387 guard would drop (:174; 422 with the verdict). guard_verdict (:60) runs the same scan and cap as Agent._load_soul, and GET /api/agents/{id}/soul now reports it through the same function. A line the guard only quarantines is applied, and the verdict names it. (2) Nothing live is lost. The first edit keeps the file on disk as v1 ("on disk before the first edit"). A file changed on disk since the last version, such as a hand edit, is kept as its own version ("on disk, changed outside the editor") before it is replaced (:185). The text is committed (:195; the same text twice is one version). The agent re-reads its persona (_load_soul, :197), and the result says whether the running agent now reads the written file. (5) Audited without the text. A SETTINGS_CHANGE row names the agent, the version and its hash. A plain commit and a history-only rollback are audited the same way (record_version, :224; agents/core/routers/admin.py:817, :872). Surfaces. The memory/disk warning Hermes shows is here: ranked conditions, only the worst undismissed one on screen, a suspected OOM restart, dismissal per boot, clearing on confirmed recovery, and a watch that does not depend on autonomy. agents/core/resource_pressure.py holds it apart from the autonomy observer, whose thresholds it reuses (85 % elevated and 95 % critical for memory and disk: DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS, :39, pinned to observer.DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS). (1) Ranking. CONDITIONS (:38) orders disk_critical > memory_critical > oom_restart_suspected > disk_elevated > memory_elevated. PressureMonitor.snapshot (:259) answers every raised condition in that order, with its level, percent, since and whether it is dismissed, plus the worst one not dismissed. Disk covers every watched volume, and the entry names the paths near or over the line. (2) Volumes. take_sample (:81) reads psutil memory and each distinct watched path once (watched_paths, :283: the filesystem root and the data home). A reading that fails is None, never a healthy 0 %, and changes nothing. (3) Hysteresis. Each resource's _Held.update (:109) raises at once. It clears, or steps critical down to elevated, only after RECOVERY_SAMPLES (3, :40) samples in a row under the line by RECOVERY_MARGIN (5 points, :41). A reading just under the line is not counted and restarts the count, so a flapping reading neither clears nor re-raises. (4) Suspected OOM restart. A small state file in the data home (_write_state, :159, atomic through a temporary file, left behind on no failure) holds the boot id (current_boot_id, :69: the kernel's /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, else one from psutil's boot time), the memory level, the dismissals and a clean-shutdown mark. start (:172) finds a run on the same boot that ended without the mark while memory was elevated or critical, and raises oom_restart_suspected naming that level. It logs a warning, and says "suspected" because the kernel's log is not read. stop (:191) writes the mark. The web lifespan calls start before the hub serves and stop as the very first teardown step, so a later step that hangs cannot make a clean stop look like a kill (agents/web.py:644, :650). (5) Dismissal. dismiss (:269) takes a condition and this boot's id. It refuses another boot's id, an unknown condition or one not raised. The dismissal persists across a restart on the same boot; a new boot re-arms it, and so does the condition's recovery, because a new episode is a new warning. Unknown names in the file are dropped. (6) Sampling apart from autonomy. SchedulerService.schedule_pressure_monitor (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:419) samples every 60 s on the hub's scheduler, so autonomy off or ESTOP engaged does not stop it. The route samples on demand when the last sample is over a minute old (fresh, :226). Samples from the route's worker thread and the scheduler are folded in one at a time under a lock. (7) Surfaces. GET /api/system/pressure and POST /api/system/pressure/dismiss {condition, boot_id} are both user-guarded (agents/core/routers/pressure.py:30, :36; 409 on a refused dismissal). The HUD's frontend/src/pressure-banner.tsx is mounted under the power chip (frontend/src/app.tsx:527). It polls the route, shows only the worst undismissed condition in one sentence (an alert for critical and a suspected OOM restart, a status for elevated), and dismisses it for this boot. reviews.summary: Execuția guvernată pe altă mașină există. Ținta declarată de owner intră în registrul de politici din aceeași sursă ca detaliile de conexiune, iar o comandă trece hardline → politica țintei → aprobare durabilă → contractul terminal.exec pe rădăcinile remote declarate → Action Kernel înainte să atingă firul. Firul rulează un argv reconstruit cu shlex pe shell-ul remote (niciun string de shell nu pleacă de aici), cu cheia de gazdă pinuită, doar pe cheie, fără ~/.ssh/config, fără agent și fără forwarding. Default-off în spatele JARVIS_TERMINAL_SSH_HOST; cu flagul nesetat inventarul rămâne identic.
reviews.remaining: Rândul cere mult peste execuție și restul nu e livrat: manager de conexiuni ControlMaster, erori clasificate, sugestii de gazde din ~/.ssh/config, bootstrap care refolosește-sau-pornește un serviciu remote, revalidare de liveness, tranzacție de update cu jurnal de recuperare și linii de restore per profil, fan-out "update all instances". ControlMaster e o divergență deliberată, nu o scăpare: un socket de control partajat e un canal autentificat reutilizabil lăsat pe disc, iar transportul îl dezactivează explicit. NEVERIFICAT pe hardware: nicio sesiune SSH reală nu a fost deschisă din această livrare — suita e ermetică, fără socket și fără binar ssh, deci interoperabilitatea cu un sshd real rămâne nedovedită.

reviews.summary: Nerva keeps the machine awake while a turn runs, reads and streams its power state, and eases off on battery, as Hermes does. agents/core/power.py holds one shared power assertion while at least one turn runs (KeepAwake, refcounted). It is off by default and turned on with JARVIS_KEEP_AWAKE=1 (keep_awake_enabled). The mechanism is the platform's own (backend_name, backend_argv): caffeinate -i -w <hub pid> on macOS, systemd-inhibit --what=idle:sleep --mode=block around tail --pid=<hub pid> on Linux, so both helpers end with the hub even when it is killed, and SetThreadExecutionState on Windows. The helper is started in its own process group (start_new_session) and released by signalling that group while its leader is still unreaped, so the child systemd-inhibit starts ends too; a helper that already exited is reaped by its handle, and one that ignores SIGTERM is killed after one second. A missing binary or mechanism never fails a turn and is reported (status error), as is a helper that exits on its own. Every turn entry holds it: Orchestrator.handle_input, handle_input_stream and the one-shot process take it at the start (hold_for_turn) and drop it in their finally (release_for_turn), so a reply, an error and a cancel all release it; the lifespan releases every hold at shutdown (agents/web.py) and atexit does at exit. It is gated as host.control (authorize_keep_awake), in the llm_control order: the owner's system-control permission, the host-control contract, whose action list now names power.keep_awake (agents/core/autonomy/remediation.py), an Action Kernel GRANT (the kernel must be on; QUEUE, DENY and anything that is not a GRANT refuse), then a durable audit row (no audit log, or a refused row, refuses too). The action carries the fixed trusted origin, since keep-awake is the owner's switch and not the content of the turn that asks first. It is asked once per process; a refusal keeps it off until the next start and is named in the status. The power state comes from psutil.sensors_battery (read_battery: on battery, percent, plugged). A resume from sleep is seen as the wall clock running more than 60 s ahead of the monotonic clock between two reads (PowerMonitor.tick), which stops while Linux and macOS sleep, and is shown for ten minutes. The scheduler reads it every minute (SchedulerService.schedule_power_monitor, skipped under JARVIS_TESTING), so a resume is noticed without anyone asking. GET /api/power answers the power state, the deferral threshold, whether background work is being deferred and the keep-awake status (enabled, active, holders, backend, refused, error); GET /api/power/stream pushes the same payload to a connected client on every change, with a keepalive while it does not change (agents/core/routers/power.py). Both are user-guarded. Battery-aware throttling: below system.battery_defer_percent (a settings row, 50 by default; 0 never, 100 always on battery) on battery, or on battery with an unknown charge, the heavy background jobs skip their run and return deferred_on_battery, which scheduler health records as skipped: memory maintenance, the tech scout, the learning-loop promotions, prompt evolution and the WorldView KG sync (the last three through SchedulerService wrappers the scheduler now registers). An unreadable power state lets the job run. Nothing the owner asks for directly is deferred. The HUD shell shows a PowerChip (frontend/src/power-chip.tsx): on battery with the charge and whether background jobs wait, a wake from sleep, and keep-awake holding, ready or refused with its reason; a plugged-in machine with keep-awake off shows nothing. It polls GET /api/power every minute and follows the stream where the browser can attach to it. The desktop shell turns webview background throttling off for both windows (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs, background_throttling), so a HUD in the background keeps reading a streaming reply instead of being suspended and having its turn cancelled; NERVA_DESKTOP_BACKGROUND_THROTTLING=throttle or suspend asks for it back and an unknown value is named and ignored (desktop/src-tauri/src/throttling.rs). macOS 14+ honours the policy; Linux and Windows webviews ignore it. The binding-writer inventory's pinned lines in scheduler_service.py move with the file. Tests: tests/test_h182_power.py (76), including a real helper process whose own child is ended by the release, and rustc unit tests of throttling.rs; src/test/power-chip.test.tsx (6). 100 mutants: 98 killed after five cases were added; the other two were redundant checks, removed. reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 together with H153 (critic note 7: one spec, one panel), then fixed after an adversarial review. The v2 console has a Webhooks panel, WebhooksPanel (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:187), registered in the Interop group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:50; frontend/src/gap.tsx:5069). Interop mode's WEBHOOKS list links to it by an accessible name (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:341). Every panel call sends the admin credential. The backend stays admin-only CRUD: list, create, switch and delete all carry Depends(admin_guard) (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:175, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:181, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:194, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:221).

Interop mode is built from its four sources alone (hydrateInterop, frontend/src/api/live.ts:126). All four (A2A peers, MCP servers, widgets, webhooks) are admin-only routes and are fetched with the admin credential, and so is the webhooks settings category: while the receiver switch is off every webhook row reads "receiver off", and a switch it could not read is said under WEBHOOKS (frontend/src/api/live.ts:119, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:342). A section whose source failed is empty and says "not connected", and an empty real list says "none" (Section, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:302); the demo seed's rows are never shown under the LIVE chip. When no source answers nothing is overwritten, so the mode stays "Not connected" and DEMO keeps its seed. The review found that fetching only the webhooks list with the credential had marked the whole mode LIVE over seeded peers, MCP servers and widgets.

The five accepted parts:
(1) Create dialog: name, agent or workflow target, target id and an HMAC-signed toggle, and, since H153, a description, an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only, posted to POST /api/webhooks. A refusal shows the hub's own reason, and an empty target is refused before any request. The create button is held while the call is pending and while a new hook's credentials are on screen, so a second hook cannot replace a secret before it was saved.
(2) Created result, shown once (Reveal, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:145): the absolute trigger URL (triggerUrl, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:52: the page origin, the base path and the encoded id), and the token, or the signing secret for a signed hook, each with a copy button that says "copied" in a polite live region, plus the header the sender must send. Only the warning sentence is an alert, so a screen reader does not read the secret aloud. On a loopback origin it says a sender elsewhere needs an address it can reach. The secret lives only in the panel's state and is dropped on "I have saved it" (focus returns to the create form) or unmount. The list never carries it: WebhookStore masks the token to a 4-character hint (agents/core/webhooks.py:635).
(3) Detail pane: clicking a hook expands its trigger URL, auth header (with the token hint), calls, last call and creation time, the deliveries its event list skipped and the last event skipped, and an editor for its event list and prompt template (H153). The row shows target_type:target, an HMAC or token badge, an on/off badge and an event-count badge.
(4) Delete with confirmation: "delete…" arms an inline confirmation that explains the sender's credential dies with the hook and moves focus to "delete for good", which sends DELETE; "keep it" returns focus to "delete…". Each row button's accessible name includes the hook's name. A row's buttons are held while its call is pending, and every switch or delete reloads the list whatever the hub answered: a hook already deleted elsewhere is reported as gone ("ci was already deleted", "ci no longer exists") and its row disappears, with focus moved to the create form; a refused delete keeps the confirmation and says why. A per-hook on/off switch (PATCH, H153) is offered as the reversible alternative.
(5) Governance: creating, switching and deleting a hook each write a SecurityEvent (_audit_webhook, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:143, called at agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:190, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:215 and agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:227). It names the hook id, the target as a JSON string (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:137), so a target cannot pass its own text off as the row's id or flags, and the signed and enabled flags as the store reads them, never the token or signing secret. A delete of an unknown id writes nothing and answers 404 "webhook not found".

The receiver-disabled banner: when the receiver switch (H153, the setting webhooks.receiver_enabled) is off, the panel's receiver row says every delivery is refused until it is switched back on (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:352). The restart-gateway banner is not needed: a delivery sees the switch at most a second old (at once after a write in this process), and hook CRUD is served live; the receiver row says so. Not built, and not part of this row: a `nerva webhooks` CLI verb (critic note 7 places it with H409, as `nerva webhooks inbound|outbound`) and a mobile screen.

Tests: frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx has 56 cases. reviews.summary: The HUD's keyboard shortcuts live in one registry, as in Hermes. frontend/src/shortcuts.ts defines every action once (ACTIONS: id, category, label, default chord, scope): the ten mode keys, World (w), the Console (`), Ambient (a), Cinema (m) and its three stages (o, n, b, scope cinema), focus the message box (/), the command palette (mod+k) and the Keyboard Shortcuts panel (mod+/). app.tsx (World's key included: WorldAwareApp passes onWorld and shares the live overrides through useShortcutOverrides) and the cinema overlay in shell.tsx dispatch through matchAction over bindings(overrides) instead of literal key maps, and every key hint (palette, top bar, World, Console, cinema stages) is read from the registry (chordOf, displayChord). A matched action takes the key from the browser (preventDefault); Shift+letter falls back to the bare letter unless it is bound itself. frontend/src/shortcuts-panel.tsx is the panel mod+/ opens: categories Navigation, View, Composer and Session with search (searchBindings); click a chord to record a new one ("Press a key…", Esc cancels, a lone modifier keeps listening; chordFromEvent, rebind); the palette and the panel take only a chord held with Ctrl/⌘ or Alt (acceptsChord), fire in an input only then (firesInInputs), and the palette always has a Keyboard shortcuts entry, so no rebinding can lock the panel out; Space is spelled "space", and a chord with no key is refused on record and on read; Esc closes the panel without closing what lies beneath; per-binding reset and Reset all (resetBinding); an "Also bound to X" note when two actions share a chord (conflictsFor). Overrides persist per viewer in localStorage under hud.shortcuts, validated on read (readOverrides, loadOverrides, saveOverrides), and survive storage that is off. Governance: defineActions refuses any action whose id, category or label names an approval, a decision, an accept, reject, deny or consent (FORBIDDEN_TARGET), so no chord can reach a Decision Inbox action. Tests: frontend/src/test/shortcuts.test.tsx (25), app-routing.test.tsx (+14: panel, rebinding, persistence, World, composer focus, the Space and Ctrl+Space lockout, the palette entry, the typing guard, preventDefault, World behind the panel, storage off, live hints, Esc beneath, Cinema), cinema.test.tsx (+1: rebound stage keys); voice-orb and briefing-wall expect the registry's stage titles; 38 mutants, 36 killed, 2 equivalent; the review round's 19 mutants, all killed (4 by tests added after a first pass).
