Archived chats exist, as in Hermes. CheckpointManager.set_archived stamps or clears archived_at in a session's metadata without creating a session. get_sessions(archived=...) filters on it in SQL, read only from valid JSON, so the limit counts only the view asked for. agents/core/routers/sessions.py serves several routes. GET /sessions leaves archived chats out; ?archived=true lists only them, each row with archived_at. POST /sessions/{id}/archive and /unarchive (user_guard) are 404 for an unknown session and 400 for an invalid id. Resuming a chat through POST /sessions/resume unarchives it. agents/core/session_archive.py holds the rest. run_auto_archive archives sessions whose ended_at, else started_at, is older than memory.auto_archive_days (0 = off, at most 3650) and never touches the active one; SchedulerService.schedule_auto_archive runs it daily at 03:40. DELETE /sessions/{id}?confirm=DELETE (admin_guard) holds the session's turn lease (409 session_busy) and the memory locks. It refuses the chat in use (409), a chat another chat continues (409 has_continuations), and an id that is not a session or whose snapshot is not this session's (404). delete_session first writes an encrypted, fsynced, read-back backup (the backup cipher, key under JARVIS_KEY_DIR) of the session's rows (session, checkpoints, clock, continuation seed, history binding), transcript snapshot and log (unreadable ones byte for byte), compaction archive, checklist and note. The backup goes to <data root>-forget-archives/sessions/<id>-<stamp>.json.enc, outside the data root, keeping the newest JARVIS_SESSION_BACKUP_KEEP=10. Only then does it delete them and clear the live conversation, with the chat's turn embeddings (VectorStore.remove_where; 503 recall_unavailable if the store cannot) and with secure_delete plus a WAL truncate. Facts already extracted into the knowledge graph, and the audit log, are not touched. A backup that does not land raises backup_failed and deletes nothing. The file work runs off the event loop. The HUD SessionsPanel (frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx) has chats and archived tabs, archive, unarchive and a two-step "delete permanently" that names the backup. llm.project_dir only sets the folder whose convention files H594 reads (project_context.start_dir); file tools (FileScope.resolve, list_dir, search_files) and the terminal cwd still resolve relative paths from the first file root, and the setting's label says so. Tests: tests/test_h218_archived_chats.py (73), frontend/src/test/sessions-archive.test.tsx (7). At the original build a todo_none mutant (the backup's checklist dropped) survived all 39 tests; the review round pins it, with 16 targeted mutants of its fixes all killed. reviews.summary: Nerva shows whether it is listening outside its main window, as Hermes does. agents/core/voice/listening.py keeps one process-wide, thread-safe listening state per source (ListeningState, STATE). The host's own voice path publishes it: the wake-word detector marks hub armed once it holds the mic open and off when it stops (WakeWordDetector.start, stop; agents/core/voice/wake_word.py), and a capture marks hub listening while it records, thinking while it transcribes and answers, speaking while it plays the reply, and falls back to armed (or off when the detector is not running) in a finally, so an early end or a failure never leaves it lit (VoicePipeline._capture_and_process; stop marks it off; agents/core/voice/pipeline.py). Wyoming satellites publish it too: an authenticated satellite's detection or voice-started marks satellite:<id> listening and voice-stopped marks it thinking; a transcript marks it thinking while it is answered and clears it after; a closed connection clears whatever it lit; with authentication required an unauthenticated peer can set nothing, and with authentication off the one anonymous satellite is named satellite (LISTEN_EVENTS, WyomingServer._listening_source, handle_connection; agents/core/voice/wyoming.py). The API is get / set / on-change in process: set_state (a bounded, printable source name and one of off, armed, listening, thinking, speaking; off forgets the source; at most 32 sources), snapshot (each source's state, the loudest by ORDER — listening, then armed, both an open mic, then thinking, speaking, off — mic_open, and a seq that moves on every change), subscribe and unsubscribe (callbacks run outside the lock and a failing one is ignored). A transient state not re-said for 120 s expires, and the expiry moves seq, so a crashed capture never leaves the indicator on; an armed mic stays. GET /api/voice/listening answers the snapshot and GET /api/voice/listening/stream pushes it on every change with keepalives (agents/core/routers/voice.py); both are user-guarded and GET-only, so nothing can set the state over HTTP. Every writer and reader loads the one agents.core.voice.listening module (a test pins it, since core.X and agents.core.X load as different modules here). The push to the desktop shell: frontend/src/listening.ts follows the stream with the HUD's own token (EventSource cannot send one) and falls back to polling every 5 s; it combines the hub's state with the window's own mic (useVoice active counts as listening), and only inside the desktop app forwards the loudest to the shell (setDesktopListening in frontend/src/desktop.tsx sends only changes and re-sends after a refused call; a closing window sends off). The indicator surface is the tray icon (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs): a desktop_listening command, allowed only to the local HUD windows (verify, capability allow-desktop-listening, build.rs manifest), records each window's state on a board and shows the loudest (desktop/src-tauri/src/indicator.rs): a menu-bar title while a mic is open (● listening, ○ wake word) — shown on macOS and next to the icon on Linux, not on Windows — and a tooltip naming the state on macOS and Windows. It is read-only: nothing on the tray or in the command can open or close a mic. Tests: tests/test_h222_listening.py (44), including the capture's state trail, every early end, a failing transcription, authenticated, unauthenticated and anonymous satellites and a satellite dropping mid-capture, the stream framing, the routes and guard, the shell's command, permission and capability, and the rustc unit tests of indicator.rs; src/test/listening.test.tsx (8) and src/test/desktop-listening.test.ts (3). 65 mutants: 64 killed after five cases were added; the other was a redundant check, removed. The desktop crate was not compiled here: its tray calls were checked against the Tauri 2.11.5 source. Named speech compatibility review: listening state, GET-only snapshot/stream and mic authority are unchanged; listening regressions pass.

Hermes' "what can it do right now" view is here: one read-only answer, for one agent as seen by one principal, built from the code a turn runs and served on three surfaces. agents/core/inspector.py holds it; build_inspector (:108) returns up to five sections (SECTIONS, :63). (1) Views. VIEWS (:56) names the five tool-profile postures: the owner and a guest on the HUD (owner, guest), the owner and a stranger on an external channel (inbound-owner, inbound; Telegram stands for every channel, under the inbound action origin a real channel turn has) and no human (internal). The look binds that principal and origin in a task of its own (:125), so nothing it binds, and nothing the runtime notes while resolving the offer, outlives it. (2) status (_status, :155): version, the backend and model the router serves, the local model's state through project_llm_status, the transcript budget llm.tool_loop_context_tokens (0 reads as 75 % of the model window), the tool loop and safe mode. (3) tools (_tools, :194): the tool runtime's own resolved offer for the agent under that principal (_resolve_offer: registry or the capability registry's view, job toolset, posture, the agent's tools: list, the shared-session rule), not the raw registry. Each row says whether the tool is gated and whether its output is fenced as untrusted, with the description cut to DESCRIPTION_CHARS (160, :65). The withheld names are listed, a resolver failure offers nothing, and loop_enabled says whether the model sees any of them (with the loop off they are what the posture would offer). (4) skills (_skills, :215): the rows prompt_catalog gives the prompt under that principal and that offer, or none when llm.skills_in_prompt is off. (5) mcp (_mcp, :225): each server's transport, trust tier, transport-aware liveness (is_connected, so an HTTP server reads connected; a probe that raises is down) and visible tools, with no URL or command line. (6) system_prompt (_prompt, :253): the agent's system prompt and the user part Agent.build_prompt sends for an empty user message: persona, agent context, the core-memory block, the runtime, language and grounding rails and the skills block. tokens (:266) estimates what that fixed part costs every turn before history. The texts are masked by the log redactor (SecretRedactionFilter; nothing is shown when it cannot load, _redactor :73) and capped together at PROMPT_CAP_BYTES (64 KiB, :64) on a character boundary. The core block is read with freeze=False (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3198, :3258, :3338): the frozen block when a turn froze one, else a fresh render that is not kept, so a look never fixes the day's snapshot. (7) Surfaces. GET /api/admin/inspector?agent=&view=&section= (agents/core/routers/status.py:123, admin-guarded; 404 for an unknown agent, 400 naming the views or sections, 503 before the hub is up). nerva inspect [agent] [--as VIEW] [--section tools|skills|prompt|mcp|status] [--json] (cmd_inspect, agents/cli/nerva.py:1029; render_inspector :1046) prints the same payload section by section, or as it came. The HUD's Inspector panel (frontend/src/panels/inspector.tsx, Console → Admin) reads the same route with a status line, an As switch and folding sections. Tests: tests/test_inspector.py (43) builds a partial orchestrator over the coordinator's real ToolRPC registry. It covers the guest's tools equal to ToolProfileResolver's set and not the registry, every view's posture and bindings, the agent's list, the marks and the cut, the loop off, a failing resolver, an unwired runtime, the skills, the prompt (skills block, core memory, rails, empty message, tokens), the unfrozen core block, masking, the withheld prompt, the 64 KiB cap on a split character, no leaked binding, MCP liveness, the status line and safe mode, section order, the route (payload, defaults, refusals, admin token, guard snapshot, 503) and the CLI (--json equal to the payload, rendering, --section, the loop-off line, the tree, one list of views and sections). frontend/src/panels/inspector.test.tsx has 4. 82 mutants: 79 caught, ten after survivors got cases. The local half is admin-guarded and working. `GET /api/models/local` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:103) lists LM Studio/Ollama models and marks the active one. `POST /api/models/local/switch` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:363) switches models, and `POST /api/llm/load` / `unload` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:487, agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:515) load and unload them. The HUD reaches all of this through `LMStudioPanel` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2498). The cloud side is read-only. `GET /api/llm/auth-profiles` (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:442) returns masked Anthropic/Gemini pool status, rendered by `AuthProfilesPanel` (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2711). HybridRouter builds those pools only from environment variables (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:328, via `AuthProfilePool.from_env` at agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:86). The shared command catalog the row depends on exists: `GET /api/commands` (agents/core/routers/commands.py:29) with name/description/tier/usage, and `GET /api/quickbar/help` (agents/core/routers/quickbar.py:59). Both are consumed by `QuickbarPanel` (frontend/src/panels/quickbar.tsx:98), which lists commands but does not complete a partial line. Path completion is conditional in the rationale on a terminal client shipping. `nerva` has only the one-shot `nerva chat` and no interactive composer, so path completion is not owed yet.
reviews.remaining: (1) No provider options: no route returns models grouped by provider (cloud and local) with cost hints, and cost_tracker's price table is not shown per model. (2) No save-key: no admin route writes a provider API key to the secret store and returns the refreshed model list. The pools read env vars only, so a key saved at runtime would never reach the router without a pool rebuild. (3) No disconnect: no route removes a provider's credential and rebuilds its pool, so there is no single place to revoke a provider. No audit event exists for either write. `/api/secrets/broker` (agents/core/routers/secrets.py:29, agents/core/routers/secrets.py:56) stores action-time `{{secret:NAME}}` values, not the router's provider keys. (4) No slash completion: neither the chat composer nor QuickbarPanel completes command names or their `usage` arguments from `/api/commands` as the user types.

Nerva now knows which surface holds each microphone. A surface arms only if the owner allowed its kind; one device's microphone has one holder at a time; and arming, pausing, resuming and stopping carry the surface's identity and are audited. This is the adaptation's missing concept, on top of the voice primitives that already existed (wake word, push-to-talk and hands-free capture, TTS, STT, capabilities, and H222's listening indicator). The lease table is agents/core/voice/mic.py (MicArbiter, agents/core/voice/mic.py:93; one process-wide ARBITER, agents/core/voice/mic.py:232).
(1) Surfaces and devices. A surface is kind:client: host:hub (the hub's own wake-word pipeline), hud:<tab> or mobile:<device> (ARMABLE, agents/core/voice/mic.py:39). A Wyoming satellite has its own microphone and is not armed here. A lease is for one device. host is the machine the hub runs on, and a browser that the route sees on loopback shares it. The route decides that from the address a trusted proxy vouches for (_mic_device, agents/core/routers/voice.py:527), so a LAN client cannot claim to be local. Otherwise a browser gets remote:hud:<tab>, and every phone gets mobile:<device>.
(2) One holder per device. A second surface arming a held device is refused, naming the holder (MicRefused mic_busy, agents/core/voice/mic.py:49; HTTP 409). With take_over, it pauses the holder and tells it (on_change, agents/core/voice/mic.py:144). A pause frees the device (agents/core/voice/mic.py:199). A resume asks again, both for consent and for the device's holder (agents/core/voice/mic.py:212). A stop releases the lease (agents/core/voice/mic.py:221).
(3) Consent. A kind arms only if the setting voice.mic_surfaces allows it (allowed_kinds, agents/core/voice/mic.py:59). The setting is a declared tags setting whose values are validated against host, hud and mobile (agents/core/settings_db.py:219, :902). The default is hud and mobile (DEFAULT_ALLOWED, agents/core/voice/mic.py:40): surfaces someone uses on purpose. The hub's always-on listener needs host added. So VoiceChannel.start (agents/core/channels/voice.py:29) opens the host microphone only with a lease. Before this, it started at boot with no check. It stops the pipeline when taken over and starts it again when given back (_on_lease, agents/core/channels/voice.py:48). Withdrawn consent ends a lease at its next renewal.
(4) Leases lapse. A browser or phone lease lapses LEASE_SECONDS (45, agents/core/voice/mic.py:42) after its last renewal (_expire_locked, agents/core/voice/mic.py:108). The host pipeline's lease does not lapse. The table holds at most 32 leases.
(5) Audit. Every arm, take-over, pause, stop and refusal is one audit row naming the surface and the device. A renewal is not.
(6) Routes, all user-guarded. GET /api/voice/mic answers who holds each device, the paused leases and the allowed kinds (agents/core/routers/voice.py:548). POST /api/voice/mic/arm (agents/core/routers/voice.py:557) takes hud or mobile and answers 403 or 409. /pause, /resume and /stop act on a lease by name (agents/core/routers/voice.py:576, agents/core/routers/voice.py:587, agents/core/routers/voice.py:601).
(7) The HUD. The voice loop arms its lease before getUserMedia (frontend/src/voice.ts:414; armMic, frontend/src/mic-lease.ts:47) and renews it every 20 s (frontend/src/voice.ts:434). It releases the lease on every end of the loop (frontend/src/voice.ts:135). If a renewal is refused, it stops and says who took the microphone. Only a hub refusal blocks: a hub that cannot answer does not. The loop offers take over (takeOver, frontend/src/voice.ts:454; the voice pill, frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:255). The voice settings list the holders, with pause, resume and stop (MicLeases, frontend/src/mic-leases.tsx:17).
Tests: tests/test_h247_mic_lease.py has 27. They cover consent, kinds, client and device names, withdrawn consent, a conflict and a take-over, renewal, lapse, pause and resume, stop, the bound, status, the numbers, the setting and its reading, the voice channel's lease, loopback against LAN against a phone, the routes and their guard. frontend/src/test/mic-lease.test.tsx has 10: arm before the mic, a named holder and take-over, no consent, an unreachable hub, renewal and loss, a cancelled start, an unmount, a click handler, the pill and the settings list.
61 mutants: 60 caught, eleven of them after survivors got cases. One of those survivors exposed a device name that was too long for a 64-character client id; it is fixed. The last was a redundant check, removed. Not in this row: no install path installs a voice engine. The named STT/TTS command-provider change touched only the voice router's provider catalog, intake and selector fields; the mic lease routes and the consent check are unchanged, and both test files above pass. Re-review on 2026-10-02: InputBar now passes its active agent into the image hook; voice arming, capture and liveness controls remain unchanged. Collateral active-image review (2026-10-03, a30603e0): cockpit InputBar now treats an explicitly selected prior image like a fresh image for submit readiness. Wake-word, microphone, push-to-talk and voice-control branches are untouched; pinned citations remain unchanged. The complete frontend suite passes 1,881 cases; existing equivalent verdict preserved.

reviews.summary: A settings reset now shows what it will change, never touches a secret and can be undone, and the HUD marks every setting that differs from its default. Hermes' config-reset and defaults surface is covered, on top of H157's search, secret-free export, dry-run import and per-category reset. (1) Defaults. Every declared row that is not a secret carries its declared default (agents/core/settings_db.py:617, in _mark_overlay :608, used by GET /api/admin/settings and each category read). A secret carries none. The Settings panel marks a row whose value, or staged edit, differs from its default ("changed", with the default in its tooltip); a ↺ button stages the default and the usual save writes it through the validated PUT (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2853). (2) A preview before any reset. plan_reset (agents/core/settings_db.py:1242) computes what a reset of one category, or of every category, would write: each declared setting that is neither a secret nor a route-only row (settings_db.ROUTE_ONLY: the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) and whose stored value is not its default. POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset and POST /api/admin/settings/reseed take {"dry_run": true} and answer the changes as current → default without writing anything (agents/core/routers/admin.py:391, :430; _dry_run_asked, :379; only a JSON true, in a body of at most 4 KB). The changes use describe_changes, so a credential-shaped value shows as (hidden). Arming the reset in the HUD asks for that preview and lists it, and counts the settings kept (secrets and route-only rows, all labelled secrets) and names the settings the posture still forces (ResetPreview, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:64; ResetCategory, :92). (3) The reseed no longer deletes the store. It used to run DELETE FROM settings, wiping every setting, secrets included, with no preview and no way back. It is now the per-category reset over every category: secrets and route-only rows are kept (and named), rows nothing declares are left, it takes a JSON request from this origin only (415/403 otherwise, as H157's writes), and it is audited with the settings that moved (agents/core/routers/admin.py:430). The v1 admin page sends it as JSON (agents/web/static/admin.js:1520). The HUD gets "reset every category…" with the same preview (ResetAll, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:115). (4) Undo. reset_settings (agents/core/settings_db.py:1281) writes the defaults and records what it replaced in settings_resets (:119) in the same transaction, keeping the last 20 (RESETS_KEPT, :1260). POST /api/admin/settings/undo (agents/core/routers/admin.py:461; undo_last_reset, agents/core/settings_db.py:1336) puts back the latest reset not yet undone. A setting changed since that reset, one its declaration no longer accepts, or one no longer declared is left as it is and named in skipped. The undo is audited, and the listeners hear every value a reset or an undo writes, so the webhook receiver switch follows it. GET /api/admin/settings/resets (agents/core/routers/admin.py:91; list_resets, agents/core/settings_db.py:1323) lists the resets, newest first, naming settings but never their values. The HUD shows "last reset: <scope> · N settings · <time>" with "undo…" (UndoReset, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:135). Every reset and undo in the HUD is a two-step ConfirmAction at the REVERSIBLE tier (H168). Adapted from the row's ask: the reseed does not go through the approval queue's irreversible tier, because it is no longer irreversible. It keeps secrets, previews, and can be undone. Routing it through the queue would need a new kernel action kind for it, and none is declared (agents/core/kernel/registry.py's one settings kind is H613's settings.voice_command). Tests: tests/test_settings_defaults_undo.py has 24: defaults on rows and none for secrets; the plan (what moves, never a secret); a recorded reset and its undo; nothing moved means nothing recorded; the listeners; a setting changed since, no longer valid or no longer declared left as it is; latest first; the list keeps 20 and names no values; everything reset with secrets and undeclared rows kept; and the routes (admin-only, dry run, a hidden credential, JSON only with a 4 KB bound, the reseed's preview, audit and undo, nothing to undo 404, and /resets not taken for a category). frontend/src/test/settings-reset-undo.test.tsx has 7. The H157 reset test, the H153b reseed test (a JSON body) and the settings row-shape test (default) follow. Of 54 mutants, all 54 are caught, ten of them after survivors got cases. Image-recovery collateral review (2026-10-02): changes to shared CLI/image-turn or HUD local-panel disclosure are outside this row's claimed symbols. Complete base evidence pins and unchanged text anchors verified; existing capability/status preserved. Claim-specific source inspection is recorded in the bounded image source review. House-presence collateral review (2026-10-02, 39a82964): the shared HUD diff adds only the explicit HousePanel explanation request, display state and button; this row's claimed UI and producer branches are outside that change. Its prior verdict is preserved after source-diff inspection, 66 focused backend/API checks, 1,874 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build. The full backend run first stopped at the expected stale Hermes generated report, with no behavior failure before that point.

Chats and data now have a governed lifecycle: prune, archive and VACUUM run in one interval-gated sweep, which runs in one process at a time.

Settings. The sweep reads new retention rows: `retention.min_interval_hours` (24), `retention.vacuum_after_prune` (on) and `retention.min_vacuum_interval_days` (30, Hermes' default) (agents/core/settings_db.py:458-460). Whole-number bounds are enforced on every lifecycle row (_LIFECYCLE_INT_BOUNDS, agents/core/settings_db.py:767). The Hermes keys map as follows. `sessions.auto_archive` / `auto_archive_days` is `memory.auto_archive_days`, the only archive setting (critic note 5). `auto_prune` is `retention.enabled`. `retention_days` is `retention.conversation_ttl_days`.

Scheduling. One hourly job, `data-retention-sweep`, replaces the 03:30 cron and the separate 03:40 archiver (schedule_retention, agents/core/scheduler_service.py:184; run_retention_purge, :600). It runs run_sweep (agents/core/lifecycle_sweep.py:213). The sweep is claimed through a compare-and-set row in checkpoints.db, `maintenance_state` (CheckpointManager.claim_sweep, agents/core/checkpoint.py:459). The hub and the coordinator share that row, so a sweep runs at most once per `min_interval_hours`. A stored claim counts as clock-skewed only when it is more than one interval ahead. Only the process holding `hub.lock` runs the sweep. A coordinator runs it only when no hub is running (_ours, agents/core/lifecycle_sweep.py:205). A read-only pid probe decides this (install_identity.hub_lock_held_elsewhere, agents/core/install_identity.py), so only the hub's view of live chats ever decides.

Archiving (reversible, runs without approval). Chats idle longer than `auto_archive_days` are archived using H218's `archived_at` (session_archive.run_auto_archive, agents/core/session_archive.py:79). A pinned chat and every chat a channel or the hub is on (Orchestrator.live_session_ids, agents/core/orchestrator.py:1692) are exempt. The pin is new: POST /sessions/{id}/pin and /unpin (user-guarded, agents/core/routers/sessions.py:96), a `pinned_at` stamp and a HUD toggle and badge. Unarchiving or resuming a chat stamps `kept_at` (CheckpointManager.unarchive, agents/core/checkpoint.py:380). Idle time is measured from the later of the last turn and that stamp, so a chat the owner kept is not archived again straight away.

Deletion. Retention deletes only chats that are archived, not pinned, idle past the horizon, and archived at least DELETE_GRACE_DAYS (7) earlier (agents/core/retention.py:233; _EXPIRED_WHERE, agents/core/checkpoint.py:409). Every chat therefore shows in the Archived view for a week before it can go. Deletion is measured by the database's clock, not file mtime. Each chat goes through H218's backup-first delete_session under its turn lease (delete_expired, agents/core/session_archive.py:409). The sweep's backups are kept until the next prune. The session row is deleted first, inside the same transaction, and only while it is still expired (delete_session_rows, agents/core/checkpoint.py:568). A pin, unarchive or resume that lands mid-delete therefore keeps the chat. Audit rows, private ingestion and attachments are pruned by their TTLs as before (run_retention, agents/core/retention.py:186). Orphan compaction archives are pruned. Orphan transcripts are only counted, no longer deleted (a narrowing).

VACUUM. The sweep compacts checkpoints.db, audit.db and artifacts.db only after a prune deleted rows from that database, and at most every `min_vacuum_interval_days`. A database whose VACUUM waits stays pending for the next due sweep (_vacuum, agents/core/lifecycle_sweep.py:184). checkpoints.db connections wait up to 30 s for its lock. audit.db is compacted from outside the protected module, under the logger's own `_lock` (vacuum_audit, agents/core/retention.py:382). artifacts.db is compacted under the upload lock.

Governance. Every widening goes through the approval queue's irreversible tier. A write that makes retention delete deeper than a person approved is queued as a tier-3 `settings.retention` task (agents/core/autonomy/irreversible.py, a shared helper for critic note 28). The task is applied only on a human accept (execute, irreversible.py:112): a machine decider or a non-approval decision is refused. The executor is registered in autonomy_coordinator.build_executor (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1722). Every writer is gated:
- PUT /api/admin/settings/{category} answers 202 for the gated keys and writes the rest (admin_put_category, agents/core/routers/admin.py:195). It answers 503, writing nothing, when the queue cannot take the task.
- An import is refused 409.
- A reset or reseed keeps the keys it would deepen.
- An undo is refused 409.
- `nerva config set` refuses (agents/cli/nerva.py:917).

The card names every class the accept deepens, with its new horizon. It counts what the new values delete: archived chats past the horizon, whatever their archive age; chats the next sweep archives; and audit rows. A capped count is shown as N+, and ingestion and attachments as "not counted". The same deepened classes go into the audit row. The approved state is a per-class horizon snapshot (APPROVED_STATE, agents/core/retention.py:228). Only apply_approved raises it (:633). Every direct narrowing lowers it (lower_approval, :331), so deepening again needs a new approval. An accept is refused `changed_since_request` when a class would end deeper than the card showed, or when the owner narrowed it since the request. The sweep never deletes beyond max(current, approved) (effective_horizons, :267). With nothing approved it deletes nothing (`awaiting_approval`). The HUD shows "sent to Approvals", a "retention is on but not confirmed" banner with Confirm (or the waiting card), the Decision Inbox card and the kept or refused keys on reset and import. GET /api/admin/retention (admin) gives the stored, approved and effective horizons, the sweep state and a waiting card's id.

Residuals, stated where they live:
- `settings.retention` is not a registered Action Kernel kind (agents/core/kernel is protected; owner item P30.1). Under JARVIS_TASK_MEDIATION enforce or hold, a widening write answers 503, and the card carries no capability manifest.
- The audit VACUUM borrows AuditLogger's private lock and path. A first-class AuditLogger.vacuum() is a protected edit, and the coordinator's own audit writes wait at most 5 s.
- A crashed hub's reused pid makes the coordinator skip, which deletes nothing. A hub in another pid namespace sharing the data root is not seen.
- An install that already had retention on deletes nothing until the owner confirms once.

Tests:
- tests/test_h262_lifecycle_sweep.py (69 cases) covers the settings bounds, the claim, the hub-only sweep, the archive phase with pins, live chats and kept chats, the grace, deletion order and continuations, late pins, backups, the approved-horizon clamp, VACUUM per database, and the scheduler.
- tests/test_h262_retention_approval.py (48 cases) covers the gate on every writer, the executor, the card's counts and title, lowering, staleness, card reuse, the pending lookup and the state route.
- The rewritten test_retention, test_h218, test_h427, test_scheduler_health and test_ingestion_data_lifecycle suites follow the new semantics.
- frontend/src/test/sessions-pin.test.tsx (6), frontend/src/test/settings-retention.test.tsx (19) and tests/frontend/admin-retention.test.js (2) pin the HUD and v1.

Review and mutation:
- An adversarial review in four lenses confirmed 14 findings (3 MAJOR: same-sweep deletion, an understated card, a coordinator sweep). Two verified fix rounds and a verify pass closed them all.
- 59 mutants were run: all killed, 3 by cases added after a first pass.

Test manual: MEM-206, GOV-293. Adapted from Hermes: its sessions.* prune, archive, vacuum and min-interval lifecycle, with one archive state (H218), backup-first deletion after a visible grace, a hub-owned sweep, and widening held at the approval queue's irreversible tier. Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability. Collateral active-image review (2026-10-03, a30603e0): the only drifted evidence for this row is agents/core/orchestrator.py. Its diff changes complete_selected_image_turn for explicitly reviewed browser image turns; this row's cited implementation lines and feature path are unchanged. The focused active-image and route regressions pass, and this existing code-equivalent verdict is preserved.

reviews.summary: H270 stays PARTIAL; the triage's "already equivalent" does not survive contact with the code, and this re-read retires three claims the row had carried since before H502 (#1174 moved the hash while the text stood still) plus one the text was about to inherit. Hermes' contract has two halves and Nerva has only one of them. Outbound (what a child inherits) is genuinely stronger than Hermes and is tested: scrub_child_env (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:172-210) is default-deny with SAFE_ENV_PREFIXES (:17-33) plus the three-name JARVIS_CHILD_ALLOWED_ENV (:47-51), covered by tests/test_environment_primitives.py:62,90; STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST (agents/core/mcp/client.py:161-173) with stdio_env_baseline (:245-280) drops a credential-shaped name even when it is on the static list (:275, _SECRET_LIKE :174-176), covered by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:351 — and since H502 the baseline is the DEFAULT, not an opt-in: stdio_env_baseline_enabled() returns env_flag(STDIO_ENV_BASELINE_FLAG, True) (:179-190; flag :90 "Default ON"), docs/FLAGS.md says "on by default since H502" (its MCP defaults block, the JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE entry and the flag table row), and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins unset-flag → OPENAI_API_KEY withheld and =0 → full inherit (the row previously cited :395-399 as pinning the opposite; that was the pre-#1174 test, which at 45be62bd read "Flag off (default): historical behaviour — inherit everything"). The outbound allowlist's one deliberate exception is the owner's own: a name listed in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — owner-declared and host-wide, not an inbound gate. What #1179 changed here is disclosure, not policy: the module docstring (:17-39) now names the filesystem as a second recovery route for a same-UID child (cwd defaults to the hub's, so open(".env") reaches the file the keys came from), cwd_secret_files (:215-242) reports a readable .env/.env.local in the child's cwd, and _merged_env (:561-572) logs a WARNING "withholding is undercut" (:567) beside the INFO count, filenames only — pinned by tests :830-853 and :854-890. None of it touches a name policy, a writer or the override path, so it moves nothing for this row. The fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) is likewise off-subject: it added tool_patterns_over_bounds (agents/core/mcp/client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ (:407-418) and a bounds refusal for tools_allow/tools_deny in admin_mcp_add (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:202-208); none of it reads or writes an env name, and MCPServerConfig still has no env field, so only line numbers moved (client.py +19 from the new helper on and +31 from that __init__ block on; routers/mcp.py +4 from the filter check on). Inbound (what a surface may persist) does not exist as a policy at all: no ENV_VAR_NAME/ENV_WRITE/WRITE_DENYLIST/writable_env symbol anywhere in agents/, scripts/, tests/ or frontend/src/, and no `config.write` kind in agents/core/capability_actions.py. A correction the row must carry, because it shapes the deliverable: Hermes' hijack names are NOT all absent from the code. LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and PAGER appear nowhere outside the research docs, but PATH and SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are MEMBERS of the two outbound allowlists — deliberately, because a child needs them as plumbing — and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 pinning that collect_tokens keeps only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. So the two allowlists the rationale points at as the pattern to reuse admit precisely the names Hermes forbids on write; the inbound registry has to be its own list, and "run overrides through the same name policy" is not by itself a fix, since that policy passes PATH/NODE_PATH/PYTHONPATH untouched. Confirmed there is still no env writer to gate: no os.environ assignment in agents/ except the reality harness's JARVIS_STRICT_EGRESS toggle (agents/core/observability/reality_harness.py:685,714; scripts/qa_audit_probes.py and scripts/install_smoke.py set os.environ only as probe/smoke harnesses); no set_key/dotenv write; agents/core/paths.py:135-139 only copies .env.example verbatim; GET /api/admin/env (agents/core/routers/admin.py:561-573) is read-only and mask-redacted, and its one sibling, GET /api/admin/env/sources (H273), is read-only and returns key names and layers only, so neither writes the environment; the HUD states it in its own copy (frontend/src/panels/workflows-advanced.tsx:48 "There is NO route to change either"). Nerva's actual config writer is settings_db.put_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:949-984), which UPSERTs only DEFAULTS-declared keys and skips the rest (agents/core/settings_db.py:965-975), behind validate_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:861-897) and the 422 at agents/core/routers/admin.py:195-206 — the right shape, but over settings keys, not env names. Three things are nevertheless still owed, so this is not equivalence. (1) The row's own deliverable — a declared-names allowlist at the write boundary, depends_on "the key registry" — is unbuilt, and the rationale defers rather than excludes it ("the moment the config writer lands, this must land with it"). (2) The MCP env boundary is unrefused: MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:131-142) has no env field and sets no model_config, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" SILENTLY DROPS an `env` body key rather than refusing it — reproduced at HEAD both on the model (model_config {} and env absent from model_dump) and end to end through TestClient: POST /api/admin/mcp with {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}} → 200 {"ok": true}, the stored MCPServer.env is {} and to_config() carries no env — and POST builds the MCPServer without one (:212-224). The non-round-trip half IS now pinned — test_per_server_env_has_no_owner_reachable_config_surface (tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522, from #1174) asserts "env" not in MCPServerConfig.model_fields, to_config (agents/core/mcp/client.py:798-812) exports no env and load_from_config (:814-849) ignores one — but no test asserts the route REFUSES an env body, and the field it would fill is live: MCPServer.env (:424) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Reachability today: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449; no add form, nothing sends env) and no CLI or script adds servers, so the raw API is the only path. (3) Per-server overrides still bypass the allowlist in both branches: stdio_env_baseline applies them unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:278-279; docstring agents/core/mcp/client.py:253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch — reachable only under JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 since H502 — does merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env) unfiltered (:575-576). Latent, not live: the only production caller passing an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret plus the WORLDVIEW_HOST_ENV names set on the host (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:222-227, :49-56), and the admin route cannot pass one. Also checked and cleared: scripts/nerva_import.py IS a setup-flow writer that persists foreign env-var names verbatim (docstring scripts/nerva_import.py:31-32, .env lines scripts/nerva_import.py:357-358, JSON walk scripts/nerva_import.py:371, settings.json env block scripts/nerva_import.py:389-393, SecretStore write scripts/nerva_import.py:1034), but _SECRET_NAME_RE (scripts/nerva_import.py:85) is applied on every path and admits only credential-shaped names — tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 is the one existing test that exercises a hijack-shaped name (EDITOR) at an import boundary and pins it dropped — and SecretStore (agents/core/secrets.py) never exports a name to a process env (it reads only JARVIS_SECRET_KEY, :111). reviews.remaining:
Nerva has no write-side policy for environment-variable names — the row's deliverable (a declared-names allowlist, depends_on "the key registry") does not exist, and the row defers it rather than excluding it. #1179 changed nothing on this row's subject: its client.py change is an outbound disclosure (cwd_secret_files :215-242 and the "withholding is undercut" WARNING in _merged_env :561-572), not a name policy or a writer. Neither did the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1: tool_patterns_over_bounds, a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ and a tools_allow/tools_deny bounds refusal in admin_mcp_add) — it touches no env name, writer or override path and only moved line numbers. H502 (#1174) did change item 3 and half of item 2, and that is folded in here. Three items owed, two shippable today against real surfaces:

1. THE REGISTRY (the row's core item, blocked on its stated dependency). No ENV_VAR_NAME allowlist/denylist exists anywhere (grep for ENV_VAR_NAME/ENV_WRITE/WRITE_DENYLIST/writable_env across agents/, scripts/, tests/, frontend/src/ is empty at HEAD) and no `config.write` capability kind exists in agents/core/capability_actions.py. Of Hermes' hijack names, LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and PAGER are named nowhere in code or tests — but PATH, SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) ARE named, as members of the two OUTBOUND allowlists, and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 (pinned dropped at tests/test_nerva_import.py:825). Design consequence: the outbound lists cannot double as the write-side registry — they deliberately admit the plumbing names Hermes forbids on write — so the registry is a separate, inbound-only list. When any env/config writer lands, that allowlist must land in the SAME PR, refusing an undeclared name before authorization — the shape of agents/core/capability_actions.py:139-143 refusing missing_inputs before the authorizer at :151-152.

2. THE MCP `env` BOUNDARY IS UNREFUSED (shippable now; the "untested" half closed with #1174). MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:131-142) sets no `model_config`, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" makes `POST /api/admin/mcp {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}}` return 200 and silently drop the key instead of refusing it — reproduced end to end at HEAD through TestClient (200 {"ok": true}; stored MCPServer.env == {}; to_config() has no env key). The field it would populate is live — MCPServer.env (agents/core/mcp/client.py:424) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Already pinned by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522: `env` is not a MCPServerConfig field, to_config (:798-812) does not export it and load_from_config (:814-849) does not read it. Reachability: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449) and no CLI adds servers, so the raw admin API is the only path today. Still owed: `extra="forbid"` (or an explicit named refusal) on MCPServerConfig, plus a test asserting the route refuses an `env` body rather than swallowing it — and the same refusal must cover the hijack names above on the day `env` becomes operator-settable.

3. PER-SERVER `env` BYPASSES THE ALLOWLIST IN BOTH BRANCHES. stdio_env_baseline applies overrides unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:278-279; docstring :253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch does `merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env)` with no filter (:575-576). The "decide whether the baseline should become the default" half of this item is DONE: since H502 the baseline is on unless JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 (:179-190; docs/FLAGS.md "on by default since H502") and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins both directions, so the legacy branch is now the explicit escape hatch rather than the shipped path. Owed: gate per-server overrides on the item-1 write-side registry (NOT merely on STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST + _SECRET_LIKE — that policy passes PATH, SHELL, NODE_PATH and would pass an operator-supplied PATH/NODE_PATH override untouched), or make the bypass an explicitly reviewed, audited exception. Severity, checked directly rather than inferred: LATENT. `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field, the admin route constructs MCPServer without one (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:212-224), and the only production caller passing an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret plus the WORLDVIEW_HOST_ENV names (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:222-227, :49-56). No untrusted input reaches the override loop, so this is a boundary to close before `env` becomes operator-settable, not a live hole. The outbound allowlist's one intentional exception — a name the owner lists in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — is owner-declared and host-wide, and is not this row's write boundary.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, then fixed after eight adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. The fourth found that the MCP transport and the HTTP user guard asked different questions, so a lapsed or revoked user credential locked every route but left MCP open to a local caller; that the coordinator built its Orchestrator before the load, so its audit rows went unkeyed beside the hub's keyed ones; that an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1) escaped both loopback checks; and that the CLI sent the admin token to any hub. The fifth found that the admin tier still trusted a loopback caller once no admin credential was active, so after the owner revoked every credential a local process with no token could mint a fresh user token over HTTP and reopen the user routes and MCP (older than H273, but it falsified this row's credential sentence); that a managed user token that had expired counted as never configured; that the CLI asked the owner to set an admin token it had withheld; and that the supervisor wrote its respawns apart from a run-log named in .env. The sixth found that the sentence about minting did not hold where no admin credential was ever configured, that the offline recovery wrote a tokens.db the hub never read when the data home was named only in a .env (and a packaged build had none to run), that the CLI's withheld message fired on refusals https would not fix, and that a named-pipe .env still split the run-log. The seventh found that the supervisor now told its child a default the hub never read (a named-pipe .env hid the runtime from the brief), that the packaged recovery revived env tokens that had been rotated away or revoked, and that the CLI still asked for a token that was set. The eighth found that the packaged recovery still missed a token in the start environment or a moved data home, and left a LAN-bound app unable to start, and that the new hint called a valid user token refused on an admin verb and proposed a rotate that revoked the owner's working admin token. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only.

The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:356) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour:
- Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO.
- The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used.
- PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch.
- The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read.
- A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once.
- It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?".
- files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read.

provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:531) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running.

The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:454) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once:
- serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:244). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard.
- The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:457). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed.
- The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:106), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:73): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:481), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:72; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:110; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183).
- agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect.
- PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:83), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry.
- Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off.

Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:517) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment.
- What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:91).
- JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72).
- Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:84): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies.

The lists are measured, not declared:
- A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there.
- A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:666).

The two false read-again entries are fixed:
- The MCP transport, the HTTP user guard and the MCP identity check ask one predicate, _user_credential_required (agents/web.py:286; agents/core/routers/mcp.py:393). A token from .env guards MCP on this machine and lets a remote client in. The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:108): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Such a credential that has lapsed, been rotated away or been revoked locks MCP exactly as it locks HTTP. The admin guard asks the same question for its tier (_admin_configured, agents/web.py:136), and so does the owner flag on /chat, so where an admin credential was ever configured and every credential is revoked or has expired, no local process mints its way back in over HTTP. Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits).
- The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:35), which re-reads the client ids after the load.

Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:193): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:134) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too.

derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:318) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:285). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe.

Surfaces:
- GET /api/admin/env/sources (agents/core/routers/admin.py:576) is admin-guarded and no-store, at the same boundary as GET /api/admin/env. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It also names what the load did with each file (path, kind, present, read); values are never included.
- `nerva doctor`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:702):
  - Reading the hub. It reads the running hub's own table when /readyz is ok, asking without a credential first. Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:379). The hub address brackets an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1 gives http://[::1]:8080; scripts/doctor.py:297), and an unbracketed IPv6 address, whatever its first group (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 too), is read the way http.client dials it (scripts/doctor.py:337). The admin credential goes only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address rather than its spelling (127.0.0.2, 127.1, localhost., ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 count; scripts/doctor.py:353). config_sources sends it only after a refusal, and runtime_resolves only when no user token is set (scripts/doctor.py:395). Otherwise the doctor predicts the table from its own shell and says which of the two it did and why.
  - Which keys. It shows every key a .env file sets, and the shell's keys that the hub's code reads or that carry Nerva's prefixes. The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, *_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's *_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:570).
  - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:816). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:588); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters.
  - Hub mode. On this machine it reads the files the hub names to tell names from value material. For a hub on another machine it shows only the names Nerva knows, and says why.
  - Other reports. It names a .env that is not UTF-8, which the hub's load fails on (env_not_utf8), and a named pipe it does not open. For each key it prints the .env values a higher layer overrides and the note. Any failure inside the check becomes a named reason, never a crash.
- The `nerva` CLI's client (agents/cli/client.py:111) follows the same transport rules: no redirect (urllib carried both tokens to wherever one pointed), no proxy to a hub on this machine, and http or https only. Its loopback rule is the doctor's, pinned equal over one table of spellings. It sends the admin token only to a hub on this machine or over https (agents/cli/client.py:151), never in clear text to another host, whether or not a user token is set; the user token goes to the hub it names. When it withheld the admin token and the hub refuses, it names that as one possible cause beside the user token, never as the only one (review-H273g m3). The hint reads the hub's own reason for the tier it wanted: a verb that needs the admin tier asks for JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN when only the user token is set, only a token of the wanted tier that was sent is named as refused, a hub with no token of the tier configured is named as such, and the recovery offered is the additive token_recover.py issue (rotate only for a leaked token, since it revokes every token of the tier; review-H273i m2); nerva status reads the same reason on its runnable and e-stop lines (_auth_hint, agents/cli/nerva.py:696; review-H273h m3, review-H273i m2, n4).
- The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:577). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown or unreadable stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection. `nerva config list` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:867).
- The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:254).

Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment.

Known limits:
- On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled.
- A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound.
- In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once.
- JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split.
- The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why.
- A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1).
- A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together.
- A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked.
- A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py.
- Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value.
- A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token.
- The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines).
- The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it.
- Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it.
- The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today.
- JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before.

Tests:
- tests/test_env_provenance.py (61 cases): parity and fuzz (tests/test_env_provenance.py:130), the named pipe, the plugin manager's order and the posture overlay.
- tests/test_doctor_hub_credential.py (8): a real redirect and a real proxy, pinning where the credential goes (tests/test_doctor_hub_credential.py:93).
- tests/test_h273c_provenance_review.py (56): the import, the names withheld, the bound-mapping scan and the second round's nits.
- tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py (74 cases, the third round):
  - the start measured and the lists by where they are used (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:119);
  - knobs the start reads, in effect from a .env (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:158);
  - the bind guard through serve.py and the lifespan, the redaction floor, one load per process, the refused roots;
  - the MCP transport, the OAuth routes, and the doctor's and CLI's transport rules;

reviews.summary: The hub now speaks systemd's sd_notify, and the operator can tell the model what kind of machine this is. Host detection was already richer than Hermes' (probe_host, agents/core/host_probe.py:406; detect_hardware, agents/core/hardware.py:215; /healthz and /readyz, agents/core/routers/ops.py:42 and :149), but nothing wrote to NOTIFY_SOCKET and the model was told only the live backend. agents/core/sd_notify.py: notify (agents/core/sd_notify.py:66) sends one datagram to NOTIFY_SOCKET, a path or an @abstract name (_address, agents/core/sd_notify.py:48), and never raises (a socket nobody listens on is a debug line); with NOTIFY_SOCKET unset (a shell, Docker, launchd, Windows) nothing is sent (enabled, agents/core/sd_notify.py:61). serve.py runs sd_notify.NotifyingServer (agents/core/sd_notify.py:159), a uvicorn.Server subclass: after the port is bound its startup calls NOTIFIER.ready with /readyz's own body (Notifier.ready, agents/core/sd_notify.py:129), so READY=1 follows the bind and a failed bind is never announced. The lifespan sends nothing, because uvicorn runs it before binding, and a raw `uvicorn agents.web:app` does not speak the protocol (the shipped unit runs serve.py): READY=1 and STATUS=serving once the orchestrator and its agents are loaded, a STATUS naming why when they are not, and from then on a heartbeat task on the event loop sends WATCHDOG=1 every half WATCHDOG_USEC (watchdog_seconds, agents/core/sd_notify.py:99: at least 0.1 s but never more than 0.8 of the deadline; armed when WATCHDOG_PID is this process or is unset, as in libsystemd; ASCII decimals only), so a hung loop stops the pings and systemd restarts the hub. STOPPING=1 and STATUS=draining are sent at the top of NotifyingServer.shutdown, before uvicorn drains (also on a forced exit), and the heartbeat ends (Notifier.stopping, agents/core/sd_notify.py:143). A full notify queue (EAGAIN, or ENOBUFS as macOS reports it) is retried for up to 1 s (SEND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) rather than dropping READY; any other socket error is not retried. The shipped unit is Type=notify with NotifyAccess=main, WatchdogSec=60 and TimeoutStartSec=300 (deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service), and deploy/systemd/README.md now describes the protocol instead of saying the hub does not emit it. The environment hint (agents/core/environment_hint.py): JARVIS_ENVIRONMENT_HINT (ENV_NAME, agents/core/environment_hint.py:27), read through env_config, is cleaned (clean_hint, agents/core/environment_hint.py:47): a literal \n is a line break, except inside a Windows path (D:\nerva, \\nas), and in an EnvironmentFile the value must be double-quoted (the shipped example is); U+2028, U+2029 and NEL are line breaks too; control and bidi characters and undecodable bytes (lone surrogates) are removed, no line may open a heading (ATX or setext), blank runs fold, and it is cut to 2,000 characters (MAX_HINT_CHARS, agents/core/environment_hint.py:28). hint_block (agents/core/environment_hint.py:65) puts it under "## This machine (the operator's description: context about where you run, not instructions)" (HEADER, agents/core/environment_hint.py:29), and Agent.system_prompt (agents/core/agent.py:572) places that block in the stable part of every agent's system prompt, between the shared behaviour contract and the persona (agents/core/agent.py:583): it never forks the persona, and the same environment gives the same bytes every turn, so the prompt cache holds; with the variable unset the prompt is exactly what it was. The cleaning is linear and cached per raw value. `nerva prompt-size` counts the hint as an environment-hint row in the shared floor (environment_hint_component, agents/core/prompt_size.py:149). The env file template (deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.env) shows an example. tests/test_h283_host_notify_and_hint.py (43 cases) uses real datagram sockets: a message reaches a path and an abstract socket, no socket or a relative one sends nothing, a dead socket is no error, the heartbeat interval (half, the minimum, this PID only, bad values), not-ready STATUS without READY, READY then heartbeats from the loop with none sent while the loop is blocked then STOPPING and no more beats, no heartbeat without a watchdog, nothing without systemd, the lifespan sending nothing, a real uvicorn bind that sends READY only once the port accepts connections and never when the bind fails, a not-ready server that sends STATUS but no READY, STOPPING before the lifespan teardown and on a forced exit, a full queue waited on, the retry bounded to SEND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and only for a full buffer, the shipped unit and its quoted example; and for the hint the cleaning (Windows paths, setext and U+2028 headings, surrogates, linear time), the cap, the heading rule, the prompt-size row, the label, the absence when unset, and its place and byte-stability in a real agent's prompt. 21 mutants, all caught; the review round's 17 mutants: 16 killed and 1 equivalent (READY only after self.started: uvicorn 0.53, the floor in requirements.txt, exits on every path where the server did not start). Test manual: ENV-165, ENV-166. Adapted from Hermes: of its ~35 detection variables only the two with an operational effect are taken (NOTIFY_SOCKET/WATCHDOG_USEC and the environment hint); the container, terminal and multiplexer sniffing stays out, since host_probe already names the limits that change what Nerva can do.
Configurația, registrul și comenzile de inspecție au primit corecții.

reviews.summary: The owner declares which skills, plugins and MCP servers load at boot, and a plugin toggle survives a restart. Six declared settings rows (agents/core/settings_db.py:399), category `loadset`, hold comma lists: skills_disabled/skills_only, plugins_disabled/plugins_only, mcp_disabled/mcp_only, editable from the settings page and `nerva config set` (which says a loadset.* key or a plugin switch applies at the next start). A disabled name does not load; a non-empty only-list loads only what it names; the disabled list wins (permits, agents/core/load_set.py:96). A list is read at call time (declared, agents/core/load_set.py:74), trimmed, de-duplicated and bounded to 256 names of at most 128 characters without control characters (parse_names, agents/core/load_set.py:43), and an unreadable store narrows nothing. For plugins the settings page's existing per-plugin `plugins.<id>` switches, which nothing used to read, count too: an explicit off is off (agents/core/load_set.py:84). SkillLoader.discover reads the lists once per pass (agents/core/skills/loader.py:652-653) and a skill named by its registry name or its folder is not registered at all, before any quarantine row (agents/core/skills/loader.py:731); a registration from an earlier pass is taken out when a later pass denies it, the per-pass snapshot is cleared in a finally, and in safe mode (the owner folder unread) no declared name is reported as unknown. PermissionGate switches off the plugins the lists name when it is built (apply_load_set, agents/core/plugin_gate.py:647), and PluginManager.build drops them from orch.plugins before binding oracle_bridge and Argus (_drop_switched_off, agents/core/plugin_manager.py:198), so the probes, the dashboard and WorldView never reach a switched-off plugin. Each gate holds its own copies of the built-in manifests (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:641), so switching one off never reaches the module table or another gate, and the readers of a plugin's enabled state ask the live gate: CloudImageRuntime is wired with orch.permission_gate (_available, agents/core/cloud_image_runtime.py:183) and the capability board reads the gate's manifests (_plugin_records, agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:127). The plugin toggle (toggle_plugin, agents/core/routers/plugins.py:99) keeps the choice in one place, the plugin's plugins.<id> settings switch when it has one and otherwise plugins_disabled; switched on, it leaves plugins_disabled and joins a declared plugins_only (persist_plugin, agents/core/load_set.py:140). It reads the lists fail-closed (read_setting), so an unreadable store is not overwritten, and answers `persisted` (false when the store refused or could not be read, the live toggle standing). It writes a SETTINGS_CHANGE audit row naming the keys, and a re-enable that cannot be audited is switched back off and answers 503 audit_failed. The MCP load registers only the permitted saved servers (agents/web.py:1823-1830); a switched-off one is held (_MCP_HELD, agents/web.py:1800) and written back unchanged by every save, so the saved configuration never loses it, and adding a server of that name or removing it answers 409 `switched_off` naming the list (_held_refusal, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:145). The lists only narrow: nothing is installed, approved, registered or written to the approval store, and a declared name that matches nothing installed is reported as unknown (finish, agents/core/load_set.py:121). The status rows carry it: /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:76), /plugins (agents/core/routers/plugins.py:88) and /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:118) return `load_set` with the declared lists, what was switched off and what is unknown (status, agents/core/load_set.py:132). Safe mode (H275) applies first; the load set narrows further. tests/test_h285_load_set.py (49 cases, plus one in tests/test_cloud_image.py) covers the parsing and its bounds, the six declared rows, the permit table, an unreadable store, a disabled skill and an only-list with their status rows and unknown names, a skill named by its folder, a named-but-absent skill installing or approving nothing (asserted on a private approval store), the skills route, MCP servers switched off and still saved, an MCP only-list, the add and remove refusals for a held server, adding and removing other servers keeping the held one, the MCP list route, the gate's disabled and only lists, the settings-page switch and that only an explicit off counts, that the lists never enable or register, the toggle kept across a restart both ways, a plugin without a settings switch, enabling under an only-list, a toggle the store refuses, and the plugins route. 33 mutants over the parser, the permit table, the persistence, the three loaders, the refusals and the status rows: all caught (two after their cases were added: an explicit off, a refused write). Test manual: ENV-169, ENV-170. Adapted from Hermes: the lists live in the settings store Nerva already persists and edits rather than a YAML file, the plugin toggle writes them, and an MCP server switched off is kept in the saved list rather than dropped.
