reviews.summary:
Both ideas the row said were "worth taking and cheap" are shipped, proven and correct, and the audit's 2026-09-07 nerva_evidence did undersell Nerva. The row is still not equivalent, because the cron half of Hermes' contract has three clauses that are still unmet.

Shipped and verified at 55d625f. The claim lease with a TTL is `autonomy.running_ttl_seconds` (agents/core/settings_db.py:412, default 3600). The coordinator resyncs it on every tick (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:508-513), and `TaskQueue.reap_stuck_running` enforces it (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:2597-2627) through `AutonomyWorker._reap_stuck` (agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:919-933), which `tick` calls first (worker.py:1483-1485). The crash-grace window is the same mechanism, and it meets the row's governance note exactly: the reaper FAILS the stranded row with `result.error="stuck_running_ttl"` + `stuck_since` and audits `autonomy.reaped`. It never re-queues, so an action that was already authorized is never re-executed. Proven by tests/test_q6_autonomy_killswitch_scope_reaper.py:91-135 and manual case GOV-224 (docs/test-manual/07-autonomy-governance.md:690). The jobs lane has the same property on its own path: when a manual request is found `running` and its cross-process gate is free, it is recorded as `unknown` / "execution interrupted after claim; not replayed" (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:203-209), proven by tests/test_job_dispatch.py:130. Beyond the reaper, the scheduled lane has these guards: a 64-stripe cross-process file gate that every firing must hold (jobs_dispatch.py:44-59 via jobs.py:1450-1458); an identity fingerprint that voids a claim if the job was edited after acceptance (jobs_dispatch.py:15-18, 179-184; jobs.py:1468-1472); APScheduler `max_instances=1`; a workdir allowlist (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_workdir.py); estop/kill-switch seams (jobs.py:1479-1483, worker.py:1487-1498); and a validated media deadline, `jobs.media_send_timeout_seconds` (settings_db.py:318, validated at :786; jobs_media.py:18/257).

Correction to the triage on the claim CAS: `claim_mediated` (queue.py:1574-1645) returns None unless `mediation_mode == "enforce"` (queue.py:1577). `resolve_task_mediation_mode()` returns "off" when `JARVIS_TASK_MEDIATION` is unset (agents/core/autonomy/mediation_head_store.py:195-211, docstring: "shipped-dark default"). In that default posture the worker claims with a bare `transition(task.id, RUNNING)` (worker.py:1519-1521). The current `transition_with_group` implementation serializes status validation and mutation under one SQLite write transaction (queue.py:1830-1894), so a second claimant cannot pass the same status edge even though that path does not bind a `mediation_execution_id`. This corrects the earlier claim about the default posture; it does not close the three remaining cron clauses.

What is still owed, and why this is partial. Hermes' text names seven CRON_* clauses. (a) The plain cron path has no per-run wall clock. `_fire_once` → `_execute` → `_ask`/`_brief`/`_deliver` (jobs.py:1460-1522, 1550-1571, 1573-1612, 1683-1709) contains no `asyncio.wait_for` at any level. The script path already uses that pattern, at jobs_scripts.py:405 (120 s) and :455 (30 s). (b) `JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS` defaults to 0, which means unbounded (executor.py:57-60, autonomy_coordinator.py:1439-1442). Out of the box, the only bound on a hung in-process task is the 3600 s reaper. (c) The jobs store opens sqlite with neither `timeout=` nor `PRAGMA busy_timeout` (jobs.py:737-740), while the task queue sets both to 30 s (queue.py:306-308). The row's own rationale excludes the delivery-destination knobs, so they do not count against it (they are also covered by per-job `channel`/`deliver` plus `AUTONOMY_OWNER_CHAT_ID` / `autonomy.owner_chat_id`, jobs.py:1701-1756). The ~14-knob Kanban board is still a product decision, not a slice of this row.

Re-run at 55d625f: the five cited test files (tests/test_q6_autonomy_killswitch_scope_reaper.py, test_job_dispatch.py, test_jobs_media.py, test_executor_budget.py, test_autonomy_worker.py; 95 cases) pass, with zero failures. H487 promotion collateral review (2026-10-02, 42d4678a): the queue diff adds only a private grouped-approval notification outbox and records effects on ordinary grouped withdrawal; the worker diff only drains those effects from approval housekeeping and immediate promotion. The claimed behavior of this row and its other cited source branches are unchanged. Focused H487/grouping/expiry regressions pass; no new capability claim is made for this row. H487 dispatch collateral review (2026-10-02, 17c49efc): the worker diff only rechecks a blocked approval card and its private group/revision at the broker callback and before pushed bookkeeping. The row's claimed routing, speech, completion or cron behavior is unchanged; 163 focused approval/expiry/broker tests pass. No new capability claim is made for this row.
reviews.remaining:
Three cron-lane clauses of Hermes' contract are unmet. The Kanban claim-lease and crash-grace asks are done.

1. HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT: the plain cron path has no per-run wall clock. `JobRunner._fire_once` → `_execute` → `_ask`/`_brief`/`_deliver` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1460-1522, 1568-1589, 1591-1630, 1701-1727) has no `asyncio.wait_for` at any level. In particular, `_send_tracked`/`_send` (jobs.py:1729-1762) awaits the channel adapter bare. A hung Telegram/Discord send therefore holds the job's gate stripe (jobs_dispatch.py:44-59) and its APScheduler `max_instances=1` slot, and nothing breaks it. The script path already does this correctly: `asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._ask(...), 120)` at agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:405 and `asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._send_tracked(...), 30)` at :455. The fix is to apply the same bound to the cron path, ideally as a `jobs.run_timeout_seconds` setting next to the existing `jobs.media_send_timeout_seconds`. The overrun should be recorded as a normal failed run through `_failed`, so the 3-strike pause and the incident path still apply.

2. `JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS` defaults to 0, which means unbounded (agents/core/autonomy/executor.py:57-60, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1439-1442). Out of the box, a hung in-process queued task is bounded only by the 3600 s stuck-running reaper. Fix: give it a non-zero shipped default, or promote it to a validated `autonomy.*` setting like `running_ttl_seconds`, and add a test asserting the default is finite.

3. HERMES_CRON_SESSION_DB_TIMEOUT: the jobs store opens sqlite with neither `timeout=` nor `PRAGMA busy_timeout` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:737-740). The task queue sets `timeout=30.0` + `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:306-308). jobs.db writers therefore fall back to SQLite's 5 s default, on a WAL shared by the gateway drain loop and cron firings. One-line parity fix.

Out of scope, not gaps: the row's own rationale excludes the delivery-destination knobs (_AUTO_DELIVER_PLATFORM / _CHAT_ID / _THREAD_ID, TELEGRAM_CRON_THREAD_ID). The residual ~14-knob multi-agent Kanban board (_BOARD / _WORKSPACES_ROOT / _ATTACHMENTS_ROOT / _GOAL_MODE / _DISPATCH_IN_GATEWAY) is a product decision about whether Nerva grows a shared task board, not a slice of this row.

reviews.summary: A tool now tells the model what this install can do, and the live shape reaches a running session. register_tool takes schema_overrides (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:329), a zero-argument hook (SchemaOverrides, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:99) refused at registration when it is not callable. ToolRPCServer.tools() (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:397) asks every hook each time the tool list is built and merges the answer over the static description and schema (advertised_schema, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:172). The merge (_apply_override, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:125) takes only a `description` (non-empty text of at most 2,048 characters), `properties` whose keys are merged over properties the static schema already declares (an override never invents an argument, changes a declared type, raises or removes a declared maximum, lowers a declared minimum or widens a declared enum; keys it cannot compare, such as a pattern or nested items, are the hook's to keep narrow) and `required` (a list naming declared properties that keeps every statically required name); None or {} changes nothing, and the result must be plain JSON. A hook that raises, or answers with an unknown key, an undeclared property, a non-mapping, a bad `required` or a value JSON cannot carry, is logged at WARNING once per tool, naming the tool and the exception type but not its message, and the static schema is advertised (_OVERRIDE_WARNED, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:52); a hook that recovers is cleared and warns again if it fails again. The static schema is never mutated and every row is a copy. The registry projection gets the same shape, because its records are built from tools() on every snapshot (_tool_records, agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:314, inputs at agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:339), except on the two routes that answer without a token: GET /sandbox/status (tools(live=False)) and GET /api/metrics/capabilities (snapshot(live_schemas=False)) carry the static schemas, so speaker ids, room names and terminal target names never reach an unauthenticated client. At the H672 compaction boundary refresh_tools compares each still-offered tool's description and schema (_shape, agents/core/session_refresh.py:95) and reports the ones that moved as `reshaped` (agents/core/session_refresh.py:153), which is a change and a rebuild (agents/core/session_refresh.py:159); the runtime's tool_offer_refreshed event names them (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:593) and rebuilds the specs, and boundary_note says "tool schemas moved: …" (agents/core/session_refresh.py:180). Four tools use it. terminal_run (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:834) advertises `target` as the targets its runner would run on (TargetRegistry.usable_names("jarvis", "terminal.exec"), agents/core/environments/targets.py:250, a non-auditing read of what authorize() would not deny: enabled, open to the agent, granting terminal.exec), sorted and at most 64, or says in its description that terminal targets are switched off (JARVIS_TERMINAL_TARGETS) or that no target it can run on is enabled, so every call is refused (_terminal_run_overrides, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1282). desktop_run (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:751) says the desktop operator is switched off (JARVIS_DESKTOP_HOST, JARVIS_DESKTOP_ISOLATED) or names the driver_for_host refusal, and otherwise advertises its step `action` as the validator's actions that this host's driver performs (the driver's supported_actions; launch only with the Windows driver), the host being looked at at most once a minute (_desktop_run_overrides, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:131). speak (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:718) advertises `target` as the announce-capable device ids, the rooms whose one announce default resolves (an ambiguous room, or one named like a registered device, is left out) and presence:auto when the presence room resolves, each only when its device has a media driver, at most 64, past which no enum is advertised and the description says so (MAX_ADVERTISED_TARGETS, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:146), or says that the Media Director is not available, that no speaker can announce yet, or that no speaker that can announce has a media driver (JARVIS_MEDIA_DRIVERS) (SpeakTool.schema_overrides, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:328). memory (H314; its hook at agents/core/memory_tool.py:459, registered at agents/core/memory_tool.py:526) adds to its description that memory is switched off on this hub and every call is refused while cognition memory is off, safe mode is on or the memory module cannot be read, and otherwise changes nothing. An override changes what the model is told; each handler still checks every call. tests/test_h296_schema_overrides.py (71 cases) covers the registration check, the merge, a row as a copy, nothing to change, the hook asked on every build, seventeen malformed or failing answers falling back to the static schema, the longest description, the one warning and its re-arm after recovery, the capability-registry projection, the boundary's reshape (a moved schema, a moved description, key order that is not a move, an added tool that is not also a reshape), a real tool loop in which a target registered mid-loop is offered after the fold with the event naming it, terminal_run switched off, with no target and with targets (sorted and bounded), desktop_run's enum without touching the static schema, and speak's devices, rooms and presence, an ambiguous room, a room named like a device, a stable room order, the bound, no announce speaker, no Media Director and the registered tool picking up a new speaker at once; the review round added usable targets from default_targets and a mixed registry with no audit entry, desktop flags off, no driver, the cross-platform and Windows action sets and the once-a-minute probe, the open routes serving static schemas, a shadowed room, driverless speakers, no warning per build from a failing director, the widening refusals and the over-bound speak description; tests/test_agent_runtime_v2.py pins the two changed rows of the wired tool list. 35 mutants over the merge, the fallback, the boundary, the event and the three overrides: 33 caught (five after their cases were added: an unknown key beside a known one, pairs instead of a mapping, a tuple for `required`, a row shared with the registered schema, the room order) and two equivalent (removing the mapping check or the declared-property check still raises on the next line). Test manual: GOV-261, GOV-262. Adapted from Hermes: dynamic_schema_overrides becomes a registration hook merged over a static schema that bounds what it may change, and a changed shape is picked up at Nerva's compaction boundary rather than on every call.

The complete frozen tool-result contract is wired into real tool turns:
- the threshold precedence: pinned infinity (PINNED_THRESHOLDS: file_read, keyed on READ_TOOL, and since H315's review `todo`, whose store keeps its whole answer under 7,000 bytes), then owner override, the MCP family, tool declaration and the default threshold;
- per-result/per-turn scaling;
- bounded previews with full-file paths, sizes and hashes;
- finalized-file retention;
- centralized byte/line/line-length limits.

Since H661 the spill notice is an exact, followable call. `page_recipe` fills in `file_read(path=…, offset=0, max_bytes=…)` with the resolved path, the preview and execute_code stream fields carry it as text and as `read_with` arguments, and `file_read` pages from any offset and returns `next_offset`. The call is checked, not assumed: the store's `read_back` probe is asked about that exact path. The coordinator wires it to three checks: registry + job-toolset allowance, the turn's own offer, and FileTools reach. The spill directory is also a read-only door for exact spill names, and spill names never look like secrets. When file_read cannot page the file from this turn, the notice says the file is kept for the owner and does not name a dead call.

Other guarantees:
- Exclusive per-writer temporary files preserve concurrent stream and whole-result receipts.
- A shape-truncated stream keeps its bytes even when its annotation makes the preview longer.
- Upstream byte truncation and small-output discard still work.

Ordinary Agent and Orchestrator tool paths snapshot configured/cached backend capacity before guardrails. They forward immutable per-turn metadata without unwrapping or bypassing generation. Known capacity and resolved job bounds constrain the completion reserve, initial and later transcripts, schemas, structured tool arguments and finite result thresholds, and file_read never re-spills. Invalid metadata refuses the tool turn. Unknown capacity, including adapters without loaded metadata, keeps the documented model-family estimate, and token accounting remains heuristic.

Re-run at 55d625f: 243 cases pass across tests/test_tool_result_store.py, test_tool_loop_result_spill.py, test_environment_output_limits.py, test_code_tools.py, test_effective_tool_window.py and test_spill_paging.py.

Honest limits:
- A *streamed* spill now has a ceiling, DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES = 5,000,000, which the code calls Hermes' own figure. Past it, the file ends in one explicit '[... spill capped ...]' marker, the result reports capped/kept_bytes/file_bytes, and the stream's end survives only in the inline tail. Whole-result spills are uncapped.
- Retention has a newest-file exception.
- Interrupted captures, orphan cleanup and arbitrary storage failure are not permanent complete-output guarantees.
- This is code equivalence, not live provider/Windows containment proof. Runtime-ul oprește apelurile identice și seriile de eșecuri, aplică limite per unealtă și înlocuiește rezultatele identice reușite cu referințe.

Oferta este calculată din principal, origine/suprafață și restricțiile agentului; seturile sunt verificate prin snapshot. Catalogul Hermes de platforme excluse nu este copiat. Din H672, aceeași rezoluție (`_profiled`, prin `_resolve_offer`) se reaplică și la granița de compactare din tură, cu eșec închis: un profil care nu poate răspunde retrage toate uneltele în loc să păstreze o ofertă posibil revocată.

file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. It can also open an exact spill-file path through a read-only door when the owner's roots exclude the spill directory, and tool_result_store pins file_read to an infinite spill threshold, so reading a spill never spills again. file_search is a bounded literal content search with case_sensitive, whole_word and a file-name glob filter; it never follows symlinks, prunes secret names and reports which cap stopped it.
reviews.remaining: Paging is by bytes, not lines: file_read output is not line-numbered, there is no 1-indexed line offset/limit window, and there is no per-line length cap, so one long line can fill a page. file_search matches a literal phrase, not a regex, with a Python line scan rather than ripgrep. There is no glob file-finding mode: the glob only narrows which files' contents are searched, a pattern is required, and file_list lists a single directory. Document extraction covers .pdf and .docx only.

reviews.summary: K1, K2 și K3 sunt livrate: execute_code înregistrat pentru model, celule într-un interpreter rezident pe sesiune (K2, `llm.execute_code_sessions`, implicit oprit) și controale de operator peste el. Spill-ul stdout/stderr într-un fișier funcționează pe ambele căi. `_open_stream_spills` (agents/core/code_tools.py:480) deschide scriitorii în flux înainte de rulare. Pe K1, sinks trec prin `ToolRPCSandboxRuntime.run_python` (code_tools.py:449) până la `Sandbox.execute_python`. Pe K2, worker-ul trimite ieșirea celulei în cadre de cel mult 4096 de caractere (agents/core/session_kernels.py:358), iar `_Capture` dă fiecare cadru scriitorului (session_kernels.py:671). Gazda vede deci tot fluxul, iar memoria ei rămâne mărginită: păstrează doar capul și coada. Un flux care a încăput nu lasă fișier; rezultatul unui spill poartă calea, referința, dimensiunea și sha256. Lotul HEQ 1 (H661) a făcut din notiță apelul exact. `_spill_notice` (code_tools.py:191) scrie `file_read(path=…, offset=0, max_bytes=…)`, construit de `page_recipe` (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:145), și cere paginarea prin next_offset. `stdout_read_with` (code_tools.py:272) apare doar când turei i s-a oferit file_read și sonda `_spill_readable` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:861) confirmă că poate deschide acel fișier; altfel notița spune că fișierul e păstrat pentru owner și nu poate fi paginat din tura asta. file_read primește directorul de spill ca ușă read-only (autonomy_coordinator.py:857). Un spill în flux are acum un plafon: DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES, 5 MB (tool_result_store.py:130, cifra lui Hermes). Peste el fișierul ține primii 5 MB și se termină într-un marcaj explicit (coada fluxului rămâne doar inline), iar rezultatul poartă `stdout_spill_capped`, `stdout_kept_bytes` și `stdout_file_bytes` (code_tools.py:274). tests/test_code_tools.py paginează înapoi tot fluxul pe ambele căi (tests/test_code_tools.py:824) și verifică plafonul (tests/test_code_tools.py:877).
reviews.remaining: Rămân kernelul remote și proba pe un daemon Docker real. Modul `project|strict` al lui Hermes rămâne necopiat deliberat: postura o decide profilul de unelte (agent × suprafață × principal).

reviews.summary: The model points at the HUD, as Hermes' pointing does (the canvas is shared, so a tip shows on every user-tier viewer's HUD). agents/core/canvas.py gains two element types. A tip is a target and a one-line caption; a tour is a title and at most MAX_TOUR_STEPS (8) such steps. Both are sanitised in _sanitize: whitespace is collapsed, captions are cut to MAX_CAPTION (160), and a target must be one of POINTER_ANCHORS. Those 19 anchors are the rail's 16 modes, the message box, the Decision Inbox panel and the Console button; no single approve or reject button is one. Tips and tours keep a ring of their own in CanvasStore (_evict, agents/core/canvas.py:204): at most 20, unpinned ones gone 600 s after posting (POINTER_TTL_SECONDS), never counted against the other 200 elements, so they cannot evict a saved element. agents/core/pointer_tool.py registers canvas_point, an ungated ToolRPC tool whose schema offers exactly those anchors (register_pointer_tool, wired in agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py on the live orch.canvas). It posts through CanvasStore.post as the calling agent and refuses a call that is both or neither by name. A tip written by an untrusted turn, by any posture other than operator/owner, or by a turn whose origin cannot be read is marked untrusted. The mark is a keyword of CanvasStore.post, never read from the payload, and POST /api/canvas/post (agents/core/routers/canvas.py:52) sets it unless an admin credential sent the element. It is not in DEFAULT_GUEST_TOOLS. frontend/src/pointer.tsx mirrors POINTER_ANCHORS (a parity test reads both) and mounts PointerOverlay in app.tsx (not in demo or the floating window). The overlay polls GET /api/canvas/pointers (agents/core/routers/canvas.py:44; only live tips and tours, with the hub's clock) every 5 s and takes the newest one of the last 600 s by the hub's clock that this page has not closed (currentPointer; closes kept in sessionStorage). It finds the element carrying that data-anchor (added to the rail buttons, the composer, the decisions panel and the Console button), rings it, and draws the caption with an arrow, flipping above near the window's bottom, placed by its lower edge with the arrow on that edge and over the target's centre; it re-measures on DOM changes, and a target under another layer (Ambient, Dossier) counts as not on screen. A tour pages with Back/Next/Done and restarts at step 1 for a new tour (PointerView is keyed by the pointer id). A target not on screen is named, and an untrusted tip says so. frontend/src/artifacts.tsx lists tips and tours as text. Tests: tests/test_h309_pointer.py (60), frontend/src/test/pointer.test.tsx (16), artifacts.test.tsx (+1). The review round added the pointer ring against a flood of tips (and an untrusted turn's), the server-side trust mark on the tool and the route, the pointer feed, every real posture key and the coordinator's own wiring, re-measuring on DOM changes, the flipped bubble and its arrow, a new tour's first frame, a device clock that is off, and an anchor under another layer. 37 mutants, all killed; the review round's 33 mutants, all killed (3 by tests added after a first pass: a pinned element outlives the overflow, a pointer whose time cannot be read counts as expired, and no re-render for a DOM change that leaves the target in place). reviews.summary: The model can decide to say one short text aloud on one room's device, and can do it again. register_speak_tool (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:684) adds a ToolRPC `speak` tool with gated=True, trusted execution and its own gated intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:711, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:717). It is registered only while JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR is on (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:697), and AutonomyCoordinator wires it with the broker kernel and the governed enqueue (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:725, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1618). It reaches the same Media Director instance the media routes use, so the owner's device registry and session board apply (agents/core/routers/media_director.py:272). SpeakTool.preflight (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:388) runs at proposal and again before the approved run. It refuses text over the spoken-reply cap and code-only text (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:394, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:396). It resolves a room to that room's one announce-capable default device, so the card title and the persisted args name the speaker (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:268, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:467). It raises no card the run could only refuse: unified API off, kernel off or unbound, no media root, no speech backend, no driver for the device, or no configured presence room each refuse by name (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:415, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:410). SpeakTool.intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:445) shows the kernel the exact toolrpc.speak row it enqueues. Under the production composition (worker.kernel_gate over MediationKernelBridge, agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:648, agents/core/kernel/binding.py:108) that decision binds as the row's intake evidence, and a DENY raises no card (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:471). Only the human-accepted durable toolrpc.speak row runs. The kind is trusted (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:68) and the executor routes it to the trusted rail (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1639-1642). ToolRPC re-runs the preflight and requires the trusted execution context (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:595, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:623), and the handler refuses a row of any other kind (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:541). SpeakTool.execute (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:536) synthesizes the clip through SpokenReply on the host TTSEngine in the owner's configured voice (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:552, agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:265, agents/core/voice/tts.py:216). It writes the clip owner-only under the first media root (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:639, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:653) and presents it only through CapabilityActionAPI.perform('action:media.present') in announce mode (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:592, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:597). The facade asks the Action Kernel before the handler runs (agents/core/capability_actions.py:176) and refuses on a DENY (agents/core/capability_actions.py:183), so the kernel authorizes the effect and the tool never reaches a driver. A kernel QUEUE on that present is honoured as the accepted row and audited as speak.durably_approved (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:500, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:522). A DENY becomes kernel_denied with the kernel's reason (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:614). The Media Director treats an announce as a one-shot notice (agents/core/media_director.py:738): it never blocks the next present and costs no interrupt budget (agents/core/media_director.py:890), and whatever it cut into stays the restore point (agents/core/media_director.py:992). Because the tool is gated, tool_profiles offers it only to the owner on the operator surface (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:190, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:194), and the snapshot pins this (tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json:50, tests/test_tool_profiles.py:202). Tests cover: registration and postures (tests/test_speak_tool.py:170, tests/test_speak_tool.py:196); named preflight refusals that enqueue nothing (tests/test_speak_tool.py:271, tests/test_speak_tool.py:320); and the card naming the device (tests/test_speak_tool.py:286). With the real kernel.authorize, AutonomyPolicy and KillSwitch behind worker.kernel_gate, an approved speak is mediated and audited, and an engaged kill switch refuses both the run and the card (tests/test_speak_tool.py:520, tests/test_speak_tool.py:543, tests/test_speak_tool.py:576). Three back-to-back normal speaks on one device all play at no budget cost (tests/test_speak_tool.py:591). Speaking over music needs high urgency, pays once and keeps the music as the restore point (tests/test_speak_tool.py:608, tests/test_media_director.py:762). A kernel DENY, a missing TTS backend, a missing media root and a driverless device each refuse by name with no playback, and an engine that yields no audio refuses as tts_failed with nothing presented (tests/test_speak_tool.py:681, tests/test_speak_tool.py:469, tests/test_speak_tool.py:666, tests/test_speak_tool.py:703, tests/test_speak_tool.py:716). A row of another kind cannot speak (tests/test_speak_tool.py:753), and the clip spool stays bounded (tests/test_speak_tool.py:779). Known limits outside the accepted adaptation: an accepted speak runs at the next autonomy tick (default 60 s, floor 15 s, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:475), like every gated tool. A presence:auto card names the sentinel, because only play time knows whether the owner is in the presence room. Audible output needs an owner-wired speaker driver (the in-repo NullMediaDriver refuses and LocalFileMediaDriver is a reference), the same host seam as every media.present. The speech-backend gate (tts_installed, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:191) needs edge-tts, Kokoro, Piper with a model or the approved TTS command, with edge-tts and the command left out under voice.local_only, like the spoken-reply channel; a named TTS provider alone does not pass it. An announce of any length, including one sent through POST /api/media/present, no longer holds its device, as docs/FLAGS.md states. Hermes's tts.provider, custom command providers and tts.speed are outside the accepted adaptation, because Nerva's TTS subsystem was already ahead. Named speech compatibility review: the host TTS engine now dispatches explicit named providers through the common registry. The governed speak tool, device binding and audio publication remain unchanged; speak-tool/Media Director regressions pass. The model now writes its own long-term memory during a turn, through a tool that is atomic, guarded, recorded and undoable. `memory` (register_memory_tool, agents/core/memory_tool.py:413; registered ungated at agents/core/memory_tool.py:519 and wired at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1142) takes `operations`, each an add, a replace of the one fact `old_text` matches, or a remove of it, against target `memory` (the LivingMemory `core` ring of agent notes) or `user` (the `user_core` profile ring) (TARGETS, agents/core/memory_tool.py:61); a call with no operations reads both. The rings are reached only when cognition memory is on (_living_memory, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1136). Both rings come from one LivingMemory, so the enabled set is both or none: when memory is off the tool's offer says so through the H296 schema hook (OFF_DESCRIPTION, agents/core/memory_tool.py:459-460) and every call is refused `memory_disabled`, rather than the target enum being narrowed to an empty list. Every operation is checked on a working copy before anything is written (plan, agents/core/memory_tool.py:156): one line of at most 300 characters, the core block's own cut (MAX_FACT_CHARS, agents/core/memory_tool.py:63), with no control, format, private-use, surrogate or other invisible character (the quarantine.strip_format_chars set: variation selectors, Hangul fillers, U+034F, U+2800) (_clean_text, agents/core/memory_tool.py:112), scanned with the normalised injection scanner (_scan, agents/core/memory_tool.py:135), an old_text that matches exactly one fact, compared against the whitespace-normalised fact as the prompt shows it (_match, agents/core/memory_tool.py:144), no duplicate, and a full ring refusing an add instead of silently dropping its oldest fact; one refusal changes nothing. The rings are then written by a new compare-and-set (CoreMemory.compare_and_set, agents/core/cognition/memory.py:314) under the lock a forget clears them with, so a forget or another write that ran in between wins and nothing forgotten is written back; a second ring that fails puts the first back (_commit, agents/core/memory_tool.py:320). A compare-and-set that lost is refused `memory_changed_meanwhile`; a ring that cannot be saved is refused `memory_write_failed`. Only a clean owner turn at the operator surface writes: the resolver offers the tool to operator/owner alone, whatever llm.guest_tools says (OWNER_OPERATOR_TOOLS, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:102 and :237), the handler refuses any other posture (agents/core/memory_tool.py:449) and a turn whose origin is untrusted, an inbound message, web content or a flagged recall (agents/core/memory_tool.py:452), so an injected instruction cannot make itself permanent. Every write is committed and then recorded as an intent-log `memory.write` entry carrying the actor, the undo ref, the targets and per operation its target and action — never the text nor a hash of it, since an unsalted hash of a short fact is guessed back and the intent log survives a forget (agents/core/memory_tool.py:497). A record that cannot be made puts the rings back and records the put-back as `memory.write_reverted` (undo: `memory.undo_reverted`) with the same ref, naming exactly the rings it restored, because the intent log keeps a record whose save failed and writes it with its next one; a put-back that cannot be made (a ring moved again) is logged as an error and not recorded as one (_revert, agents/core/memory_tool.py:344; _record_put_back, agents/core/memory_tool.py:307). With no intent log nothing is written (_record, agents/core/memory_tool.py:299). The rings' previous contents are kept under the ref in a bounded undo store beside the rings (UndoStore, agents/core/memory_tool.py:228), which a forget deletes with them and which POST /api/admin/forget empties together with the live rings (clear_live_memory, agents/core/data_purge.py:429), so an undo during a forget cannot write the facts back. undo (agents/core/memory_tool.py:363) restores a write while the rings still hold what it wrote, by the same compare-and-set, recorded as `memory.undo`. The owner reads the rings and the writes undo would still restore — only those whose rings hold what they wrote (UndoStore.recent, agents/core/memory_tool.py:263) — at GET /api/memory/core (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:872) and undoes one at POST /api/memory/core/undo, admin-only (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:886). The Console's Long-Term Memory panel shows both rings and the recent writes with an undo each, and says when an undo is refused (LongTermMemoryPanel, frontend/src/panels/long-term-memory.tsx). A write that changes a ring leaves a `memory_updated` trail row with the changed targets and the actions, never text; a call that changes nothing leaves none (_record_event, agents/core/memory_tool.py:394). The prompt's core block stays frozen per session, so a write reaches the system prompt at the next session and the tool answers with both rings as they now are. tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py (72 cases) covers the plan and every refusal (malformed, injected, invisible-character, ambiguous, duplicate or over-full operations), the compare-and-set and a ring that cannot be saved, an owner write of both rings with its record and its undo, a read, an add already saved, the five postures and untrusted origins, a failing getter, memory switched off and its offer, a broken memory module, an unknown argument, no intent log or one without a record method, a record that fails and its recorded put-back, an undo whose put-back also fails claiming none, a forget between the read and the write, a forget that empties the undo store, a second ring that fails, a full ring, undo after the ring moved, undo of a replace and a remove, undo without memory, an undo that cannot be recorded, the undo store's bound and its listing of only restorable writes, the trail row, the profile offer and the routes; frontend/src/test/long-term-memory-panel.test.tsx pins the panel. 47 mutants: 33 at the build (32 caught, four after their cases were added: a raw over-long padded fact, an audit sink without record, an empty operation list, the undo listing's limit; one equivalent, rewriting a ring the call did not change) and 14 in the review round (13 caught, one after its case was added: an undo whose put-back also fails; one equivalent, widening _moved to rings it is never given). Test manual: MEM-204, MEM-205. Adapted from Hermes: its memory tool's add/replace/remove on the two injected stores, with the writes restricted to the owner's clean turns, committed by compare-and-set, recorded in Nerva's intent log without their text and undoable by the owner.

Built in #1207, then fixed after nine adversarial reviews. The model keeps a checklist of its own work and re-reads all of it on every change. The owner can read the same list, with who wrote each item and whether its text is trusted, before any approval card it leads to.

The tool. agents/core/todo_tool.py registers `todo` on the ToolRPC server, ungated (agents/core/todo_tool.py:590), with the schema {todos: [{id, content, status, parent?}], merge} (agents/core/todo_tool.py:90); the optional parent is H666's.
- Items use Hermes' four statuses: pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled. A call with todos replaces the list. With merge=true it updates items by id, changing only the fields sent, and appends new ones. A call without todos reads the list. Every call answers with the whole list and its counts.
- TodoStore.apply (agents/core/todo_tool.py:296) is bounded: at most 50 items, content of one printable line up to 200 characters, ids of 1 to 64 characters, 7,000 bytes for the whole list in the UTF-8 the tool sends it in, and at most one item in progress. A merge that only moves statuses is never refused as too long.
- Control and format characters are dropped, text is NFC, each character keeps at most three combining marks (enclosing marks included), and whitespace runs collapse. Text that renders blank (only fillers or marks) is no content; punctuation or a symbol alone is content (agents/core/todo_tool.py:136, agents/core/todo_tool.py:160-163). So what the owner reads is what was written. Two ids that are canonically equal are one id; look-alikes from another script or width stay two.
- Every refusal is named, and each comes with a sentence the model can act on: todo_too_many, todo_content_too_long, todo_content_required, todo_bad_status, todo_bad_id, todo_duplicate_id, todo_one_in_progress, todo_bad_list, todo_bad_item, todo_bad_merge, todo_no_session, todo_unknown_field (a key the schema does not have, top level or item), todo_plan_too_long and todo_shared_session. A refused call changes nothing, because a merge is built on a copy.

Whose plan it is. The coordinator passes the session, the turn's posture and whether the turn runs on the shared default session (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1099; Orchestrator.on_shared_session, agents/core/orchestrator.py:908). A turn keeps the answer it got when it resolved its session (agents/core/orchestrator.py:311), so an owner resuming another session does not let an in-flight turn in. A turn that binds no session of its own runs on that shared session, and the plan kept there is the owner's. Such turns include the HUD, the web widget (its route binds none), voice, rooms, notes, workflows, MCP ask_*, a webhook, a job, a subagent and a direct POST /api/toolrpc/call.
- On it, only an owner's turn keeps a plan. Anyone else is refused todo_shared_session and is never read the plan (agents/core/todo_tool.py:561). Neither the turn's offer nor a script's reach includes the tool for them (SESSION_SCOPED_TOOLS, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:235; agents/core/code_tools.py:362). Voice carries no identity, so even the owner's voice is a guest's turn there and keeps no plan.
- A turn on any other session keeps that session's plan, whoever it is. That covers a chat of its own and an explicit session a user token continues. Text written there by a turn that is not the owner's (a household member, a guest) is untrusted to the owner, and the owner's next turn reads it as DATA (agents/core/todo_tool.py:574).
- Otherwise it is offered like any ungated tool. An inbound guest reaches it through `llm.guest_tools`, whose default is now echo, time and todo (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:84). An install that still holds the old default (echo, time) gets the new one once, at start (agents/core/settings_db.py:561). A list the owner changed is left alone. An owner who empties it keeps guests off the tool loop entirely.
- At most 256 plans are kept in memory. The one the agent least recently wrote or read is dropped first, and an empty list frees its slot.

Where its text came from. Each item records three things: the posture of the turn that set its text (by), which turn that was, and whether it was untrusted (tainted). A turn is untrusted when it came from an inbound channel (the owner's own Telegram DM included), is not the owner's, or had already read untrusted content.
- A status set by an untrusted turn taints the item too. A clean rewrite of the text keeps the taint, in a merge or a replace alike, because the id came from whoever wrote it first (review-H315f n3). The same text again is no write, in a merge or a replace: the item keeps its writer, its turn, its taint and the plan's labels, and a status or place moved by an untrusted turn still taints it (review-H315e n2; agents/core/todo_tool.py:367). A status re-sent unchanged moves nothing in either mode.
- A call that answers with a tainted item another turn wrote says so (agents/core/todo_tool.py:587). The loop then fences the answer as DATA and raises the reading turn's taint. An item the reading turn wrote itself is its own argument, already in its transcript, and is not fenced (agents/core/todo_tool.py:472; the loop gives each run a turn token, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:369).
- So the owner's HUD turn that reads a plan written from Telegram is tainted by it. That follows the kernel's inbound policy, and the HUD tags such items "untrusted source".
- A script's own writes cannot launder text into the plan (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:37). The broker for an execute_code script's calls reads an answer as the loop reads a result (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:106): it raises the origin once a tool that declares untrusted_output answers ok, an answer says tainted, or the answer is flagged as the loop's fence flags one (an injection pattern anywhere in it, or the fence's own markers). Once the run is tainted, by the broker's own flag or by the origin an earlier read raised, nothing is scanned: the K1 loop builds a broker per request, so the origin is what carries it there (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:104; review-H315f m3). Otherwise a small answer (under 16 KiB as it encodes, counted exactly with the encoder's own string function: a newline costs two characters and a quote two, non-ASCII one, bytes as str() spells them, and the separators between items (review-H315i m1, n4; review-H315j n1, n2), a container wider than what is left is refused before it is listed, and a value JSON spells through str(), a huge int or an object, is never small) is scanned inline, where it costs microseconds, and a larger one on the scan's own single thread, never the loop's default pool, so one script's small calls do not queue behind other scripts' multi-megabyte scans (review-H315g m2). One thread, not four: the scan holds the GIL, so more gave no throughput and made the loop wait 4-5x longer at p99 (review-H315h m2, review-H315h n1). An answer too deep to encode is flagged, never raised out of the broker. It covers the whole answer in overlapping 64 KiB slices, and a slice never ends inside a word of up to 256 more characters, so a pattern's closing boundary is the answer's own (review-H315g n2); no single regex call holds the interpreter lock for a large answer, and a forked child gets a pool of its own (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:224, agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:140-148; review-H315e m2). A refusal, or a tool that raised, taints nothing. Every later call of that run then writes tainted items.
- A script's calls belong to no model turn (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:89), so what it wrote is data even to the turn that ran it.
- A session kernel that has held untrusted text taints every later cell's calls until a reset replaces its record (agents/core/session_kernels.py:829). It has held it once a cell read it, or ran in a turn that had. Each interpreter gets a mailbox directory of its own, removed with it (a reset, a crash, an idle expiry, an eviction, a failed start). The directories sit under one per manager (p<pid>-<token>), whose lock (an exclusive flock on its .lock) the manager holds while its process runs. The directory is made and locked under a temporary name and only then renamed into place, so no start ever finds it with a lock nobody holds; before each mount the manager checks that the lock it holds is still the file there, and when it is not (the file is gone or another file has the name) locks a new file there again, where its live mounts are (made and locked under a staging name, then renamed over .lock, so the name never holds a file nobody has locked: review-H315i m2), taking a new directory only when that cannot be had and giving no mount when no lock can be had at all (review-H315g m1). An owner path that is no longer a directory (ENOTDIR, a link loop) or an fd that is gone (EBADF) reads as lost too, and closing that dead fd never fails the mount (review-H315i n1, review-H315j m2); any other error reading the lock (ESTALE, EACCES) says nothing about it, so the lock is kept: giving it up let the next start remove the live mounts under it (review-H315h m1; agents/core/session_kernels.py:129, agents/core/session_kernels.py:160). With no flock (Windows) a kernel is mounted as before, and the directory ages out. A start removes an owner directory whose lock it can take and that is still the file at .lock after it took it (a file an owner relocked away from is an orphan that says nothing about it: review-H315j m1), which is a process that ended, in any pid namespace sharing the root: a pid is not asked, since the hub is PID 1 on every container start (review-H315f m1; agents/core/session_kernels.py:234, agents/core/session_kernels.py:1144). A directory with no lock (an older layout) ages out after the idle expiry, an owner directory by its newest interpreter's time, which a busy interpreter moves. A lock that cannot be asked (another user's, ENOLCK), or a directory that cannot even be looked into (another user's under umask 077), reads as alive and is kept, and one unreadable entry never stops a sweep or a start (review-H315i m3). So two processes on one data root (jarvis-hub and jarvis-runtime, or a container and the host) never delete each other's live mounts (review-H315e m1), and a file a tainted kernel wrote there never reaches the clean kernel after it.
- A run's result says tainted whenever it printed anything, read untrusted text, or ran on a kernel that held some (agents/core/code_tools.py:604), so the loop fences its output and raises the turn's taint whether the run succeeded or failed. A plan therefore cannot carry an injected instruction into a later, clean turn as the tool's own words, and the web tools' taint refusals and the kernel's queueing apply to the turn that ran the script.

The loop. It never replaces the answer with a "same as call N" stub, and never counts a todo call against a per-tool cap (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:125). The cap setting's label says so (agents/core/settings_db.py:195), and a start gives a stored row the current label (agents/core/settings_db.py:547).
- The repeat detector keys a todo call on its arguments and on the plan the model last saw (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1596, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1644). A read after the plan changed is the tool doing its job. The same call with nothing changed in between is stopped like any other repeat: the third is refused and the fourth ends the turn. A failed call leaves the plan the model saw unchanged. A script (execute_code) may have changed the plan behind the model's back. So each one that made tool calls, or did not finish cleanly (a crashed one reports none), opens its own revision, and the next read after it is a new call, however many scripts ran (review-H315e M1; agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1615). The revision is applied after the reads of the script's own step, which answered the plan from before it (review-H315f m2). A script that ran cleanly and called nothing changed nothing, so the repeat stop holds across it (review-H315f n2), as does one execute_code refused before any script ran (switched off, no sandbox, not isolated, no authority) or a session-kernel call refused before its cell (e-stop, expired, denied, no kernel, an empty or overlong cell; review-H315h n2), but not an unconfirmed teardown, which also ends a cell that ran; a handler that raised may have raised after its script ran, and opens a revision. A K2 cell's call count is the host's, never the count the kernel reports, and 0 when the cell had no mailbox (review-H315g n1, review-H315h n2).
- The answer is never cut: 7,000 bytes fits the smallest per-result budget, and the tool is pinned whole even after the turn's allowance is spent (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:100).
- The description asks the model to mark the item it starts in_progress, and completed when it is done.

The owner's view:
- A write leaves a todo_updated event in the tool trail (agents/core/todo_tool.py:484). It carries the session, the statuses, the position of the item in progress and the total. It never carries the text or the ids, which are free text too. A read or a refusal leaves no event.
- GET /sessions/todo and GET /sessions/{id}/todo (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:145, agents/core/routers/sessions.py:154) are user-guarded and no-store; an invalid id is a 400.
- Each item carries its by and tainted, never its turn. The recent list puts first the plan the agent most recently wrote or read. A plan's labels (when, which agent, whose turn) move only when its list changes.
- `nerva todo [SESSION]` (agents/cli/nerva.py:1731) prints the plans with [ ] [>] [x] [-] marks and each item's tags (agents/cli/nerva.py:1689): guest turn, household turn, background turn, untrusted source. A bad session id exits 2 before any request. A malformed reply, a non-object item included, exits 1.
- The Decision Inbox shows the plans with open work under the decisions (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx:65, mounted at frontend/src/gap.tsx:3374). It shows at most three plans of eight items each, how long ago each plan was written, and every tag of each item (frontend/src/panels/plans.tsx:39). A failed read is shown as failed, with its reason, not as "no plans".
- The capability registry calls the tool reversible session state with a compensating rollback: a later call can write back what a call replaced, and the tool keeps no copy of it (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:287).
- A forget clears every plan (agents/core/data_purge.py:561) and lists todo_plans in live_stores_cleared. A turn already running when the purge starts can still write its plan afterwards, just as it still saves its reply.

Adapted: Hermes classifies todo as mutating in its loop guardrails. Here it is ungated because it writes only its own session's list: the shared session's list only for the owner's turns, and every item's origin is kept and shown.
