Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability. Collateral active-image review (2026-10-03, a30603e0): the only drifted evidence for this row is agents/core/orchestrator.py. Its diff changes complete_selected_image_turn for explicitly reviewed browser image turns; this row's cited implementation lines and feature path are unchanged. The focused active-image and route regressions pass, and this existing code-equivalent verdict is preserved.

The supporting pieces exist, but the feature does not. Signed inbound webhooks exist: compute_signature is HMAC-SHA256 (agents/core/webhooks.py:107), and WebhookStore.verify_signature compares it in constant time (agents/core/webhooks.py:667), verified by tests/test_h16_4_signed_triggers.py. A lifecycle event catalogue now exists too: ExtensionEventBus builds allowlisted payloads from FIELDS for command.completed, session.started, session.ended and tool.completed (agents/core/extensions/events.py:51-56, agents/core/extensions/manifest.py:16). The orchestrator, the command runner and the tool-event log emit those events. Their only subscribers, however, are signed and consented extensions that run in a container with --network none (agents/core/extensions/runtime.py:32). Outbound HTTP goes only to chat channels (agents/core/channels/webhook_channels.py). There is no outbound lifecycle webhook: no registry of external subscriber URLs, no signed JSON POST of lifecycle events, no bounded retry or redirect policy, no estop or budget silencing of the feed, and no redaction hop on its payloads. Speech prerequisite compatibility review: the exact new voice-command registry entry adds no webhook egress or delivery capability; existing partial status and delivery gaps are unchanged.
reviews.remaining: The whole accepted delivery path is missing: (1) an admin-managed registry of outbound subscribers (URL, secret, event filter) with an operator entry point (admin route plus a `nerva` CLI verb or HUD control). (2) A delivery worker subscribed to the same event catalogue as ExtensionEventBus that POSTs the allowlisted JSON payload with an HMAC signature header from compute_signature. (3) Bounded retries with backoff and an explicit no-follow redirect policy. (4) Egress through the plugin.egress kernel mediation (agents/core/kernel/registry.py:45) and an estop check, so a kill-switch or budget stop silences the feed. (5) Payloads passed through the redaction engine before they leave the box. The reaction/vibe detector is excluded by the rationale.

reviews.summary: Every log record, from every process, now goes through two filters: H495's shape scanner and a catalogue of credential-bearing names plus the Romanian identifiers. agents/core/log_catalogue.py (outside security/, additive) is a scanner over the names that make a value a credential whatever it looks like: query parameters (QUERY_PARAMS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:54: access_token, refresh_token, id_token, token, auth, api_key, client_secret, secret, password, signature/sig, the AWS presign parameters, session, jwt), masked at any length up to the next separator; body, form and structured-log keys (SECRET_KEYS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:62), quoted in JSON or a Python repr, assigned with a quoted value, or unquoted when the value is six characters or more; the Authorization header after any scheme (Bearer, Basic, Token, Digest, ApiKey, HMAC…), or without one when the value is twelve characters or more and carries a digit, so `Authorization: denied` stays; the credential headers X-Api-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-Access-Token, X-Goog-Api-Key, X-User-Token, X-Admin-Token, Api-Key and X-Webhook-Token (SECRET_HEADERS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:68); and the whole value of Cookie and Set-Cookie. It also runs PIIScanner's own CNP and IBAN patterns (agents/core/security/scanner.py:287-288) with their checksum validators, and an IBAN written in spaced groups of four; the other PII patterns stay out (an e-mail or phone number in a log is often the point of the line; card and SSN shapes carry no checksum). A bare `key` parameter (settings routes use it for a setting's name) and a bare `token:` key (token counts) are not in the catalogue. The rules are in _rules (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:91); a value already masked is never re-masked, so a JWT the first filter named keeps its name. CatalogueScanner (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:126) offers redact, scan and the _compiled rows H495's prefilter is built from, and CatalogueRedactionFilter (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:161) runs it through an unchanged SecretRedactionFilter (agents/core/security/log_redaction.py:230): the arguments uvicorn's AccessFormatter unpacks are kept, a secret split between the format string and an argument masks the argument whole and is named after the finding that holds, tracebacks and stack info are masked, a failing scanner drops the record's content to [redaction-unavailable], and the one JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION switch, snapshotted at import, turns both filters off. It wraps rather than subclasses, so H495's installer, which skips a handler already carrying a SecretRedactionFilter, never mistakes it for its own. install_catalogue_redaction_everywhere (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:220) covers the root handlers and every logger's own (uvicorn's detached ones included), idempotently, and counts and names a handler that refuses the filter. core.log's _install_redaction (agents/core/log.py:69) installs it right after the H495 filter, so setup_logging (agents/core/log.py:108) gives every handler both, in that order; install_redaction (agents/core/log.py:102) is the same for a process that configures its own logging. The two entry points that called a bare basicConfig and wrote every record unredacted now call it: the headless coordinator (configure_logging, scripts/coordinator.py:145) and the MCP stdio bridge (configure_logging, scripts/nerva_mcp_stdio.py:149, still stderr only, since stdout is its protocol channel). Neither takes setup_logging's rotating file handler, which a second process would rotate under the hub (critic note 32). The H145 log reader runs the catalogue on every line it serves (agents/core/log_tail.py:167), for lines written before it or by a process it did not cover. The test isolation fixture strips the catalogue filter with the H495 one (tests/conftest.py:271). The H495 module's docstring (agents/core/security/, a protected path) still names the coordinator and the MCP bridge as uncovered and says no PII pass runs; it describes that module alone. tests/test_h410_log_catalogue.py (52 cases) covers the five probes the audit found unmasked and every other name in the catalogue, ordinary text that must stay (a failed authorization, a setting key, an exit code, a token count, a 13-digit order number, an IBAN-shaped string that fails its checksum, a short value), the exact line kept around a mask, CNP and IBAN compact and spaced, an access-log record keeping its five arguments, a traceback, a JWT keeping the first filter's name, a straddling IBAN, the switch, a failing scanner, both filters on every handler once and in order, a refusing handler counted and named, both entry points with a fresh root (the bridge writing nothing to stdout), and the log reader. 31 mutants: 30 killed (4 by cases added after a first pass) and 1 equivalent that removed a redundant `(?:proxy-)?` prefix (`\b` holds after the hyphen). Test manual: SEC-216.

A session is named from its first message, the way Hermes names one, in two stages. agents/core/session_titles.py holds the rules. instant_title (agents/core/session_titles.py:82) takes the first user message, normalises it (NFKC; control, format, private-use and unassigned characters dropped; one line with spaces collapsed) and cuts it at a word boundary to 60 characters with an ellipsis. A slash command (as CommandRegistry.parse reads one, so `/etc/hosts …` is a title), blank text or a run of separators alone is not a title, so the next real message names the session. The orchestrator calls _title_session (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2871) right after the user turn is stored, on both chat paths (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2013, agents/core/orchestrator.py:2215), with the turn's channel. An internal channel (notes, builder, eval, arena, workflow, room, internal) never titles, and neither does an inbound turn from anyone but the owner on the shared session (a widget visitor, a webhook, MCP). The title and the model's input are the owner's own words: /chat and /chat/stream bind req.message through session_titles.bind_own_words (agents/web.py:1246), so the session-notes block a route composes around them never reaches the title or the title model. It does nothing when the owner's switch memory.session_titles is off (agents/core/settings_db.py:249, on by default) or the session already has a title. Otherwise it writes the first-words title at once and queues one upgrade. handle_input and handle_input_stream start the queued upgrade only after the turn's reply is final (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1993, agents/core/orchestrator.py:2196), as Hermes titles after the first response, so the title call never competes with the answer for the local model. The upgrade (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2930) goes through model_title (agents/core/session_titles.py:140), which hands the message (bounded to 2,000 characters) to the model as a JSON string under a system prompt that says to name the conversation, not answer it or follow it. clean_model_title (agents/core/session_titles.py:92) accepts exactly one line of 1 to 10 words and at most 60 characters. It strips Title:/Titlu: labels, quotes and markdown until the text stops changing (a label inside quotes goes too), removes trailing punctuation, and rejects URLs and instruction-, preamble- or refusal-shaped text in English and Romanian; anything else keeps the first-words title. The call is strict-local (_session_titler, agents/core/orchestrator.py:2941): it uses LLMRouter.local_backend only, never a cloud backend, initially at temperature 0 and 24 tokens, with /no_think for Qwen3. It refuses under a job model pin. With no local backend there is simply no upgrade. The title lives in the session row's metadata as title and title_source (first_words or model). CheckpointManager.set_session_title (agents/core/checkpoint.py:294) is a compare-and-set: a first title creates a missing row, but a replacing write (the model's upgrade) never does, so a session deleted between the reply and the upgrade stays deleted; it keeps the row's other metadata, and writes only when there is no title or the current one's source is in replace. The model's name therefore replaces only a first-words title, never a newer one, and never a legacy title with no source. session_title (agents/core/checkpoint.py:278) reads it, with unreadable metadata counting as no title. title_fields (agents/core/session_titles.py:128) gives every list the same view. GET /sessions returns title and title_source on each row (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:41). The /sessions command prints the title after the id and start time to the owner (an admin principal) only; a widget visitor, a paired guest or a non-owner web user sees the id and start time (agents/core/commands.py:220). `nerva sessions` prints it after the start time (cmd_sessions, agents/cli/nerva.py:1657). The HUD SESSIONS card shows the title, with the id's first 8 characters and the full id on hover (frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:93). The mobile resume list prefers the title over the summary and the id (mobile/src/components/SessionsModal.tsx:80). tests/test_h413_session_titles.py (131 cases) covers the first-words cut and cleaning, the model-answer filter (8 accepted, 20 rejected shapes), the JSON hand-over, the input bound and the failure paths. It also covers the compare-and-set store (missing row, kept metadata, no overwrite, legacy title, unreadable metadata, a closed or failing store), and the orchestrator hook (switch, titled session, slash command, no titler, unusable answer, lost write, newer title, no loop, and deferral inside a turn). The strict-local titler cases are temperature, tokens, default model, Qwen3, the job pin, no router, and a real HybridRouter with only a cloud backend. Two real golden turns (plain and stream) show that the turn's own call runs alone, the title arrives after it, and the second turn is not re-titled. The route, the /sessions command and the settings row are covered as well. The review round added the /sessions title for the owner only, a deleted session never re-created by the upgrade, no title from an internal channel or a non-owner's inbound turn on the shared session, the owner's own words through both real routes, `nerva sessions` with and without a title (test_nerva_cli.py), the Romanian refusals and preambles, command-shaped text that is not a command, a run of separators, and nested labels and quotes. frontend/src/test/sessions-title.test.tsx covers the HUD card. There are 67 mutants: 65 killed and 2 equivalent (the no-connection guard, which the except already covers; a source compare that no caller can tell apart). IterationBudget (agents/core/iteration_budget.py) is still only a counter. AgentToolRuntime._run_loop consumes one unit per model turn (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:537). On exhaustion it emits tool_loop_exhausted and returns a fixed safety-limit string (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:746-754). Since the audit, Hermes absorption 5c has coordinated two of the scattered clocks. orchestrator._agent_call_timeout (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3718) picks a flat or reasoning ceiling per agent and hands it to the agent as wall_seconds (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4264). run() then clamps it into the tool-loop deadline (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:398-402), which tests/test_reasoning_timeout.py pins. There is still no single bounded-execution primitive or timeout resolver. The tool-call timeout (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1292), the sandbox file-RPC deadline (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:318), the per-attempt retry timeout (agents/core/resilience.py:28) and the per-plugin deadline (agents/core/plugin_gatherer.py:151) are each site-local. There is no 80%-spent wrap-up nudge and no iteration-budget exhaustion protocol. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. reviews.remaining: (1) One deadline/budget primitive that extends iteration_budget.py, as the 2026-08-28 delta doc chose: a wall-clock deadline plus an iteration count, remaining and fraction-spent readings, and a timeout resolver per call kind. The orchestrator turn, the tool loop, tool calls, ToolRPC and plugin gathering derive their timeouts from it instead of their own constants. (2) An 80%-spent wrap-up nudge, injected once into the tool-loop transcript, asking the model to deliver from what it has. (3) The exhaustion protocol: tell the model exactly once, grant one final tool-less call, and force a summary from the transcript if that call yields no text, instead of returning the fixed safety-limit string. (4) Deadline and budget stops reported through the H396 exit-reason vocabulary.

reviews.summary:
The per-item cascade algorithm exists. DecayMemory.forget() (agents/core/memory/decay.py:112) walks _dependents() (:109) and removes the item plus its transitive dependents. It is exposed as POST /api/memory/decay/forget (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:575), which two HUD controls call: KgPanel's forget box (frontend/src/gap.tsx:205) and MemoryHygienePanel's per-row ✕ (frontend/src/gap.tsx:307).

The whole-store forget is governed. POST /api/admin/forget (agents/core/routers/backup.py:99) is admin-guarded and requires {"confirm":"FORGET"} (:115). It checks the data.purge contract, backs up first by default and reports not_erased when something survived.

The accepted adaptation for the per-item path is not built. The route crosses only user_guard and calls d.forget directly (memory_kg.py:589). There is no memory.forget kind in ACTION_REGISTRY; agents/core/kernel/registry.py:73 still lists /decay/forget as out of kernel scope. There is also no cascade preview, no approval card and no audit row: one click deletes irreversibly.

The cascade also retracts less than its name says. The ids it deletes are the decay tracker's activation entries: LivingMemory turn ids registered at agents/core/orchestrator.py:3598, and ambient situation ids. The route never calls LivingMemory.forget() (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:194) or any vector/KG delete. The LivingMemory record with the same id survives a per-item forget. Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability. House-presence collateral review (2026-10-02, 39a82964): the shared HUD diff adds only the explicit HousePanel explanation request, display state and button; this row's claimed UI and producer branches are outside that change. Its prior verdict is preserved after source-diff inspection, 66 focused backend/API checks, 1,874 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build. The full backend run first stopped at the expected stale Hermes generated report, with no behavior failure before that point.
reviews.remaining: Add a memory.forget kind at the irreversible tier. POST /api/memory/decay/forget must return the transitive dependent list as a preview and queue an approval card carrying that list instead of deleting on the spot. The cascade runs only from the approved task and writes an audit row with the removed ids. KgPanel and MemoryHygienePanel show the preview and the pending state. The executed cascade must also retract the records the ids name (at least LivingMemory.forget for turn ids), not only the decay tracker's activation entries.

reviews.summary: Compaction now checkpoints the turns it is about to discard, and fails closed when a required checkpoint does not land. ContextCompressor takes a checkpoint callable (agents/core/context_compressor.py:321). compress() awaits it with exactly the turns the summary replaces (the evicted middle, all of it even when a prior summary covers part) and the whole transcript, before the summary is built (agents/core/context_compressor.py:579-586). The orchestrator builds that callable in _precompress_checkpoint (agents/core/orchestrator.py:392) and hands it to the compressor on every compacting history build (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3999). It calls precompress.run_checkpoint (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:107) over the registered providers, or the default transcript archive. The hook is versioned. A provider declares checkpoint_api_version, and only one at CHECKPOINT_API_VERSION 2 or above counts (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:63). The optional keyword arguments (evidence_messages, require_checkpoint, checkpoint_api_version, session_id) are passed only when the provider's signature accepts them (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:69). A synchronous provider runs off the event loop, and providers get copies, so they cannot change the transcript. The shipped provider, TranscriptArchive (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:174), keeps a raw per-session JSONL copy of the evicted turns. It appends each evicted turn once, by a hash of speaker, time and content, to a file whose name is a hash of the session, under the data folder (compaction_archive), owner-only (0600 in a 0700 folder); the append is flushed and fsynced before on_pre_compress returns (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:208). It remembers what it holds across restarts, skips damaged lines (including a line cut inside a multi-byte character), starts the next record on a new line after a torn last line, and writes images as [image]. It is not an extraction. Nothing mines those turns into episodes, consolidation or LivingMemory, and nothing checks that per-turn LivingMemory extraction landed for them. Recall and session_search never read the archive (TranscriptArchive.read() has no production caller), and no production code registers precompress_providers. The archive runs only while memory.persist is on (agents/core/orchestrator.py:404), and a chat's backup-first delete (H218, which the H262 sweep uses) removes it with the chat, while the sweep prunes orphaned archives (purge_orphan_compaction_archives, agents/core/retention.py:100). memory.compression_checkpoint_required (agents/core/settings_db.py:255, off by default; only a literal true turns it on) makes it fail closed. A failing checkpoint provider, or no checkpoint provider landing ("No active memory provider completed pre-compress checkpoint API v2"), raises CheckpointAborted. The compressor then summarises nothing. Old images are still dropped, with an images-tier lineage row when any were (agents/core/context_compressor.py:509-521). The orchestrator refuses the turn with the compaction refusal reply only when the image-dropped transcript does not fit the model's window (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4043). With the setting off, a failing provider is logged and compaction proceeds. A checkpoint that landed new turns, or had a provider fail, writes memory.precompress_checkpoint to the signed intent log with an archived count (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:148). One that landed nothing new, the steady state once over budget, writes nothing. Every abort writes memory.precompress_abort. The rows carry turn counts, provider names and the reason, never the turns, and every audit write runs off the event loop. tests/test_h427_precompress_checkpoint.py (54 cases) covers the contract (version, names, signature sniffing, copies, a synchronous provider, nothing to evict), the not-required and required paths (failing provider, old provider, no provider, a missing or non-callable hook, a failing audit), and the archive (write once, fsync, restart, damaged lines, hashed names, images and structured content, turn identity, default location). It also covers the compressor (exactly the evicted turns before the summary, a prior summary, abort, under budget, compact fail-closed) and the orchestrator (archived and audited, required failure keeps the transcript with no clock commit, not required proceeds, no provider, refusal exactly at the window, a literal-true switch, the default archive, the settings row, no turn text in the audit). The original build had 51 mutants: 49 killed and 2 equivalent (a non-callable hook fails with the same TypeError either way; re-reading the archive file each time is only slower). The review round added the retention prune, the memory.persist gate, the steady-state audit, the torn-line and multi-byte handling and the file modes, each with a case that fails without it. Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability.
reviews.remaining: A memory-extraction checkpoint provider registered on the orchestrator, writing to episodes, consolidation or LivingMemory, or an interlock that verifies the per-turn LivingMemory record landed for each evicted turn; plus a read path from recall or session_search into the archive. This needs an owner decision: Episodes E3.0 never copies source payloads automatically, and LivingMemory turn records are content-free digests.

reviews.summary: Getting back into a conversation now comes with a free recap, rendered locally from the stored turns and never by a model, on resume, as /recap in every channel and in the HUD. render_recap (agents/core/memory/recap.py:80) groups a session's turns into exchanges (an owner turn and the replies that follow it), keeps the last 10 by default (DEFAULT_EXCHANGES, agents/core/memory/recap.py:24; at most 50, MAX_EXCHANGES, agents/core/memory/recap.py:25), and puts each turn on one line of plain text, whitespace folded, control and bidi characters removed and cut to 280 characters with an ellipsis (_clean, agents/core/memory/recap.py:35; the raw text is cut to four times the limit before cleaning, so a huge stored turn costs no more than a short one). A reply's tools collapse to a count and their distinct names, "[3 tool calls: web_search, web_fetch]" (tool_line, agents/core/memory/recap.py:57), names only, never arguments or results, and an owner turn never shows one. The answer carries the exchanges as data and the same recap as text lines (● you / ◆ the agent) with "the last n of m exchanges" when some are left out. The tools had to be recorded first: turns persisted only role, content, agent, time and tokens. The orchestrator opens a per-turn collection when an owner turn arrives (turn_tools.begin, agents/core/memory/turn_tools.py:23; agents/core/orchestrator.py:2014 and :2216), the agent's tool-event sink notes each finished call's tool (turn_tools.note, agents/core/memory/turn_tools.py:30, from the sink's record, agents/core/agent.py:903) while still landing every event in the trail, and the reply that closes the turn is stored with the names (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3622) on Turn.tools (Turn, agents/core/memory/conversation.py:38; a stored value that is not a list of names reads as none, _tool_names, agents/core/memory/conversation.py:67), persisted, reloaded at start, on resume and on an explicit session load (session_continuation._load_locked, agents/core/session_continuation.py:290), carried in a continuation's immutable seed (seed_json, agents/core/session_continuation.py:89), and absent from a turn that called none. The collection is a context variable, so concurrent turns in other sessions never mix, and a tool loop run through asyncio.to_thread still lands in its own turn. POST /sessions/resume answers with "recap" beside the last 20 raw turns it always returned (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:197), rendered from the whole stored session. /recap [n] (_recap, agents/core/commands.py:375; registered at agents/core/commands.py:408) answers in any admitted channel from that channel's own session (a chat's session is its own, pinned by the channel handler); on the owner's shared session (a widget visitor, an agent-target webhook, an MCP caller, or any channel with memory.cross_channel_sessions on) it answers only the owner and refuses anyone else before reading a turn, with n exchanges (at most 50; anything else, a non-ASCII digit included, is the default ten), and leaves out its own /recap line, recognised by the command parser in any case (/Recap, /recap@bot). The HUD's Sessions panel (SessionsPanel, frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:51) now shows the recap after a resume (RecapView, frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:30; toolLine, frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx:23) as text, never markup, names a refused resume and drops the old recap then, and says "resumed <id>" when a hub sends none. tests/test_h441_session_recap.py (22 cases) covers the renderer (last exchanges and the count, tool lines, one bounded line, odd input, no model), the collection (terminal events only, names only, concurrent turns and a worker thread, no turn open, a caller's copy), the agent's sink, the turn's tools stored and reloaded at start and on resume, the manager passing them down, the resume route's recap with no model call, /recap in a guest's channel with a count, with nothing and with no memory, /help listing it, and the orchestrator storing a turn's tools; the review round added /recap refused to a widget visitor, a webhook and MCP through the real routes while the owner still gets it, a guest on the shared session refused before anything is read, the /recap line left out in any case, a non-ASCII digit, a huge turn cut before cleaning, and tools kept through prepare_session and a continued session's seed, resume and next turn; frontend/src/test/sessions-recap.test.tsx (3) covers the panel. 28 mutants (24 Python, 4 HUD), all caught, three after their cases were added (an owner turn with tools, a caller's copy of the list, the reload on resume). file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). local_docs and agents/core/ingestion/ remain the bulk-ingestion path into memory.
reviews.remaining: The part this row says is worth copying is missing. A scanned (image-only) PDF extracts to empty or near-empty text, and file_read returns that as a normal successful read, with no coverage warning naming the page ranges that yielded no text. No size ceiling applies to a document: the whole file is parsed again on every page request, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned, where Hermes refuses documents over 50 MB. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. The wider format matrix (.ipynb, .xlsx, legacy Office, OpenDocument, .rtf, .epub) and Markdown conversion are not built; the row's rationale does not ask for them.

reviews.summary: Plain-words scheduling now covers the four families Hermes accepts that the job store did not. It also no longer turns a one-shot said in words into a daily job. (1) One-shots. nl_schedule.parse_schedule (agents/core/autonomy/nl_schedule.py:196) takes a now and a zone and answers a one-shot as {ok, at (UTC ISO), description} (_parse_one_shot, :120). It accepts a delay: in 30m, in 1h30m, in 2 hours and 5 minutes, in an hour, peste 2 ore, în 10 minute, peste 2 zile (_duration, :85). It accepts an ISO timestamp (2026-10-01 09:00, anchored to the zone, or with Z / ±HH:MM kept). And it accepts a day word with a time (tomorrow at 9, mâine la 9, today at 18:00, azi la 18, once at 9am, o dată la 9, the next 9 o'clock). A one-shot must be at least one minute ahead and within a year (MAX_ONE_SHOT_AHEAD, :29, _one_shot, :101); a passed time, a date without a time, an impossible date, a bad time, and a delay with anything else after it ("in 2 hours at 9") are refused by name. So 2026-10-01 09:00, tomorrow at 9 and once at 9am are no longer armed as the daily cron 0 9 * * *; a bare time with no day word still means daily, as documented. resolve_schedule (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:271) stores a one-shot in the cron column as @at <UTC ISO> (ONE_SHOT_PREFIX, :229; is_one_shot, run_at, :233-238). The store anchors times said in words to the scheduler's zone, which the runner binds (_schedule_zone, :990; :1126). schedule_trigger (:249) gives a DateTrigger for it. register arms a date job (:1184). tick fires it in the minute it falls in (:1279). slot_timing gives its one slot and none after (:1347). A one-shot runs once. Job.runnable is false after one attempt (:131). reserve_attempt refuses a second (:1004). _fire_once reserves the one run before any executor, script jobs included, and records a later firing as skipped: "one-shot already ran" (:1495). register_all does not re-arm a spent one-shot. Giving it a new time re-arms it (_reset_attempts, :981), and a rename does not. It stays out of H687's first run even when first_run is asked for (first_run_policy and first_run_decision answer "one-shot", :563, :589), so it never spends its only run early. The confirmation names its time (arm_confirmation, :614), and as_dict carries one_shot and run_at (:157). /remind in 30m | … works, and its usage says so. (2) Compact intervals and bare durations: every 2h, every 30m, 2h, 30m, la fiecare 2 ore (_COMPACT, _interval, nl_schedule.py:174-177). 120 minutes becomes every 2 hours. An interval a cron cannot keep (every 45 minutes fired at :00 and :45; 7h, 48h) is refused with the divisors to use. (3) Repeat normaliser: normalize_repeat (jobs.py:410) maps forever/unlimited/always/∞/mereu/la nesfârșit to unlimited, once/1x/x1/o dată to 1, twice/de două ori to 2, and Nx/N times/de N ori/N to N (1-10000). Anything else is refused. validate_options applies it, so options.repeat takes the words on every surface. (4) The HUD jobs panel shows a one-shot by its time (once at …, the viewer's clock) instead of @at, and shows a spent one as done (onceAt, frontend/src/panels/jobs.tsx:30, :62). Tests: tests/test_h450_schedule_words.py (fixed now and Europe/Bucharest zone; store and runner with a fake scheduler; the fallback ticker; script jobs), frontend jobs.test.tsx and jobs-first-run.test.ts. 62 mutants, all caught after fourteen cases were added. One survivor was a real bug: "in 2 hours at 9" read as a daily 9 o'clock; it is now refused.

reviews.summary: Scheduled self-contained Python scripts cross the existing local terminal approval path with exact source in argv. no_agent returns bounded stdout directly; script-as-context fences output and binds an inbound origin before asking the model. Empty/whitespace stdout skips both model and delivery. Pending approval, repeat reservations, deletion/e-stop races, bounded fair reconciliation, interrupted delivery and retained history survive restart in tests. Successful script stdout can suppress model and delivery with a final JSON boolean wakeAgent:false, except when transport output is truncated. Model replies support bounded-position [SILENT] and whole-response silence markers before truncation; suppression is successful history without notification spend. Bounded approved script monitors hash complete raw stdout on the trusted host, compare scrubbed snapshots and atomically persist each baseline before the model runs. Unchanged observations skip model/delivery; source/config generations prevent stale baseline updates and stale delivery. Invalid UTF-8, incomplete or oversized observations leave the baseline intact. URL monitors now use the existing signed enforced task queue for one exact plugin.egress GET per human-approved hop, with fresh approval for redirects. Public-address DNS validation/IP pinning, live post-DNS kernel/e-stop checks, one-use dispatch claims, credential screening and scrub-before-persistence are verified with real queue/worker/executor tests. Only complete final successful UTF-8 identity responses within 256 KiB advance the baseline. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported.
reviews.remaining: Unattended execution is not granted: each script firing and URL hop needs fresh approval, with live enforced signed mediation required for URL authoring. URL scope is credential-free public ASCII HTTP(S), at most five redirects, 30 seconds per hop and 256 KiB uncompressed UTF-8; private, credentialed, compressed or invalid-text observations are unsupported. Script snapshots remain bounded by the terminal cap (at most 50,000 bytes). Monitor mode excludes no_agent and treats wake JSON literally. Model workdir/tool contexts and monitor/URL authoring UI remain unsupported; script-only workdir and script/no_agent UI are implemented. No live production egress, scheduler/channel or full production-kernel proof.

reviews.summary:
H456 re-read against 55d625f. The 2026-09-07 evidence ("no per-item toolset allowlist") is stale, but the row stays partial.

The enabled_toolsets half of the contract is shipped and well built. agents/core/job_toolsets.py holds:
- an immutable CATALOG (:7-11: basic/files/terminal);
- a strict `validate()` that refuses unknown, non-list or duplicate ids (:14-21);
- `resolve()`, which refuses a group whose members are not all registered ('enabled_toolsets contains an unavailable toolset', :30-37);
- `toolset_scope()` (:63-79), whose nested frame is `parent.names.intersection(names)` (:72) with a shared _Lifetime, so a closed parent raises 'job toolset scope expired' (:66-67) instead of falling back to defaults. Intersect-never-union is enforced.

It is enforced at three boundaries, not one:
- the offering boundary (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:226,234 `allowed = allows(name) and _posture_allows(...)`, narrowed again by agents.yaml patterns at :239-240);
- the runtime filter before and after the profile (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:285-294), re-applied at the in-turn compaction boundary by `_resolve_offer` (H672);
- RPC intake, ahead of preflight and handler (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:446-448, reason `job_toolset_not_allowed`).

Store boundary: agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:435 lists the option, :438-442 validates it and refuses it with `no_agent`, validate_action:310-311 refuses it on non-`ask` actions, and create and edit both re-resolve it (:1324, :1393). Fire time: jobs.py:1601-1603 `with toolset_scope(self._toolset_names(job.options)), selection_scope(job.options)`. Doctor reports the catalog, each job's `toolset_upper_bound` and a `toolsets_unavailable` problem (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_health.py:51-55, :113). Reachable from the CLI (`--toolsets default|none|<ids>`, agents/cli/nerva.py:264,275,1475-1481) and the HUD (frontend/src/panels/job-builder.tsx:35-49). PATCH /api/jobs/{id} refuses an unavailable toolset with 422 (tests/test_job_toolsets.py:327-328).

Hermes' two removal rules are met structurally. Every register_tool on the production server was enumerated: agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:518-835 (image_generate, H313's `speak` at :531-547, desktop_run, terminal_run, desktop_plan, operator_plan, osint_enrich, echo, time) and :839-928 (session_search, file_*, web_search/web_extract, search_memory, execute_code), plus H315's `todo`, registered after the tool profile (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:972), which writes only its session's own checklist (on the owner's shared session, only an owner's turn keeps one). None creates a job, and no `schedule.create` kernel capability exists. None is a messaging/clarify tool that needs a live human. The new `speak` announces into a room, but it is registered only with JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR on and is gated (ask-tier card, trusted execution only from an owner-accepted row), so it is never offered off the owner posture.

Verified green at 55d625f: 27 cases in tests/test_job_toolsets.py and 28 in tests/test_job_model_pins.py. The HUD cases in frontend/src/panels/job-toolsets.test.tsx were not re-run in this pass.

What keeps the row open is the contract's second half: a job cannot pin reasoning effort.
- Selection carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25).
- validate_options rejects any unknown option (jobs.py:435), so the pin cannot be stored; neither jobs.py nor job_selection.py mentions reasoning at 55d625f.
- _ask never enters `reasoning_scope`, so every scheduled run inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read in agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:339,352,390,419-420.
- The closed-lifetime transport machinery already exists (agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-72), but only the live chat path enters it (agents/web.py:1256, :1321).

Secondary gap: the bound can be expressed over only 8 of the ~18 tools the server can register. A job that needs web_search, execute_code or search_memory must run unbounded on the default net, a residual that docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-job-toolsets.md:44 names itself. H513 fixture review: synthetic local backends now declare their actual LM Studio profile and loopback endpoint; original behavior assertions remain unchanged.
reviews.remaining:
(1) The per-job reasoning-effort pin (Hermes' `.cron-reasoning`, rolled into this row) is not implemented:
- `Selection` carries only model/provider (agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:21-25), and `validate_pins` (:35-43) never sees an effort.
- `validate_options` rejects any option outside the known ten (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:435), so the pin cannot reach the store.
- `JobRunner._ask` (jobs.py:1601-1603) enters `toolset_scope` + `selection_scope` but never `reasoning_scope`. A job therefore always inherits the global `llm.reasoning_effort` / `reasoning_effort_overrides` read at agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:339, :352, :390, :419-420.

The transport half already exists and is clamped: agents/core/llm/request_context.py:44-72; agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:83-88 with per-model overrides; agents/core/llm/gemini.py:135; agents/core/llm/xai.py:73; agents/core/llm/provider_request.py:46 and :54. Only the live chat path enters it (agents/web.py:1256, :1321). Work owed:
- accept `reasoning` in validate_pins/validate_options against LADDER;
- enter `reasoning_scope(...)` in `_ask` beside the other two scopes;
- expose it on the CLI/HUD/doctor like the model and provider pins;
- test it in tests/test_job_model_pins.py.

(2) The bound can be expressed over only 8 of the ~19 tools the production server can register. CATALOG (agents/core/job_toolsets.py:7-11) covers echo/time, the five file tools and terminal_run. These belong to no group: web_search, web_extract, search_memory, session_search, execute_code, desktop_plan, desktop_run, operator_plan, osint_enrich, image_generate and (with the Media Director on) speak, registered at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:518-835 and :839-928. A job that needs any of them must leave `enabled_toolsets` unset and run on the full default net. H315's todo is not among them: a job runs on the owner's shared session, where only an owner's turn keeps a plan, so no job uses it, with or without a group. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-15-job-toolsets.md:44 names this residual itself ("does not claim ... arbitrary plugin/delegation/code-runner groups"), and doctor reports the upper bound, not the effective offers.

(3) Minor: Hermes' middle precedence tier has no equivalent. That tier is a per-platform `cron` tools config that sets defaults for every scheduled job. Here, only the per-job list, the internal posture (`llm.internal_actuation`) and the agent's agents.yaml `tools:` patterns narrow an unattended run.

reviews.summary: The pieces around the feature exist, but nothing binds a standing instruction to a conversation. HeartbeatScheduler (agents/core/heartbeat.py:180) schedules per-agent routines from HEARTBEAT.md or agents.yaml, with MIN_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL 3600 s (agents/core/heartbeat.py:52) and 15–30 s jitter. Since H506 it also refuses a HEARTBEAT front-matter that its injection scan flags. Admin routes /heartbeat/{agent_id}/start|stop|run (agents/core/routers/heartbeat.py:27) and the HUD HeartbeatPanel drive it. Owner-armed jobs accept plain-words schedules, can be paused, resumed and deleted, and include an `ask` action that sends a prompt to an agent. That prompt goes through a one-shot Orchestrator.process call on channel 'job' (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1609), and the reply goes to the owner's channel, not into the originating chat's history. The only chat slash commands are /help, /status, /sessions, /pause, /stop, /resume, /jobs, /remind and /voice. CommandContext (agents/core/commands.py:50) carries no explicit session id, but its principal is a Principal with channel and chat (agents/core/commands.py:37-46), and ctx.orch.session_id already resolves to the bound channel session because the channel handler sets the active session before handle_input dispatches a command. Turns are serialized per session: Orchestrator.turn_lease (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1711) keeps a per-session asyncio.Lock table with a re-entrant held set. But nothing records an idle boundary or consults that lease before firing a heartbeat. Existing heartbeat and jobs tests pass (tests/test_heartbeat.py, tests/test_heartbeat_actions.py, tests/test_owner_jobs.py). Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. reviews.summary:
A work run can now be parked on real async work instead of being poked. Three barrier kinds hold a run's next tick without spending anything (BARRIER_KINDS, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:141):
- a registered process until it exits;
- a trigger until it fires: a queued task of this run reaching a terminal status, or an enabled webhook being called;
- a wall-clock time.

The barrier is a `barrier` column on the run (the _v2 migration, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:423). It also adds `run_events` (set and clear audit) and `run_procs` (processes registered for a run). Setting and clearing a barrier are events, not steps: they cost no budget, stay outside the fingerprint, and never change a verification result (set_barrier, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1457; clear_barrier_if, a compare-and-clear, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1532). A move to stopping or any terminal status clears the barrier in the same write, so stop always wins.

Validation, probes and stale clearing live in RunBarriers (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:280):
- request (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:314) refuses a spent or unparkable run and bounds every barrier. Its cap (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:355) is the earliest of its own wait (at most MAX_BARRIER_SECONDS, 7 days, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:74), the run's deadline, and the time the run's budget has left. Since H464b that is the EFFECTIVE budget (now + budget_state's seconds_left), so H487's proven approval-wait credit counts at barriers too; before, a run with credited wait time was refused `no_time_left` or capped early by the whole credit.
- A pid must first be registered for this run through the Python-only register_process (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:562). That refuses pid ≤ 1, the hub, its parent and dead processes, and allows at most 16 per run. It captures the process's start token, pid namespace and boot id.
- A trigger must be a task of this run or an existing, enabled webhook.
- active (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:589) is the one check the scheduler and the supervisor share. It clears the barrier on the next check if any of these hold:
  - the cap or the clock has passed;
  - the process has exited, its pid was reused, it is in another namespace, or it cannot be proven (default_pid_probe, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:229);
  - the trigger fired or vanished;
  - the probe raised.

  A check that fails ticks the run normally. So no barrier outlives its cap or the run's budget, and none can wedge the loop.

While a barrier holds, nothing is spent:
- ScheduleRuntime.due answers `waiting` after the budget check, so a spent budget still wins (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:222). Only the sweep clears a spent run's barrier.
- CompanySupervisor.tick returns `waiting` before planning or judging, so there is no step, no budget use and no judge call (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:271, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:302).

A planner sets a barrier with Action(kind="wait", barrier=…). _park (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:366) never enqueues:
- A wait with nothing to wait on is free, and so is one whose check failed for a moment (NOTHING_TO_WAIT_ON, WAIT_CHECK_FAILED, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:98, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:108).
- That is capped at MAX_FREE_WAIT_REFUSALS (3) in a row. After that, each is a failed plan step with one fixed reason, so the streak rule ends a planner that keeps asking (_free_refusal, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:447).
- The planner is told the last refusal.
- A malformed or forbidden wait is a failed plan step at once.

The judge sees the run's live background processes (RunBarriers.background, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:677) and can answer a third verdict, wait (WorkJudge.wait_probe, agents/core/autonomy/work_judge.py:124). That parks the run before grading, at most MAX_JUDGE_WAITS (3) times per run (_judge_parks, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:612). At settlement a `wait` answer withholds the pass.

H464b made one park path real in the shipped product. With JARVIS_COMPANY_MODE set at boot:
- The runtime builds from the orchestrator's real attribute names (_queue_reader, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:185; _governed_intake, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:199). Before, it looked only for `task_queue`/`queue` and `govern_enqueue`, which the orchestrator never had, so build_company_runtime returned None and no `company-mode-sweep` job was ever registered. Now the explicit arguments win, then `task_queue`, `queue`, `autonomy_queue` for the reader and `govern_enqueue`, then `autonomy.govern_enqueue` for the intake, each tested for presence rather than truthiness and only when callable. The same queue reader turns H487's approval-wait credit on in production, bound on the shared ledger only once the runtime actually builds (H464c; agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:414), and backs PendingRequests and RunBarriers (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:437). Every step still goes through the governed intake.
- The approved checklist is read back from the goal's own approval task (_read_back, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:228). The task named in the run's `approved_by` (`task:<id>:<decider>`) is re-read from the durable queue and re-minted through approve_from_task, which re-checks that a human accepted that very task. The goal is then bound to the run (the same approval and decider, title, deadline and budget, and, since H464c, the fingerprint pinned on the run when it opened) and given the run's own goal_id so the judge's goal-identity rule holds. What happens when it does not bind is H464c's M5 below. An explicit `goals=` still wins.
- When the checklist is done but a task this run queued was approved and is still executing, the hub parks the run on it before any grader is asked (_hub_parks, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:584, called first in _grade, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:556). RunBarriers.park_in_flight (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:382) picks the oldest such task (IN_FLIGHT_TASK_STATUSES = approved, running; agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:117) and sets a `task:<id>` trigger with source `hub`, a fixed reason "task N is still running" and the default 6 h wait, capped by the deadline and the budget left, each less a grading margin since H464c. The park is an event, not a step: it spends wall-clock time, never a step or a verdict. The hub waits on a task at most once per run (WorkRunLedger.barrier_sets, read from the append-only audit, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1605), so a capped wait is never renewed and a restart buys nothing. It never parks on a task the owner let the run go from, whoever set that wait, so the owner's "stop waiting" sticks against the hub too (the model-source rule itself is unchanged). A task that finished between the two reads is skipped. Any refusal or error (budget, no time left, barrier limit, a queue that cannot be read) falls through to grading exactly as before, and the tick never raises. The run resumes on the first sweep after the task is terminal.

H464c (the second review of H464b: six MINOR and two NIT findings) binds the chain to what the owner approved:
- M1: open_run pins the approved goal's fingerprint on the run (ApprovedGoal.approved_fingerprint, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:317; a nullable `approved_fingerprint` column, the _v5 migration, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:467), covered by the row's own fingerprint once set (identity, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:279). The read-back compares the re-minted goal with that pin, so an edit of the approval task after the run opened (a stale, recomputed or dropped fingerprint) drives nothing, and a run with no pin (opened before it existed) drives nothing.
- M2: a `task:<id>:…` approval opens ONE run, ever (open_run, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:782; _run_for_approval_locked, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:872). The check and the insert are one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that rolls back on any failure, so a commit that raised leaves no row for the retry's commit to write. A retried goal.approve gets the run the first attempt opened (same pin), reported with that run's goal id, or `approval_already_used`. This closes known gap 1 of the Codex review handoff (2026-09-28).
- M3 (sized exactly in H464d): the hub's park stops a grading margin short of the deadline and of the time the budget has left (the reserve in request, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:354). The margin is the floor the runtime passes, at least a minute (grade_margin, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:136; GRADE_MARGIN_SECONDS, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:133): the time from a tick to the next sweep on which the scheduler's per-run interval lets the run be due again (next_due_after_tick, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:115: the first multiple of the sweep cadence at or past the 300 s interval) plus a minute (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:434) — 360 s at the default 300 s cadence and at 60 s, 420 s at 120 s, 460 s at 200 s, 1,260 s at 1,200 s. It is never a share of the budget, and the same margin applies before a deadline. With nothing to spare past the margin the hub does not park and the run is graded now. Planner and judge waits are unchanged.
- M4: safe mode leaves company mode out: schedule_company_mode builds nothing and registers no sweep (a new `company_mode` safe-mode layer), and a sweep that finds safe mode on does nothing (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:134).
- M5: the read-back says why it has no goal (_ReadBack, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:216). "Cannot tell right now" (no reader, a read that raised) HOLDS the run: the planner returns Hold(stop=False) (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:164) and the tick is `idle` "held: …" with no step, no park and no grade (_hold, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:408). Provably not bound (not opened from a goal card, no pin, a task that is gone, a policy decision, an edit, another run's goal, a binding check that raised, and since H464d anything re-minting the task raises) STOPS the run with `plan not bound to its approval: <reason>` as its stop reason, the way a stuck run is stopped, so the brief shows it. Neither is ever graded as a finished checklist.
- M6: a plan row's queued task kind must be inside the goal's scope (task_kind_in_scope, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:91: a scope kind, or under a whole one then a dot, `research.collect` under `research` and, since H464d, `file.write.append` under `file.write`). GoalDraft refuses the card (`plan_task_out_of_scope`, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:234), the planner clamp refuses the proposal (agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:184), and an approved row the checklist has to refuse stops the run with the reason (_walk, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:336; since H464d recorded as `approved row refused by scope: …`, not as unbound).
- N1: snapshot, and so every report route, is read-only (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1776). budget_state(settle=False) (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:960) reads only the tasks an open approval wait is on (_open_wait_tasks, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:537), writes nothing and opens no transaction; the tick path still settles. For 50 runs × 25 steps (the reviewer's perf_r5.py): 1,250 queue reads and 0.054 s before, 0 reads and 0.020 s after.
- N2: the reader is bound on the shared ledger only when the runtime builds.

H464d (the third review, of H464c: one MAJOR, four MINOR, four NIT, and two MINOR the closure found in older code) makes the grading margin exact and the rest of the chain honest:
- A1/B2/F1: the margin above. The 10 % share graded an 8 h run with 40 minutes left over its still-running task (the reviewer's e10: graded at minute 440 on `running`; now at minute 455 on `done`), and a sweep-only floor left a run parked into a window where the scheduler's own interval never let it be ticked again at cadences under 300 s. A run is now graded before its time runs out at 60, 120, 200, 300 and 1,200 s cadences through the real due() gate, whose per-run interval allows 1 s (at most 1 %) of timer jitter (due_slack, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:110; agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:249), so a sweep a moment early does not push grading a whole sweep past the margin.
- B1: anything re-minting the approved goal raises is provable (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:276): a budget edited to zero steps stops the run with `plan not bound to its approval: invalid_max_steps` (WorkRunError keeps its code; anything else is `approved_goal_invalid`) instead of failing every tick. Only the read is transient.
- B3: the reconciler records each still-open approval wait on every sweep (_observe_wait, agents/core/autonomy/pending_requests.py:307, a settling budget read), so an ask the owner edited before approving is credited up to the last sweep that saw it open whether or not the HUD polled (the reviewer's e1/e1b, ported with a sweep a minute: 180 s credit and 30 s used both ways, 0 and 210 s before). The report routes stay read-only.
- B4: a hold writes one `hold.start` run event per hold (note_hold, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1631, deduplicated while the same hold is open), the first tick that can plan again writes `hold.end` (end_hold, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1648; _end_hold, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:436), the snapshot carries the open hold (hold_state, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1659), and the brief lists the run as held with a plain reason (_held, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:139). A run the scheduler skips as budget_spent is settled through the supervisor's settle_spent (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:520; _settle, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:269), which re-reads the budget, so a read that failed settles nothing; before, a spent run was never ticked and stayed open for ever.
- F2/F3 (older code): a checklist row whose step failed (the intake raised or returned no task, or the task vanished) is not done; it is tried again on a later sweep, at most MAX_ROW_ATTEMPTS (3, agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:77) attempts, then the run stops with `approved row kept failing: <row> (3 attempts)`. A failed read of the run's own steps is a refusal (_run_steps, agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:300) the runtime holds on, instead of reading "nothing done" and asking for row 1 again.
- M05/M43 test gaps closed; C4 stop wording; C2 an upgrade note (docs/UPGRADE.md) and plain stop reasons in the brief (_hub_stop, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:150): an in-flight run from before the pin stops once, as "opened before this version tied a run to the plan you approved; approve the goal again to run it"; C3, a rollback reading pinned runs as tampered, is documented there.

The owner can always let a run go:
- POST /api/company/runs/{run_id}/barrier/clear (user-guarded, agents/core/routers/company.py:179);
- `nerva company clear-wait`;
- the Company room's two-step "stop waiting".

The clear reports what it did, or what a newer barrier now waits on. A wait the owner cleared is not set again on the same target by the planner or the judge, nor by the hub's in-flight park. The brief and the HUD say "parked — waiting on …" only while the barrier is in force (_in_force, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:112).

A barrier only suppresses work. It grants nothing:
- no approval;
- no resume of a blocked run;
- no budget extension;
- no path around the governed intake.

tests/test_h464d_company_run_grading.py (19 test functions, 32 cases) ports the third review's repros (e1/e1b, e3, e4, e7, e8, e9, e10, intake_fail, steps_fail) and closes the M05 and M43 gaps; tests/test_h464c_company_run_binding.py (28 test functions) ports the reviewer's repros for M1–M6, N1 and N2, and pins the two survivors of the H464b pass that no test covered (a binding check that raises is a mismatch; an empty park answer is not a park). tests/test_h464_run_barriers.py (60 test functions) covers the barrier layer: bounds and caps (including the credited-budget cap), pid registration and probes (reuse, namespace, unprovable, EPERM), triggers, stale clearing, compare-and-clear, owner-clear stickiness, the migration, barrier_sets and park_in_flight (oldest in-flight task, undecided/missing/terminal ignored, once per task, the owner's clear, reader failures, a task finishing between reads, other refusals passed on, restart). tests/test_company_runtime.py (38) adds a real-shaped orchestrator (only `autonomy_queue` and `autonomy.govern_enqueue`), the checklist read back from a real TaskQueue approval task with eleven binding refusals (each case pins the draft's fingerprint, so it is refused by the check it names), and the AC11 end-to-end chain with no injected callables: approve a one-row goal, the step queues and blocks, the owner accepts the step's task, the next sweep parks the run on it (source hub), a RUNNING task keeps it `waiting` at no step, DONE clears it as `fired` and the run goes idle ("no grader is wired"); the owner's clear of the hub park sticks. tests/test_company_supervisor.py (55) pins the park before grading, with no grader wired, before the judge's wait probe, no re-park after the cap or the owner's clear, and fall-through to grading on every refusal or error. Barrier cases also live in test_schedule_runtime, test_work_run_ledger, test_work_judge, test_company_report, test_company_routes, test_company_planner and test_nerva_cli.

reviews.remaining:
Not reachable in production yet:
- **No process producer (owner decision 1; blocked on H302).** Nothing in the hub starts run-owned background work and registers its pid: register_process has no caller outside tests. The best first producer is `terminal_run` with `background: true` on the local-host transport. It needs WorkRunLedger.run_for_task; a spawn with start_new_session, bounded log files and a held proc.wait() that records the exit code; a lifetime cap and killpg on cap, ESTOP or stop; a reaper for stopped runs; schema, approval-card and parity updates; and a KillMode in deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service (today a restart kills the child and the barrier clears as `exited`, indistinguishable from success). The owner must say whether the task/hook trigger is an accepted adaptation of Hermes's pid/session barrier, or whether a pid wait must be reachable for "equivalent".
- **Pid waits are unusable on macOS/BSD.** There is no start token there, so every pid wait is refused `pid_unprovable`. The fix belongs in exec_cache.py (ctypes libproc proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)) or in a producer-held Popen handle, and needs macOS hardware or a macOS CI runner to verify.
- **The judge's `wait` verdict and planner waits are not reachable in production (owner decision 2).** WorkJudge.wait_probe needs a model rubric, and the shipped runtime passes no rubric, model planner or graders. Wiring one needs the owner's choice of local model and provider under H513 (auxiliary_request_scope, strict-local, security.data_training_ack) plus opt-in settings forced off in safe mode. Before any model planner, the rest of the intake arguments must be clamped: since H464c the task's kind is scope-checked as well as Action.kind, but the task's agent, title and payload still reach govern_enqueue unchanged.
- **No graders are wired in production.** After the hub park clears, a run idles until its budget ends. Deterministic verifier and judge adapters belong to the company-mode grading work; they must reuse an existing verdict, because _grade has no try/except and a judge that raises after the verifier recorded leaves `verdict_already_recorded` / `tick_failed` on every later sweep.

Deferred:
- Wake-on-fire: a parked run resumes at the next scheduled sweep.
- A `job:<id>` trigger.
- A process output-pattern trigger (needs the process producer).
- An owner-set wait like Hermes's `/goal wait` (owner decision 3): a clock or own-task wait only, never an owner-typed pid.
- Waiting between checklist steps: the checklist still advances when a step's task is approved, not when it finishes.
- A judge-sourced wait reserves no grading margin (only the hub's park does since H464c), so a judge wait that runs to the end of the budget still leaves the run ungraded. It is reachable only with a judge wait probe (owner decision 2).
- The grading margin bounds one run's way back to a sweep, not a queue: with several runs due at once (max_concurrent 1), a parked run can lose the sweep's one slot after its cap.
- A blocked run whose budget runs out is not settled (H464d settles only runs the sweep skips as budget_spent; a blocked one is skipped as blocked and its resume is refused once the owner answers), so it stays blocked on the record.
- The HUD's live wait credit for an open ask runs to now; if the owner then edits the ask, the durable credit falls back to the last sweep that saw it open (at most one sweep's worth).
- An owner stop of a working run is never closed out: request_stop moves it to `stopping` and settles only a second stop (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1382-1384), while ScheduleRuntime.due skips a `stopping` run (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:227-228), so the supervisor that would settle it is never ticked and the run reads `stopping` until the owner stops it again (reproduced on 03643762).

Needs network: re-checking Hermes's goal-wait behaviour at the pinned commit 59b2aeef (hermes_cli/goals.py was not among the inspected upstream sources). Review residuals after round 3 (latent or bounded): a dropped grading sweep is not absorbed by the margin; a transient queue read during the per-sweep wait observation cuts approval-wait credit; a hold open when a run stops is never ended; an expired ask would be re-asked; the upgrade note's 're-approve' advice needs a new card; four test gaps (docs/handoff/2026-09-28-handover/h464-round3-brief.md).

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 and fixed after six adversarial reviews: review-H465 (one major, seven minors, seven nits), review-H465b (three minors, six nits: a per-turn pass could still run beside /refine and borrow its label, a cut-off review read as nothing, and four mutants were unpinned) and review-H465c (three minors, six nits: a per-turn review cut off by the token cap was refunded, so a model that always truncates reviewed every turn; the settings the replies named could not be set; four survivors) and review-H465d (two minors, seven nits: a day of cut-offs made /refine name the wrong setting, seven real survivors, and a GA4 private key the CLI printed unmasked) and review-H465e (two minors, seven nits: the cut-off refusal on a day of mostly real reviews, nine real survivors, a budget read outside its bounds, a secret echoed by nerva config set, a pass in flight at midnight counted on the next day, a burst of turns past the cadence) and review-H465f (seven nits: a /refine refund keyed on the wrong day, a burst given too few passes, a later bracket closing an unclosed error, a fraction below one read as reviews off). All are fixed. Hermes' /refine [focus] forks the background memory and skill review against a snapshot of the conversation, so the live session is untouched. It refuses while a turn is in flight and reports the new or updated memories and skills back into the chat. Nerva's review engine is the per-turn BackgroundReviewer (strict-local, budgeted); it now also runs on demand.

The command:
- /refine [focus] is an owner command (agents/core/commands.py:350, registered at agents/core/commands.py:416). It answers from any channel's owner, and a guest is refused like any owner command.
- The focus is one line of at most 200 characters.
- It replies with what the review kept, one line per action (profile or core memory updated, corrections recorded, skill patch proposed, new skill quarantined, facts found but not kept because living memory is off). A skill change is said to wait in the Decision Inbox, and a new skill in the pending skills list.
- Every non-run is named: a review already running, the daily budget spent, no local model answering (reviews never leave the machine), a model that spent its whole answer thinking (review_cut_off), a review cut off or malformed (review_unparsed, which names learning.review_max_tokens), reviews switched off (a daily budget of 0, reviews_off), the review outlasting its bound, nothing to review, no reviewer. An empty reply, a cut one, or a JSON object carrying none of the review's keys ({} or {"error": …}) is unparsed; only an object that says it found nothing reads as nothing worth keeping. A reply that parses as a review is the model's answer, whatever it opens with or mentions; only a reply that does not parse and is the local degraded message or opens with a bracketed [… error …] closed on its own line by its own bracket is a backend failure; an unclosed "[Note: … error", or one a later [1] or link would close, is prose (review-H465e nit 7, review-H465f nit 3).
- A local backend that is configured but down answers with a degraded string rather than raising. That is no review: it is reported as no local model and costs no budget (review-H465 M-1). A cut-off or malformed /refine costs none either; a per-turn pass cut off the same way does spend its unit, since the model ran to its cap, so the daily budget still bounds local GPU use when a model always truncates, and it is logged at INFO once a day, naming learning.review_max_tokens as the cause of a thinking cut-off and as a possible one of a malformed answer; a /refine cut-off does not use that line up. When such cut-offs are at least half of the day's spent units, /refine answers daily_budget_cut_off and says that, if they were cut off, the token cap is what to raise rather than the budget; one cut-off among real reviews is plain daily_budget (review-H465e m-1). A pass still waiting on the model at midnight refunds or counts against the day it spent its unit on, never the next (review-H465e nit 4), and GET /api/cognition/learning counts cut_offs_today. The unit is spent in run() after the budget is checked again there, so a burst of passes that all saw budget left in should_run cannot pass it; the cadence is checked there again too, so a burst of turns cannot pass it either (review-H465e nit 6), and a pass uses up only the turns that admitted it, so a burst gets the passes the same turns one at a time would (review-H465f nit 2) (_cut_off, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:513).
- It runs whether or not the per-turn learning loop (cognition.review_enabled) is on: the owner asked, as Hermes' manual /refine does.

Orchestrator.refine (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3476):
- It reads a snapshot of the session's history and never writes to it.
- The snapshot is conversation_snapshot (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:98): the newest turns whole and contiguous, each cut at 2,000 characters, up to 12,000 characters in all. Slash commands and the hub's replies to them are left out, so a chat of commands only has nothing to review. This replaces the per-turn review's last-6-turns, 300-character window for this path.
- In flight, as it really behaves: every path that dispatches /refine holds the session's turn lease first. A /refine sent while another turn runs therefore waits for that turn (up to the lease's 180-second bound) and then reviews the conversation as it stands; it is not refused (review-H465 m-1 corrected the earlier claim). The review itself is bounded at 150 seconds (REFINE_TIMEOUT_S), below that wait, so the chat is busy for at most that long.
- A direct caller holding no lease while another turn does is refused turn_in_flight: the lock is locked and the key is not among this context's held leases (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3496). No new in-flight set was added (critic note 1).
- A review's result is the reviewer's last_result, which GET /api/cognition/learning shows (reviewer.status()); a refusal does not overwrite it. Each action is logged.

The learning loop's knobs are declared settings (category learning, agents/core/settings_db.py:312): review_max_tokens (512, 1–32768), review_daily_budget (20, 0–1000), review_cadence (every_turn, every_n_turns, idle_gap), review_every_n (3), review_idle_gap_s (90) and review_max_facts (3), with the defaults the code already used, bounded in _LEARNING_INT_BOUNDS (agents/core/settings_db.py:759). The admin settings API, the HUD and nerva config set can change them; nerva config get shows a number named …max_tokens as the number it is, not masked as a credential, and masks every key the settings store encrypts (the GA4 service-account JSON among them), and nerva config set echoes such a value masked too (review-H465e nit 3). A model id is masked only under a hinted name: llm.default_model shows as typed. Every knob reads within its declared bounds whatever the stored row (a row from before the bounds, restored or hand-edited, reads as the default), the review's model call's token cap included (bounded_learning_int, agents/core/settings_db.py:774). A declared 0 for review_max_facts or review_idle_gap_s is honoured, not read as unset; corrections have a cap of their own (3), so a review_max_facts of 0 keeps no facts, still records corrections, and /refine says what it found but did not keep (_number, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:293).

BackgroundReviewer.run_on_demand (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:335):
- It skips the cadence gate but spends the daily budget, rolling over at midnight, and refunds it when no review was had (a model down, a cut-off answer, a timeout, a cancellation), on the day the pass spent it (review-H465f nit 1). A budget of 0 means no reviews and /refine says so (reviews_off); 2.5 reads as 2, and a value that is not a number or lies outside 0–1000 (text, infinity, a boolean, a hand-edited -3, a fraction below one) is logged once and 20 used (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:268). A per-turn pass that does not run leaves a DEBUG line naming why. It keeps the strict-local model, and is bounded at REFINE_TIMEOUT_S (150 s, below the lease's 180-second wait); no setting raises it.
- It neither resets nor delays the per-turn cadence. It runs one at a time and never beside a per-turn review: a /refine while a per-turn pass runs is refused busy, and a per-turn pass that would start while /refine runs is skipped, not deferred. The exclusion is taken in run() itself (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:394), so a per-turn pass spawned before the /refine, still waiting on the memory lock, is refused on_demand when it enters. A cancelled review leaves no busy flag.
- Its proposals, approval cards and new skills are labelled refine, not background_review; the label is passed down per pass, never kept on the instance. An injection-flagged correction is not recorded (on both paths). Facts found while living memory is off are counted after the injection scan, and said only to the owner who asked.
- run gains a focus slot in REVIEW_PROMPT ("Focus for this review: …", absent when there is none, so the per-turn prompt is byte-identical) and a context bound, which this path sets to the snapshot's.

Tests: tests/test_h465_refine.py (35 cases), tests/test_h465c_refine_review.py (9, the second review), tests/test_h465d_refine_review.py (31, the third review), tests/test_h465e_refine_review.py (37, the fourth review), tests/test_h465f_refine_review.py (34, the fifth review), tests/test_h465g_refine_review.py (18, the sixth review), tests/test_nerva_cli.py (a token budget shown unmasked), and tests/test_slash_commands.py pins the command in the owner's list. They cover:
- the focus slot and its bound;
- cadence skipped while the budget is spent, and the day's rollover;
- one review at a time, and facts written;
- the snapshot's bound, order, cutting and junk;
- a whole snapshot reaching the prompt;
- the reviewer receiving this session's snapshot while the session stays unchanged;
- busy while another turn holds the lease, and not busy inside the command's own lease;
- the empty and unavailable cases;
- the owner-only command and its report, each named refusal, and /help;
- the review's cases: a degraded reply is no review and costs no budget; the timeout; a cancelled review; mutual exclusion and the cadence kept; facts found with living memory off; an injected correction; the refine label; commands left out and contiguity; a chat of commands only; a refusal keeping the last result; the focus cut and where a new skill waits; a guest told /refine is the owner's.

reviews.remaining:
The completion subscription itself is missing:
- No way to subscribe a chat (platform, chat_id, optional thread) to a work item's terminal events (task done/failed, work run succeeded/failed/exhausted/stopped, mission done/failed).
- No delivery modes notify, notify+wake or wake. In wake mode the agent should be woken in that chat to read the full context and answer in its own voice, spending interrupt budget and respecting is_night_window.

- No auto-subscribe of the creating chat.
