The logging half of the row, and only that half. `agents/core/security/log_redaction.py` adds `SecretRedactionFilter`, a `logging.Filter` that runs every record's message and its `args` through `SecretScanner.redact` before a handler can write it. The enable flag is snapshotted at import, so an agent-authored mid-session write to `JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION` cannot turn it off — Hermes's `_REDACT_ENABLED` rule, ported deliberately. A cheap length/substring pre-check runs before any regex (≈8.75 µs per clean record, ~1.9× faster than the full scan; the builder's report said 17.22 µs and ~2.1×, which did not reproduce and is corrected here). `setup_logging()` installs it. **Two majors found by an independent review and fixed before landing:** the module's own docstring tripped the AUD-14 raw-env-read ratchet — the prose contained a literal `os.environ[...]` subscript and the ratchet greps file text line by line, so `tests/test_o26_p2_env_config.py` was RED in the delivered tree; and `install_log_redaction()` walked only the root logger's handlers, while `uvicorn` and `uvicorn.access` set `propagate=False` and own theirs, so the production HTTP server's own access and error logs — the ones that carry an `Authorization` header — were structurally unreachable. `install_log_redaction_everywhere()` now covers every handler owned by any logger in `logging.Logger.manager`, and a test drives a real uvicorn `dictConfig` and asserts a key in an access line is masked. Three minors fixed with it: the length floor was defeated by an extra pattern whose NAME collided with a built-in (it now matches by regex SHAPE, one-to-one, and fails closed on any mismatch); an ordinary `%`-format bug was being swallowed into a bare `[redaction-unavailable]` instead of logging's loud diagnostic (now `[log-format-error]` with the message, args and exception, all scanned first); and the test fixture destroyed an ambient `JARVIS_LOG_FILE` for the rest of the session. 47 tests, each fix red-proofed by neutering it. **Follow-up in the same PR:** the blocking bandit gate flagged both swallowed exceptions as NEW findings. Only the filter's last-ditch blank was suppressed (`# nosec B110`, with its reason); `_cover`'s per-handler swallow became a counted, warned coverage figure and `_managed_loggers`' registry-walk failure became a warning, closing the gap this row disclosed. 52 tests at landing. **#1177 (2026-09-19) closed a log-integrity hole inside this same control, re-assessed here rather than refreshed:** the in-place path used to give up and flatten the record to `msg`/`()` whenever a secret straddled the boundary between the format string and an argument ("correctness beats shape"), and flattening is exactly what DELETES a uvicorn access line — `AccessFormatter` unpacks five `record.args`, raises on an empty tuple, and `Handler.handleError` swallows it. `password_assignment`'s `\s*[=:]\s*` jumps the space uvicorn's `'%s - "%s %s HTTP/%s" %d'` puts between the request path and `HTTP/`, so `/login?pwd=` is inert on its own — 11 characters, so the 10-char floor does not even apply; `password_assignment` needs at least six unquoted (four quoted) non-space characters after the separator and the bare argument has none — and a match once rendered: any unauthenticated client could erase its own access-log entry by appending `?pwd=` to a path. `SecretRedactionFilter._mask_joined_args` now replaces whole arguments — one at a time first, then cumulatively for a secret assembled from several — the cumulative pass can also mask an innocent argument that sits between two culprits (`"%s HTTP/%s and %s HTTP/%s"` with two `?pwd=` paths loses the `1.1` between them): over-redaction, never a leak, and the arity still holds — — until the re-rendered line is scanner-clean, keeping the tuple's arity, putting an argument back when its conversion refuses the mask (uvicorn's `%d` status code stays an int), and naming the mask after the pattern the scanner reports, `[REDACTED:straddling_secret]` when it cannot. Flattening survives only for a straddle no masking can clean, i.e. the secret sits in the format string itself (`pwd=%s`). Seven tests were added — four of them through uvicorn's real `dictConfig` plus `setup_logging()`, asserting the access line for `/login?pwd=`, `/admin?password=`, `/x?passwd:` and `/z?api_key="12345678` survives with the straddling text gone (three are `password_assignment` straddles; `/z?api_key="12345678` is `generic_api_key` matching `api_key="12345678 HTTP/1.1"`, the access line's own closing quote completing the quoted value) and the client, verb and status kept — and the earlier straddle test was inverted to assert `args == ("[REDACTED:anthropic_key]",)` instead of `()`. `agents/core/log.py` did not change and still installs the filter from `setup_logging()`. `tests/test_log_redaction.py` collects 64 tests, all green on 2026-09-19. Nothing in #1177 touches the other six paths the row names; the still-owed list below stands.
reviews.remaining: This is one of the row's seven paths. Hermes applies `redact.py` to logs, verbose output, tool output, approval prompts, gateway messages, transcripts and memory; this slice covers LOGS. Still owed, and the rationale calls them the part that matters most: the hash-chained audit DB (a `cat .env` from `terminal_run` still writes a live credential into an append-only log that by design cannot be edited), the decision-inbox approval card the owner reads on a phone, task payloads, terminal output, and the observability exports — which Hermes scrubs unconditionally with no knob, returning `[redaction-unavailable]` rather than raw text. Also absent: the second mask mode (a syntactically INVALID `«redacted:ghp_…»` sentinel for file reads, so an agent cannot write a masked-but-plausible key back and silently kill the credential), `code_file=True` sparing source constants, `_mask_control_split_tokens()` for tokens smuggled across ANSI/zero-width characters, and the shared `.env` basename list. The two silent-degradation paths named at review are now CLOSED, after the SAST gate forced the question: a handler whose `addFilter` fails is counted and published through `uncovered_handler_count()` and a warning naming how many handlers are writing unredacted, and a `loggerDict` walk that raises warns that coverage fell back to root-only. The one silent swallow left is the filter's own last-ditch blank (`# nosec B110`), where a `logging.Filter` that raises would take down the caller's log call and the scanner has already failed. `install_log_redaction()` remains exported although the `everywhere` variant is what production uses. **A later slice's full-suite run surfaced one more thing about this control, recorded here rather than fixed:** the scanner's `high_entropy_secret` pattern matches an ordinary filesystem path. Under `-n auto --dist loadfile` a warning naming a pytest tmp file arrived as `truncated: [REDACTED:high_entropy_secret].md`, which is what a real operator would see when a log line names a file with a long random-looking segment — a debuggability cost the module docstring already warns about in general terms, now with a concrete case. Separately, `setup_logging()` installs the filter on every handler of every logger and nothing took it back off, so every later test on the same xdist worker ran under a live redactor. The installer is PRODUCTION code, not the tests: `agents/run.py` calls `setup_logging()` at module level, so importing it installs the filter during pytest COLLECTION — before any fixture runs — and eight test files import it; `agents/web.py` calls it from the FastAPI lifespan, so any test that drives the app installs it again; five test files call it directly on top of that. There is no list of leaking files to fix. The cleanup therefore lives in `tests/conftest.py` as an autouse fixture that strips unconditionally BEFORE each test as well as after — a snapshot-and-restore fixture, which is what the two neighbouring isolation fixtures do and what this was first written as, treats a collection-time install as pre-existing and preserves it for the life of the worker. That version went green locally and RED in CI on exactly the test it was meant to fix. The first attempt at it matched by `isinstance` and silently did nothing: `agents/` is on `sys.path`, so `core.security.log_redaction` and `agents.core.security.log_redaction` are two module objects over this one file with two distinct `SecretRedactionFilter` classes, and the root handler was carrying the other one. The match is by class name now, and four paired tests pin both halves — including the alternate import path, which is the case the first attempt missed.

reviews.summary: **Gap (a) of four, plus the row's `chmod 0600 atomic writes` clause.** Both pairing credentials stop being written in the clear: `SenderPairing._code` becomes `_code_hash`, and each deeplink entry moves from being keyed by its raw token to being keyed by an opaque 8-byte id with the token's salted digest inside the entry. Verification hashes the candidate and `hmac.compare_digest`s two fixed-length hex digests, so neither the length nor any prefix of the stored credential leaks and the deeplink failure reasons stay indistinguishable. A one-time migration accepts a pre-H497 plaintext file, rehashes it in memory and rewrites it, preserving each link's channel, `created_at` and `expires_at` — an upgrade never locks the owner out nor resurrects a spent link. `_digest` encodes with `surrogatepass` so a lone surrogate (from a hand-edited store, or from the body of the one pairing route a stranger is meant to reach) misses instead of raising. `atomic_write_json` lands every JsonStore file owner-only. **The review found three false claims and all three are corrected — two of them by changing the code rather than the prose.** (1) The module docstring said the store "holds nothing that can pair anybody". True of a 192-bit deeplink token; **false of the pairing code**, which is whatever the owner typed: a four-digit code was recovered from the file by exhausting 10,000 candidates in **0.006 s** and then used to pair. The code is now stretched with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 240,000 rounds, `kdf` and `rounds` stored beside each digest so raising the count later cannot lock an owner out, and a record written by the first cut is upgraded in place on the next successful pair — the one moment the plaintext is in hand — while a FAILED guess leaves it untouched. The deeplink token stays on plain SHA-256, deliberately: `redeem_deeplink` hashes once per outstanding link, so a slow hash there is a CPU lever for any stranger sending `/start junk`, and at 192 bits there is nothing for stretching to buy. (2) The salt comment defended leaving the code unstretched by pointing at the store-wide guess budget — an ONLINE control held in memory, which has no bearing on an attacker who has read the file, the exact threat at-rest hashing answers. Rewritten to say what stretching does and does not promise. (3) `atomic_write_json` claimed its chmod-before-replace ordering left no readable window. It left a shorter one: `write_text` creates the tmp at `0o666 & ~umask` and the whole payload is in it before the chmod runs. The tmp is now created EMPTY through a descriptor opened 0600 and closed again (json_store.py:74) before the unchanged `Path.write_text` call at json_store.py:78 opens that existing file — a mode `write_text` leaves alone — so no byte of a pairing digest ever lands in a file whose mode the umask chose; pinned by a test that neutralises `os.chmod` and still requires 0600. **#1179 (adversarial wave two) touched only this row's test file; `pairing.py` and `json_store.py` are byte-identical to the #1171 state.** The review claimed every inbound `/start` costs 240k rounds outside any budget. It does not, for two reasons worth keeping apart. First, `/start` never reaches the code KDF at all: a Telegram `/start <payload>` is routed by `TelegramChannel._maybe_pair_deeplink` (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:591-629) to `redeem_deeplink`, which is one plain-SHA-256 `_digest` per outstanding link, and every other chat message reaches `gate_inbound` through `ChannelGateway.route` with `code=kwargs.get("pairing_code")` (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:82), a kwarg no channel in the tree ever sets — so the one path on which a stranger can spend a KDF run is `POST /api/channels/pairing/request`, the route the new test's docstring names (tests/test_pairing_secrets_at_rest.py:469). Second, on that path the KDF sits behind a budget: `_code_guess_budget_spent` (pairing.py:606) is store-wide and is consulted at pairing.py:587, BEFORE `_code_matches` at pairing.py:592, so a stranger rotating sender ids — the per-sender bucket is keyed on an id the caller chose — buys at most `_MAX_CODE_GUESSES_PER_WINDOW` = 10 KDF runs per 10-minute window however many ids they present, and a request presenting no code never reaches the KDF at all. `test_the_kdf_a_stranger_can_trigger_stays_inside_the_guess_budget` (tests/test_pairing_secrets_at_rest.py:466) now pins that by counting `_stretch` calls rather than timing them, so a slow CI box cannot fail it: 60 requests from 60 fresh ids → 10 runs with 50 turned away `rate_limited` (with the budget check removed it is 60 runs and 0 refusals — re-reproduced at this re-verification), and zero runs for a code-less request. That is the code-side counterpart of the deeplink decision above — the token stays unstretched because nothing budgets `redeem_deeplink`'s per-link compare; the code may be stretched because its compare sits behind one. Nothing in #1179's persona-scan (`agent.py`, `quarantine.py`) or MCP-stdio (`mcp/client.py`) work touches this row. **Second slice (2026-09-22) — one store per process, and the one-use claim made true for the deeplink path.** The module promised a deeplink is "one use, ever", and inside one instance it was; production held two. The orchestrator registers the long-lived `sender_pairing` (the gateway gates on it, the pairing router mints and revokes on it) and `TelegramChannel` was built in `web.py` without one, so `_maybe_pair_deeplink` opened a throwaway `SenderPairing()` per `/start <token>`. A `JsonStore` reads its file once and every save writes the whole in-memory state back, so the two were two stores, not two views of one: a token redeemed over Telegram was spent in the throwaway and still outstanding in the orchestrator's copy, whose next save — any save; a stranger knocking is enough — wrote it back to disk, where the next throwaway redeemed it again and paired a second sender. With a relocated data root the two did not even share a file (the registry spelled a cwd-relative `memory_logs/sender_pairing.json`, the throwaway used `data_path(...)`), so under `JARVIS_HOME` no link ever redeemed. Fixed by wiring, not by hardening the store: `TelegramChannel` takes `pairing=` and `web.py` passes `gateway.pairing`, the same object by identity; an adapter handed nothing refuses to pair rather than building one (same reply as a bad token, a warning naming the cause, the message still swallowed); the registry entry spells the path through `data_path("sender_pairing.json")`. Five tests in `tests/test_telegram_pairing_shared_store.py` pin the resurrection with two instances over one file as the premise, a spent link staying spent after the owner's store saves, `revoke_deeplinks()` reaching the live adapter, an un-wired channel building nothing, and the real lifespan handing the channel `orch.sender_pairing` under the data root; red-proofed against the unpatched sources.
reviews.remaining: **The row names four hardening gaps; (a) is closed, (c) is closed for the deeplink path, (b) and (d) are open.** (c) *revocation reaching live adapters*: `revoke_deeplinks()` and `unpair()` now act on the one object the Telegram adapter redeems from and the gateway consults on every message, so there is no second copy for a link or an approval to survive in — pinned by `test_revoking_on_the_shared_store_reaches_the_live_telegram_adapter`. Slack and Discord have no deeplink path and gate through the same gateway instance. Still outstanding, from the row itself: (b) *no lockout after N failed attempts* — the row wants a 1 h lockout after 5 failed approvals, checked BEFORE the pending lookup so a code already in flight cannot be brute-forced past it; there is still only a rate limit and an in-memory guess budget, both of which reset on restart. (d) *no admin-vs-user command split on channels*, so any paired sender gets every command; the row wants a split with an always-allowed floor of `{help, whoami}`. **Unaddressed from the Hermes column:** pairing-code GENERATION (8 characters from a 32-char unambiguous alphabet via `secrets.choice`) and the code's 1 h TTL — the code here never expires; "max 3 pending per platform" (the store bounds 200 globally); "1 request per user per 10 min" (it is 5); `unauthorized_dm_behavior` treating inbox-shaped platforms differently from chat-shaped ones; and the ordered authorization union (allow-all flag → pairing approvals → per-platform allowlist → global allowlist → global allow-all → default DENY), which is still an ad-hoc sequence in `is_allowed`/`gate_inbound`. **Two honest limits of the second slice.** The store itself still has no defence against a second instance — the guarantee is one instance per process by construction, and the premise test says so in words. And an install that had relocated its data root (`JARVIS_HOME`) and paired senders through the HUD kept them in `<cwd>/memory_logs/sender_pairing.json`; the store now opens under the data root, so those senders are held once more until re-approved (the owner's allowlisted ids never lived in that file and are unaffected). **And the limit carried from the first slice.** Stretching is a work factor, not a wall: a four-digit code goes from milliseconds to minutes, an eight-character mixed-alphabet code becomes infeasible, and **nothing enforces a floor on what the owner types** — `PairingCodeBody` caps the length at 128 and sets no minimum — while generating the code for them, the row's own prescription, is not implemented.

reviews.summary: Nerva now warns about a dangerous host posture, as Hermes does, on top of a network half that was already stronger. assert_safe_bind (agents/core/boot_guards.py) still refuses an unauthenticated non-loopback bind and prints the exact env vars that fix it, and GET /api/security/posture still reports the secrets backend, skill signing, sandbox isolation and guardrails honestly. agents/core/host_posture.py adds the host half: three read-only checks that never block and never change anything, each answering ok, warn or unknown (it could not tell, never a false green), with a reason, what it saw and the fix. check_root (agents/core/host_posture.py:71) warns when the process runs as root (euid 0) on any host, headless included, or elevated on Windows (IsUserAnAdmin). check_sshd (agents/core/host_posture.py:168) reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config the way sshd does (_SshdScan, agents/core/host_posture.py:120): Include files are read in place, relative paths from /etc/ssh, each pattern's hits in lexical order, at most 16 deep; Keyword value, Keyword=value and trailing comments are accepted and keywords and values are case-insensitive; the first PasswordAuthentication outside a Match block wins, so a drop-in Included at the top overrides the main file; a Match block (to the end of its file, an Include inside it conditional) never sets the global value but a Match block that turns passwords on warns too; an absent directive is the sshd default yes and warns; no sshd_config is ok; an unreadable file is unknown unless the answer was read elsewhere; an unrecognised value is unknown. check_container_storage (agents/core/host_posture.py:241) detects a container (/.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv, or a docker, kubepods, containerd, libpod or lxc cgroup of PID 1, in_container) and then finds the mount the data root (resolved through symlinks) lives on in /proc/self/mountinfo (parse_mountinfo with its octal escapes, mount_of taking the longest containing mount point and the later of two stacked mounts): the container's own root filesystem or a tmpfs warns, a volume or bind mount is ok, no mountinfo or no mount is unknown. run_checks and report (agents/core/host_posture.py:273, :287) run the three independently, a failing check becoming an unknown row. The hub logs each warning once per process at start, after logging is set up, off the event loop (log_startup, agents/web.py lifespan). GET /api/security/posture (admin) gains host: the three findings and a warnings count (agents/core/routers/security.py). python scripts/doctor.py and nerva doctor show them as the advisory rows host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords and container_storage at the end of the report: a warning is warn with the fix and never fails the verdict, a check that could not tell or could not run is skip, never ok (check_host_posture, scripts/doctor.py:247). The module is stdlib only so the doctor can use it on a broken install. The shipped Dockerfile has no USER, so a stock container now shows the root warning; running the image as a non-root user is left to the deploy. Tests: tests/test_h501_host_posture.py (42), with real sshd_config trees in a temporary directory (drop-ins read first and last, lexical order, absolute and quoted Includes, Match blocks in the main and in an included file, a trailing comment naming a file, an Include loop) and real mountinfo text. 55 mutants: 53 killed after five cases were added; the other two were dead code, removed.

**`JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE` flips from opt-in to default-on**, so a spawned stdio MCP server is handed the `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` baseline plus its own `env` instead of `os.environ.copy()` — API keys, tokens, proxies and every `JARVIS_*` setting withheld. A second flag, `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV`, is the owner-reachable migration remedy: a comma-separated list of host variable names that pass the baseline even when `_SECRET_LIKE` matches them. `_merged_env()` emits one INFO line per connect counting host values the child does not receive, carrying **no variable name and no value**. `GET /api/admin/mcp` rows gain `env_baseline`. And Nerva's own WorldView MCP server is handed its `WORLDVIEW_API_URL`, which the flip would otherwise have silently replaced with the built-in `http://localhost:4000`. **The review found two blocking majors and four false claims; all six are addressed.** **(1)** `routers/mcp.py` asserted an invariant the code did not hold: the comment said a row that spawns no subprocess reports `None` "rather than a badge it has not earned" and enumerated two cases. A third exists and is the only one an owner can create today — `POST /api/admin/mcp` does no command validation, so a row with a whitespace-only command or a shell metacharacter persists, and `connect()` answers `unsafe_command` from `_command_argv()` **before** `create_subprocess_exec`. Such a row reported `env_baseline: true` for a child that never existed; the row now calls the same `_command_argv()` `connect` does, so the two cannot disagree, and the guard test carries both spellings. **(2)** `BACKLOG.md` still shipped the pre-flip claim and therefore stated the OPPOSITE of the code — "opt-in, default-off … keeps working until the owner opts in" — in the one file `CLAUDE.md` tells a reader to query for what is delivered. That is exactly the misreading the slice's own documentation work exists to prevent. Corrected, and `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` now covers BACKLOG.md too, including a check that the "opt-in, default-off" wording is gone. Two wording corrections went with them: the `env_baseline` field describes the live FLAG, i.e. the posture for the NEXT spawn, not the environment the running child holds (`_merged_env()` runs once at connect, the row is read per request); and the migration note steered the reader at auth failures only, when the flip also withholds `PYTHONPATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` — plumbing whose absence produces an ImportError, a hang or a connect timeout, nothing resembling an auth error. **#1179 (cda4e19d, adversarial-review finding 4) widened the DISCLOSURE, not the guarantee, and touched two of the five cited files.** `agents/core/mcp/client.py`: the module docstring now names a SECOND route by which a hostile child recovers the withheld keys — not only `/proc/<ppid>/environ` but the **filesystem**, which the baseline narrows not at all: `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` in the child reaches the very file `plugin_manager.build` read those keys from (`client.py:17-36`). New `_CWD_SECRET_FILES = (".env", ".env.local")` and `cwd_secret_files(cwd)` (`client.py:215-242`; `None` → `Path.cwd()`, the inherited default; unreadable and missing both count as absent) report which of them the child can open, and `_merged_env()` calls it right after the withheld-count INFO line — only when something WAS withheld (`:555`) and such a file is readable — emitting one WARNING per connect, "withholding is undercut — .env readable in the server's working directory", carrying **filenames only, never a variable name** (`client.py:565-571`), because a variable name enumerates which providers the box holds while `.env` tells the owner nothing new. Deliberately not a refusal: refusing to spawn over a `.env` breaks every dev checkout and re-pointing `cwd` breaks every server that resolves a relative path, so the module's posture stays *withhold and say so*. `tests/test_mcp_transports.py` gains `test_cwd_secret_files_reports_what_the_child_can_open` (`:830`; a directory named `.env.local` is not a file) and `test_the_withheld_count_is_not_announced_alone_when_a_dotenv_is_reachable` (`:854`; WARNING level, `OPENAI_API_KEY` absent from the line, silent when no file is reachable). Everything else above is as assessed: the default-on flag (`client.py:90`, `:190`), `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST`/`_SECRET_LIKE` (`:161-176`), `stdio_env_extra_allowed` (`:197-208`), the count-only INFO line (`:556-559`) are untouched, and `worldview_write.py` and `tests/test_mcp_admin.py` are byte-identical to the prior stamp. **The later fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) touched two cited files without touching this slice:** `client.py` gained `tool_patterns_over_bounds` (`client.py:138-154`) and a deny-bounds block in `MCPServer.__init__` (`:407-418`), and `admin_mcp_add` now also refuses a `tools_allow`/`tools_deny` over the 64-pattern / 128-char bounds (`routers/mcp.py:202-208`); neither reads the environment, the baseline flags or `env_baseline`, so the env code above only moved (+19 lines up to `MCPServer.__init__`'s filter block, +31 after it). The docstring pin `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` (`test_mcp_transports.py:554`) survived the rewrite because both strings it asserts remain (`/proc/<ppid>/environ` at `client.py:21`, "defence in depth, not a security boundary" at `:30`). 41/41 cited tests green (33 + 8), re-run at the bounds-change head.
reviews.remaining: **The documented per-server `env` migration path does not exist as a reachable surface.** `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field (`routers/mcp.py:131-143`, no `model_config`), `POST /api/admin/mcp` drops the key (pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`), and neither `to_config` (`client.py:798-812`) nor `load_from_config` (`:814-849`) writes or reads one — the module docstring says as much at `client.py:41-45`. The only remedy an owner can actually reach is the **host-wide** `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV` (`:92-98`, "Host-wide, not per-server"), which is a strictly weaker grant than the per-server one the docs describe: an owner whose forge server needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` must allow it for every stdio server on the host. Whether to ship on that or build the per-server surface first is a product decision, written up as `docs/OWNER_TASKS.md` §P28.3 with both options. **Related and also owner-level:** `XAUTHORITY` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` are both on `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` (`client.py:169`), and today one is listed-but-silently-dropped (`_SECRET_LIKE` at `:174-176` matches the `AUTH` in `XAUTHORITY`) while the other is listed-and-handed-over — they should be consistent in one direction or the other. **And the honest ceiling, stated wherever the guarantee is:** this is **defence in depth, not a security boundary**, and since #1179 the module states that ceiling by TWO routes rather than one (`client.py:17-36`). The child is same-UID with no namespace, so a server that can run a subprocess reads the withheld variables straight out of `/proc/<ppid>/environ`; and the baseline narrows the **filesystem** not at all — `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` hands back exactly the keys that were withheld, which `cwd_secret_files()` now says out loud at connect (WARNING, filenames only, `client.py:565-571`) rather than leaving the owner to infer a protection from the withheld count alone. What the baseline buys is that a *careless* or *curious* server does not get them by accident, and that an owner's `JARVIS_*` settings are not ambient in a third party's process. It does not stop an adversary, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise; closing the filesystem route as well as the `/proc` one needs real process isolation (separate UID, namespace or container — `client.py:33-36`), which is not shipped. **Unaddressed from the row:** there is no refusal of an MCP entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume — no command allow-listing, no signature or provenance check on the spawned binary (the docstring itself calls the screener "still-unshipped", `client.py:34`), and `POST /api/admin/mcp` still stores `req.command` verbatim after checking only transport, trust tier, tool-filter shape and bounds, and duplicate name (`routers/mcp.py:174-227`, `:184`); the only shape check is `_command_argv()`'s shell-metacharacter/NUL refusal at connect (`client.py:519-529`), which is not a screener. #1179 changed none of this — it explicitly chose disclosure over refusal. This slice hardens what the child *receives*; the row also asks who the child is allowed to *be*.

reviews.summary: archive_safe is the only module in Nerva that reads an archive. Backup verify and restore unpack through extract_tar_path (agents/core/archive_safe.py:573; agents/core/backup.py:598, agents/core/backup.py:667). Marketplace install_from_zip unpacks through extract_zip_bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:637; agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:816). The old backup._safe_extract and the marketplace _safe_targets+extractall pass are gone. An AST scan (tests/test_archive_safe.py:702, with probes at tests/test_archive_safe.py:688) fails when any other product module imports tarfile or zipfile outside a write-only allowlist, opens an archive for reading or calls an extract-family method. normalize_member (agents/core/archive_safe.py:122) folds backslash to '/' first. It then refuses empty, NUL, POSIX-absolute, Windows-absolute, UNC and drive-lettered names, and any '..' or empty part. Only regular files and directories are written. Symlink, hardlink, device, fifo and sparse tar members raise (agents/core/archive_safe.py:504), and so do symlink, device, fifo, socket and encrypted zip entries (agents/core/archive_safe.py:596). _Planner (agents/core/archive_safe.py:182) validates every member before the first write: name, type, in-archive conflicts and duplicates, member count and declared bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:257). It also checks the destination's existing content (agents/core/archive_safe.py:286): a link on the way to a member is refused, and so is a directory where a file goes (tests/test_archive_safe.py:365, tests/test_backup.py:471). The pre-scan reads the stream to its end (agents/core/archive_safe.py:522), so a bad gzip CRC, trailing data or a corrupt header part-way through is a refusal, not a shortened tree (tests/test_archive_safe.py:482, tests/test_archive_safe.py:517). Bytes are counted again while streaming (agents/core/archive_safe.py:389). The byte budget is clamped to free space plus the blocks of the single-link files the archive replaces (agents/core/archive_safe.py:314), so an in-place --force restore fits (tests/test_backup.py:443). PAX and GNU long-name header payloads are capped before tarfile reads them, 1 MiB each and 256 MiB in total (agents/core/archive_safe.py:461, agents/core/archive_safe.py:483; tests/test_backup.py:515). A link or hardlinked name at a member's path is unlinked and the file is created O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, never written through (agents/core/archive_safe.py:373; tests/test_archive_safe.py:323, tests/test_archive_safe.py:349). Backups take their caps from JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_MEMBERS and JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES (agents/core/backup.py:86); skill packages use SKILL_PACKAGE_LIMITS (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:42). On the producing side, create_backup writes both the encrypted and the plaintext branch through atomic_write, a sibling temp file that is fsynced and then os.replace'd (agents/core/archive_safe.py:654; agents/core/backup.py:415, agents/core/backup.py:420). Archives are GNU-format tar (agents/core/backup.py:474). The export walk skips symlinks (agents/core/archive_safe.py:715; agents/core/backup.py:401). publish_skill uses it on the staged copy it signs (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:392); the copy itself is built from the bytes of one source snapshot, which refuses a linked folder, a link or non-regular member and a file that changed while read (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:375), which has its own test (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:219). Every other name, hardlinked ones included, is archived as its own regular member (agents/core/backup.py:434, agents/core/backup.py:458; tests/test_backup.py:388). verify and restore compare the manifest's file_count with what the archive held (agents/core/backup.py:625; tests/test_backup.py:430). install_from_zip stages inside skills_dir, runs the signature gate there, and only then renames the tree into place (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:854, agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:885). A non-zip upload is a 400 refusal (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:194). Staging left by a killed install is swept once it is an hour old (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:773; tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:203). Restore stays an operator CLI action. It prints 'partial restore' when a failure came after the first write (agents/core/backup.py:716) and 'nothing restored' only for a pre-scan refusal (agents/core/backup.py:722). tests/test_backup.py:606 pins that no product module, script or subprocess caller reaches it. The pre-scan also refuses a component longer than the destination's NAME_MAX or a path past PATH_MAX, which the existing-path walk cannot see under a new directory (agents/core/archive_safe.py:251; tests/test_archive_safe.py:726), and a write the destination refuses mid-restore (permissions, a full disk) is a named ArchiveRejected marked partial, never a traceback (agents/core/archive_safe.py:445; tests/test_archive_safe.py:738). A restore leaves the archive's manifest in the target; create_backup never archives a top-level backup_manifest.json from the data root (agents/core/backup.py:482), so a backup of a restored root carries one manifest and verifies, restores and serves the forget purge's verified pre-snapshot (tests/test_backup.py:636, tests/test_backup.py:675). A backup of a restored root made before this change carries that name twice; verify and restore accept exactly that one repeat, last wins as tarfile resolved it, and count the dropped copy against the manifest's file_count (agents/core/backup.py:599, agents/core/backup.py:642; tests/test_backup.py:651). The repeat is bounded: the dropped copy still counts against the member and byte caps, and a third copy or any other duplicate is refused (agents/core/archive_safe.py:220, agents/core/archive_safe.py:223; tests/test_archive_safe.py:768, tests/test_archive_safe.py:775, tests/test_archive_safe.py:790). Known limit: backups made on main from a data root holding a symlink or hardlink fail verify and restore by design.

Nerva now fails loudly when TLS trust is misconfigured, and verification is never quietly off, as Hermes requires. agents/core/tls_trust.py is the one place that decides what outbound clients verify against; agents/core/http_client.py re-exports its tls_verify for the plugin clients (:180). (1) Boot validation: validate_ca_environment (agents/core/tls_trust.py:170) checks every CA variable that is set, JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE, SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and CURL_CA_BUNDLE as files and SSL_CERT_DIR as directories, and certifi itself. Each file must exist, be a file, load into an SSLContext and hold at least one certificate: any certificate, so a pinned self-signed server certificate counts (_check_file, :145; _count_certs through cert_store_stats, :137). certifi must also be at least 1 KB and importable. Each problem is reported with the variable, its value and what is wrong. It also carries a copy-pasteable repair for this host's shell (_repair, :107): export X="$(python -m certifi)" or unset X on POSIX, the PowerShell form on Windows, a path to the root for JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE, a certifi reinstall. When H273's provenance says a .env file set the value, the problem names that file (_set_in, :123). enforce_ca_environment (:217) raises SystemExit with every problem at once. The web lifespan runs it right after enforce_boot_posture (agents/web.py:467), before the data home is scaffolded or anything dials out, so a broken SSL_CERT_FILE is no longer an unnamed FileNotFoundError on the first model call. tls_verify's warnings now name the variable that actually held the bad value (SSL_CERT_FILE when that was the source). (2) Model egress on the anchor: llm_async_client (agents/core/llm/egress.py:104-107) gives every model backend's client verify_for(backend, base_url), so the Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenAI Responses, xAI, LM Studio, Ollama and VLM clients all verify against certifi plus JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE (or SSL_CERT_FILE). That is always an explicit SSLContext (trust_context, agents/core/tls_trust.py:94), so a client that keeps trust_env for the owner's proxy never has httpx read SSL_CERT_FILE itself; a caller's own verify or test transport is left alone. (3) Per-target switch: verify_for (:252) returns False only for a provider id or a host named exactly (case-insensitive, trailing dot ignored) in JARVIS_TLS_INSECURE_TARGETS (insecure_targets, :237). Every client built that way logs a WARNING naming its URL, and the start logs the list once. Under JARVIS_HARDENED=1 the list is ignored with an ERROR, and a bad or missing CA path never yields False. docs/FLAGS.md and .env.example document both variables. Local probes that build a plain httpx client (router.py health checks, ollama_control, lmstudio_control, model_setup, local_model_inventory) talk plain HTTP to loopback, and the boot check covers the variables they would read. Tests: tests/test_h504_tls_trust.py (45) uses real certificates made by cryptography (a CA, a leaf, a pinned self-signed leaf, a CRL-only PEM). It also runs end to end against a real HTTPS server on 127.0.0.1 whose certificate only the test CA signs: refused without the owner's root, accepted with JARVIS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_FILE, accepted only for a listed target, and refused again when hardened. Auto-vision collateral review (2026-10-02, 876c3e2b): .env.example and docs/FLAGS.md gained auto-route instructions only. The TLS trust implementation, boot guard and HTTPS validation tests were unchanged. Existing equivalent behavior remains the recorded verdict; no new TLS behavior is claimed. Egress collateral review (2026-10-03, 08e29d4a): the owned async recorder receives an inert marker that lets the private SOUL draft prove it remains the final request hook. Protocol refusal, quota handling, ledger recording and TLS trust logic are unchanged; scoped H513/egress regressions pass. Existing equivalent verdict preserved.

**The write half, as a generic mechanism rather than a special case.** `agents/core/tool_rpc.py` gains a registrar-owned *call classifier*: a gated tool may register a pure function over one call's args returning bounded labels. `handle()` stamps them onto the durable approval card's payload and appends the notice to the card title; `execute()` re-derives them from the args about to run and refuses with `approval_class_mismatch` unless the approved card carried the same `class` — so a card approved as a scratch note cannot be redeemed against a write to SOUL.md. `_classify` fails closed (a raising, non-Mapping, over-long or non-alphanumeric result refuses the call rather than letting it through unlabelled) and strips the reserved `tool`/`args`/`target` keys so labels cannot rewrite the card's identity. `agents/core/file_tools.py` registers `FileTools.classify_mutation` for `file_write` and `file_delete`, matches on the BASENAME in any directory inside the roots (an instruction file is wherever the harness that reads it looks — `_load_soul` alone searches three), carries a `steers_future_runs` flag into the kernel Action payload, and adds a secondary floor in `_mutate`. A sandboxed script cannot label its own write nor strip the label off one: the classifier is registrar-owned and `handle()` returns `approval_required` before the handler is ever reached. **The review found one major and it is fixed here.** The roster omitted `HEARTBEAT.md` and `HEARTBEAT.local.md` — the files in this repo that *literally* schedule future runs: `core/heartbeat.py` scans every agent directory for them, prefers the gitignored `.local` overlay exactly as `SOUL.local.md` does, and turns what it finds into cron-scheduled agent runs. Reproduced against a real `ToolRPCServer`: a write to `HEARTBEAT.local.md` produced `class=None` and the generic title "Tool 'file_write' via RPC" — a card byte-identical to a write to a scratch note, for an action that installs a cron expression driving every later run. Both names are in the class now, and the roster is pinned against `heartbeat.py`'s own source rather than restated, so a loader that learns a new name fails the test instead of silently escaping the class. The exact-set pin beside it was tightened, not loosened. **Widened by #1177 (the #1161–#1174 adversarial review) — same mechanism, larger class, re-assessed here.** The roster is now `INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES` (`soul.md`, `agents.md`, `claude.md`, `gemini.md`, `.cursorrules`, `heartbeat.md`) and every `.md` name's gitignored `.local` overlay is *derived* by `_local_overlay` into `INSTRUCTION_FILE_NAMES` (eleven names) instead of being spelled out by hand — which is what brought `CLAUDE.local.md` / `AGENTS.local.md` / `GEMINI.local.md` into the class; the first cut listed only the SOUL and HEARTBEAT overlays, so a `CLAUDE.local.md` write — same harness, same authority, and it wins over the committed file — asked with the title of a scratch note. `looks_instruction_name` now also matches by extension through `INSTRUCTION_FILE_SUFFIXES = (".mdc",)`, so Cursor's freely-named `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files, the format that superseded `.cursorrules`, are in the class as well. `classify_mutation`, the `steers_future_runs` flag, `_authorize`, the `_mutate` floor and `register_file_tools` are unchanged, and `tool_rpc.py` is byte-identical. Tests: `tests/test_file_tools_instruction_floor.py` (44) pins both sets exactly (the six base names and the eleven derived ones), derives the overlay requirement from the roster in `test_every_name_in_the_roster_brings_its_local_overlay` so a name added later brings its overlay or fails, keeps the heartbeat.py-derived pin, and exercises `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.mdc` through `write_file` with the kernel off; `tests/test_file_tools_instruction_class_toolrpc.py` (18) proves the durable card for `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` and `.cursor/rules/r.mdc` carries `class=agent_instructions` and the notice in its title, and that nothing reaches disk before approval. **The read half, first piece (2026-09-22), and its review round.** `agents/core/heartbeat.py` — the loader that turns HEARTBEAT.md / HEARTBEAT.local.md into cron-scheduled runs — refuses a flagged entry at parse time. `scan_heartbeat_config` runs `detect_injection_normalized` over every string in the YAML front-matter, keys and values, nested to a bound of 16, and the walker fails CLOSED: a container at the bound (`nesting-too-deep`, a `&x [*x]` alias cycle included), a `!!binary` value (`unscannable-value-type:bytes` — decoded so the verdict names what it hid, refused regardless) or any type `yaml.safe_load` never produces is a refusal, not a leaf the walker had nothing to say about; `!!set` values are walked; YAML's own scalars (bool, number, null, date) are inert. It decodes and scans a TAG-plane payload so it is named rather than merely deleted, excusing only a run shaped like a subdivision flag emoji (🏴, up to eight TAG letters, CANCEL TAG — England, Scotland, Wales) from the bare-invisible-run flag while still scanning what such runs spell; and it joins UTF-16 surrogate pairs first, because PyYAML decodes a `\uDB40\uDC70` escape into two lone surrogates that no code-point range in `quarantine.py` matches but that a JSON serialiser on the way to a model re-joins into the invisible TAG character (reproduced). One hit refuses the whole entry — a heartbeat is one scheduled job with no 'rest of the persona' to preserve, so the fail-closed answer is not to schedule it: `_parse_heartbeat` never returns a flagged config, and `load_from_config` — which the orchestrator calls right after `load_all` at startup — skips a refused agent instead of writing the agents.yaml interval entry that put it back before `start()`, so nothing reaches `_heartbeat_configs`, `start()`, `start_heartbeat()` or the `POST /heartbeat/{id}/run` path; a flagged overlay does not fall back to the shipped template; a reload starts each directory from a clean slate (no stale verdict, no stale config, in either direction); the refusal is logged with the file's absolute path, its sha256 over the one buffer that was parsed and scanned, and the matched patterns, never the payload; and `get_status()` — what `GET /heartbeat/status`, a deliberately public route, and the runtime run-log read — carries a `blocked` list (agent, file named relative to its root such as `souls/<id>/HEARTBEAT.local.md`, flags, digest) in both of its shapes. Every shipped HEARTBEAT.md loads clean. **`agents/core/security/quarantine.py` changed with it, for both loaders.** The review found that a blank-rendering character put INSTEAD of the space — the Hangul fillers (letters, so they also kill the raw `you are now\b` match), U+2800, a private-use character, or any character already in the table — defeated the SOUL path and the HEARTBEAT path alike: the raw copy had no space to match and the stripped copy had the words glued. `_detection_variants` also scans a copy in which every invisible character becomes a space, the table gains U+2800 and the three private-use planes (Co), and each copy is scanned again over its NFKC fold (fullwidth, ideographic space, ligatures). **An independent review of the first cut — two reviewers, ten distinct findings: two blocking, three major, four minor, one nit — eight fixed here, each red-first and neutered once:** `!!set`/`!!binary` skipped by the walker (blocking); the depth bound fail-open, and the 'at any depth' claim in this row, the BACKLOG bullet, the code comment and the test docstring false (blocking — corrected); blank-instead-of-space (major); `load_from_config` resurrecting a refused agent, and 'a refused entry is never scheduled' overstated for the production load order (major — corrected); the absolute path on the public route, the flag-emoji false refusal and the stale verdict on reload (minor); the two-read digest (nit). `tests/test_instruction_files_read_side_scan.py` (47) pins all of it — including equality with the plain spelling for fourteen blank characters through the detector, the HEARTBEAT loader and the SOUL per-line scan — and pins through `Agent._load_soul` the SOUL spellings the previous version of this row named as unproven ('You are now<U+200B>in developer mode' and 'You are now<U+0007>in developer mode'), which #1179 had already closed in code by routing `_scan_soul_body` through `detect_injection_normalized`.
reviews.remaining: **The read half now covers two of the three Nerva loaders and none of the external ones — the row stays partial.** H506 requires the same file class to be scanned at context-load time with a positive match replaced by `[BLOCKED: … Content not loaded.]`. What holds: SOUL.md / SOUL.local.md through `Agent._scan_soul_body` (H387's evidence, not this row's — per-line quarantine over the union of raw and normalised copies, cross-line wraps, whole-body drop above the ratio; the U+200B and U+0007 spellings after 'now' are pinned in this row's own test file), and HEARTBEAT.md / HEARTBEAT.local.md through `scan_heartbeat_config`, entry refused rather than line-stubbed. **Precisely what is not covered, stated rather than smoothed over:** the Markdown body after the front-matter is discarded by `_parse_heartbeat` and reaches no model, log or scheduler, so it is not scanned — `test_the_prose_body_is_not_loaded_and_therefore_not_scanned` is the tripwire a loader that starts reading it must flip; no heartbeat text is model input today — the checklist strings are keyword-routed to skills with constant arguments and echoed into a logged run summary — so the scan guards the mapping the loader hands to the agent, not a live prompt path; the keyword scanner is literal after normalisation, so a Cyrillic homoglyph ('Іgnore'), a combining overlay, markdown emphasis inside a phrase ('Ignore _all_ previous') and a phrase split across two checklist items still scan clean — a confusables fold is a separate `quarantine.py` slice, and the homoglyph is pinned as a tripwire in this row's test file; and the SOUL cross-line path (`_wrapped_injection_hits`) builds its own normalised copy inside `agent.py`, so a blank-instead-of-space spelling that ALSO wraps across lines is not covered there (agent.py is untouched here; it is H387's evidence, being re-evaluated by a sibling stream). **Adjacent, pre-existing, NOT fixed:** the orchestrator's `load_from_config` overwrites every shipped HEARTBEAT.md cron+checklist with the agents.yaml interval (all twelve shipped agents carry one), so at runtime `Agent.run_heartbeat` finds no checklist and returns None for the shipped roster — the loader semantics this row describes are what the code does, not what the shipped agents experience (recorded as a separate task); `load_all` keys the config by the front-matter's own `agent` field, so a clean `HEARTBEAT.local.md` in one agent's directory that says `agent: jarvis` replaces Jarvis's schedule (a refused file cannot — the verdict is keyed by directory); and `enabled: false` is parsed and never honoured. Still open on the read side: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md / `.cursorrules` / `*.mdc` are read by the external harnesses rather than by Nerva, so 'the same file class on the way in' is not met for them. The write-side deviations stand as before: the row's *"fails closed on a config read error"* clause has no analogue because the roster is a hard-coded frozenset; `allow_session=False` holds only incidentally through the gated toolrpc `autonomy_level="ask"` intake, with nothing pinning it; and the class covers `file_write`/`file_delete` only — the terminal contract, the skill importer and the desktop operator are outside it. Unverified, stated as such: whether the Telegram decision card and the HUD decision inbox render the write-side notice verbatim, and whether any HUD renders the `blocked` list (the API carries it; `frontend/src/gap.tsx` and `agents/web/static/systems.js` read `heartbeats` only). `_mutate`'s floor remains lifted by a caller-supplied `approved=True` by design.

reviews.summary: Code the agent writes is checked against a table of known-dangerous patterns, and the findings go back to the model and the owner. Nothing is ever refused. agents/core/code_guidance.py holds 26 rules (RULES, agents/core/code_guidance.py:89), each scoped to the file types it applies to. They cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill/joblib/marshal loads; yaml.load without SafeLoader, and yaml.unsafe_load; torch.load without weights_only=True); command and code injection (os.system/popen, shell=True, Python eval/exec, JS eval and new Function, child_process.exec and execSync, require('child_process').exec, a bare exec( in a file that imports child_process, a Go exec.Command of a shell); SQL built from an f-string or `%`; tempfile.mktemp; XSS sinks (innerHTML/outerHTML assignment, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML); and crypto and TLS footguns (ECB mode, createCipher without an IV on any receiver, verify=False, unverified SSL contexts, CERT_NONE, rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, md5/sha1 over a password). They also cover XXE parser flags and a remote `<script>` without integrity=. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags `${{ github.event.* }}` inside a GitHub Actions `run:` step, on the run line or in its `|`/`>` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a `- run: |` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: `model.eval()` and `obj.eval()`, `def eval(`, `yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)`, `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)`, `regex.exec()`, an `===` comparison with innerHTML, `hashlib.md5(data)`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns `{rule, line, message}`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at `\n` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a `scan-incomplete` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. `.env`, `.env.*` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1159) adds `code_warnings` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), `code_warning_count` and a title notice (`code not fully scanned` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a `./` or `//` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's `approval_required` answer carries `code_warnings`/`code_warning_count` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:197), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1572): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:958), the model reads `code_warnings` with a `code_guidance` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer `code_warnings` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:506) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1208), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a `scan-incomplete` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's `code_warnings` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:462), and generate_skill resets them first, so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and [learn:] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is `security.code_guidance` (agents/core/settings_db.py:241, on by default; only an explicit off turns it off, an unreadable store keeps it on, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:105). An aliased child_process module (`cp.exec`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. The review round added crafted megabytes (one per quadratic rule) scanned in under a second and a card labelled promptly through the ToolRPC intake, the time and size cuts, the pause reply driven through the agent loop, skill_propose's warnings and the reset, the symlink and path spellings, a package padded with assets, the `- run: |` block, the wrapped and nested calls, the child_process and createCipher spellings, CR/form-feed/U+2028 lines, the dotfiles and the safe-mode switch. The review round's 44 mutants were all killed, ten after seven cases were added.

Reviewed against live code; the inherited 2026-09-07 "partial" verdict stands, but for a different and much smaller reason than the audit recorded. The audit's "no Host-header validation anywhere" is stale: agents/core/host_policy.py is a 204-line module whose docstring (:4-22) names DNS rebinding explicitly, with normalize_host() at :54, parse_allowed_hosts() at :104 refusing a `*` entry at :119-120 and a leading-dot suffix wildcard at :121-122, host_accepted() at :157-181 matching loopback names, any IP literal, JARVIS_HOST, the ASGI scope's arrival address and JARVIS_ALLOWED_HOSTS, and assert_parseable_allowed_hosts() at :184 refusing boot on an unparseable list. It is wired at agents/web.py:20 (import) and :821-840 (`_host_guard`, returning {"error": "host not allowed", "code": 400}), registered so it runs before the rate limiter and inside the security-header and golden-signal layers (:794-797). Dumping app.user_middleware on the HEQ lot-1 head gives _golden_signals, _security_headers, _host_guard, _rate_limit, _no_store_for_polling, then lot 1's pure-ASGI _ForwardedProtoMiddleware, which only sets the request scheme and runs inside the guard. The boot guard is genuinely reached on the real serve path: agents/core/boot_guards.py:354, inside enforce_boot_posture, which the lifespan calls at agents/web.py:462-463 after the .env files load (agents/web.py:456-457, H273), so a list that lives only in .env is checked too; assert_front_door runs the same check over a caller's own mapping (agents/core/boot_guards.py:320). Refusal logging is rate-shaped (agents/web.py:803-805, agents/web.py:836) and logs only a coarse peer trust class (agents/web.py:808-817), never the attacker-chosen header value. Driven live on the lot-1 head with a loopback TestClient: `Host: evil.test` gets 400 on /status, /dashboard and /api/agents, where the real host gets 200 on /status and /api/agents. The row's other two asks hold, and lot 1 (H691) tightened the proxy half. Trusted-proxy entries are validated as bounded CIDRs at agents/core/proxy_trust.py:107 and :165 (note :308 only WARNS on a wide entry, it does not refuse). uvicorn's own forwarding-header allowlist (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, --forwarded-allow-ips) now refuses boot from the boot pass, which runs after the .env files load, when an entry is a wildcard, a /0, not an address, or a peer outside JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES and loopback (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:570). serve.py switches uvicorn's proxy-header layer off, X-Forwarded-Proto is believed only from a listed peer, and the rate limiter's localhost exemption now follows the localhost gate's origin (agents/web.py:779), so an unlisted same-box proxy is throttled. CORS is validated with reported rejections at agents/core/cors_policy.py, and no CORS middleware is installed at all by default. The WebSocket clause is excluded by the row itself and the exclusion still holds: no WebSocket server route exists in agents/ (lot 1's _ForwardedProtoMiddleware maps a listed proxy's scheme onto ws/wss scopes but adds no route), agents/web.py:798-799 says a future one must call host_accepted() itself, and agents/web.py:675 is the only ASGI app. 104/104 tests pass across the five relevant suites on the lot-1 head. What keeps this off "equivalent" is the residual the code names about itself at agents/web.py:800-802: _PROBE_PATHS is exempt from the guard (:824-825), so `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz. Re-confirmed live on the lot-1 head: a rebound page therefore still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts — cross-origin, because rebinding makes the browser treat them as same-origin. That is low severity and a deliberate operability trade, not an oversight, but it is a real deviation from Hermes' clause as written (which has no carve-out) and it is shippable work, so the row is partial rather than equivalent.
reviews.remaining: The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:767, applied at :824-825), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:800-802 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Needs a test alongside test_healthz_from_any_host_is_exempt asserting that a refused Host cannot read the counter body.

reviews.summary: The tamper-evident sink exists. AuditLogger.log (agents/core/security/audit.py:111) appends to a hash-chained SQLite log checked by verify_chain (agents/core/security/audit.py:209). The admin HUD reads it through GET /api/admin/audit (agents/core/routers/admin.py:674). One credential event is recorded: POST /api/admin/rotate-tokens (agents/core/routers/admin.py:532) writes a best-effort SecurityEventType.AUDIT_LOG row (agents/core/routers/admin.py:550) with action_taken token_rotated and no token value, and a sink failure only logs a warning. Nothing else in authentication reaches the audit. SecurityEventType (agents/core/security/types.py:22) still lists only secret_detected, pii_detected, ssrf_blocked, egress_downgrade, audit_log, llm_call and settings_change. _admin_guard (agents/web.py:246) and _user_guard (agents/web.py:327) return or raise 401/403 without writing an event, so a wrong admin token leaves only an HF-2 rate-limit bucket entry. TokenStore.issue, rotate and revoke_all (agents/core/security/token_store.py:73, agents/core/security/token_store.py:131, agents/core/security/token_store.py:143) write no audit, so CLI mint/rotate/revoke (agents/core/security/token_store.py:229) is invisible. No test asserts any auth audit row, including the existing rotation row.
reviews.remaining: Add auth event types: admin/user auth success, auth failure with reason (missing, invalid, network-disabled), token issued, token rotated, token revoked. Emit them from _admin_guard and _user_guard: failures always; successes deduplicated per token hash and client so the chain is not flooded. Also emit from TokenStore issue/rotate/revoke_all, which covers the CLI. Each event records scope, client host, reason and a token-hash prefix. A fixed redacted-field set (token, x-admin-token, x-user-token, authorization, cookie, code, state, ticket) is dropped before serialisation. Writes are best-effort: an audit failure must never change the allow/401/403 decision. The rotation route should switch to the new type. Tests must cover all of this.

A spoken reply now sounds like speech rather than read-out markdown, as Hermes requires, at every text-to-speech entry point. agents/core/voice/speech_text.py is the one normaliser (for_speech, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:152). It drops <think>/<thinking>/<reasoning> blocks, an unclosed one to the end, and everything before a closing tag that never opened. It drops fenced code (``` or ~~~, an unclosed fence to the end) and HTML tags. [text](url) reads as its text, ![alt](url) as its alt, and a bare or <autolinked> URL as "link"; the URL no longer eats a closing parenthesis or the sentence's full stop, so "doc (https://…)." is "doc (link).". Headings, list items (-, *, +, •, 1., 1), task boxes), block quotes and table rows lose their markers and end with a full stop (_line, :124). Table cells read with commas; separator rows and horizontal rules are dropped. Bold, italic, strikethrough and inline-code markers go and their words stay (_inline, :113), with word guards so 2*3*4 and my_var_name survive. Symbols are said in the reply's language (_symbols, :104, WORDS, :79): & as and/și, % as percent/la sută, -> → => as to/spre, and °, °C, °F as degrees/grade (Celsius, Fahrenheit). The language comes from the request, else a ro-RO-… voice, else the engine default (speech_lang, :95). Emoji go: pictographs, flags, keycaps, skin tones, ZWJ sequences, variation selectors and tag flags (_EMOJI, :61). Fish [emotion] tags are kept intact. Text with no letter or digit left is "" (_SAYABLE, :76), and the result is a fixed point. Wiring: TTSEngine.speak normalises before any backend, Fish included, and synthesises nothing when nothing is left (agents/core/voice/tts.py:212-220). An emotion-tags-only reply is also nothing for the other backends (:263). speak_stream normalises the whole reply before splitting sentences (:315), so a code or reasoning block spanning sentences is dropped whole. Through TTSEngine.speak this covers the wake-word VoicePipeline, VoiceChannel.send and chat voice notes: speakable() is for_speech plus its cap, and SpokenReply passes the chat's language (agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:69). POST /tts answers 204 with X-Nerva-Speech: nothing_to_say instead of synthesising (agents/core/routers/voice.py:76), and /tts/stream frames carry the spoken sentences. The HUD twin is frontend/src/speech-text.ts (speechText, frontend/src/speech-text.ts:105). Both implementations are pinned by the same cases (frontend/src/test/speech-text-cases.json, 47 cases, read by both suites). SpeechStreamFilter (:129) drops a fenced block or reasoning block whose markers arrive split across token deltas, holding back a tail that could still become a marker (including a <reasoning …> tag split inside its attributes). An unclosed block at the end is never spoken. frontend/src/voice.ts uses it on the live sentence stream (:281, :332, :343). It normalises the whole reply for /tts/stream, /tts and the browser's own speechSynthesis voice (:204), and every streamed sentence (:302). A 204 is silence, never an empty clip or the fallback voice (:244, :314). Mobile sends the reply to /tts, so the hub normalises it; ttsFetchBase64 reads 204 as '' and speak() finishes at once (mobile/src/api/client.ts:2402, mobile/src/audio/tts.ts:23). Tests: tests/test_h526_speech_text.py (Python, every shared case plus the fixed-point property), frontend/src/test/speech-text.test.ts and voice-speech-text.test.tsx (a live push-to-talk turn with a fence split across deltas), and mobile/src/api/__tests__/tts.test.ts. 126 mutants: 124 caught after nine cases were added; the other two were redundant code, removed. Named speech compatibility review: normalization still precedes synthesis, persona consent and tags retain existing behavior, and HTTP nothing-to-say/stream paths are unchanged. Shared speech-text and voice regressions pass.

Conducta de transcriere validează, pregătește și livrează: acceptă octeți direct (`BytesIO`, fără fișier temporar, deci vorbirea nu ajunge pe disc), îi mărginește, trece rezultatul prin filtrul de halucinații și întoarce santinele oneste în loc de text inventat. Are acum doi consumatori — ruta HTTP a browserului și canalul Telegram — peste un singur motor local partajat, nu unul per apelant. Named speech progress adds explicit selected STT command identities through the common registry, pinned across async selection and executor handoff. Native mode choice, input handling and sentinel cleanup remain covered by inbound voice and STT regressions; broader provider coverage remains open.
reviews.remaining: Un singur backend. Hermes are opt (faster-whisper local, `local_command`, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral cu diarizare și timestamp-uri pe cuvânt, xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe, DeepInfra) plus provideri pe comandă de shell, un ABC `TranscriptionProvider`, selecție explicită strictă cu auto-detect doar la o instalare neconfigurată vreodată, un plafon pe lungimea promptului Whisper, trunchierea liniștii înainte de upload ca să scadă octeții trimiși, un picker și `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. Nimic din astea nu e livrat. Nu din lene: clauza de guvernanță a rândului spune că orice STT în cloud trece prin `plugin.egress` și trimite vorbirea înregistrată a owner-ului în afara cutiei — e aceeași clasă de dezvăluire ca TTS-ul în cloud și trebuie clasificat, nu pus ca implicit de config. Cache-ul motorului stă tot în `routers/voice.py`, care e casa greșită pentru el; canalul îl importă în loc să-l dubleze, iar mutarea lui e o schimbare separată. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun model Whisper încărcat cu adevărat.

reviews.summary: Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură *inbound*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. `hallucination.py` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (`CANNED`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (`AMBIGUOUS`) cad doar când durata *decodată* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în `STTEngine.transcribe` și întoarce `[silence]` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în `frontend/src/voice.ts`: `recordUtterance` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după `SILENCE_MS`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un `rg -i 'vad'` peste `frontend/src/` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. `voice-vad.test.tsx` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul. Named speech compatibility review: the Whisper hallucination filter and decoded-duration handling remain on the native transcribe path; named commands preserve the existing exact-sentinel behavior. Hallucination and speech selection regressions pass.

A turn can read a document directly through file_read instead of relying on pre-indexed memory. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte).
reviews.remaining: There is no scanned-PDF coverage detection. An image-only PDF extracts to empty or near-empty text and is returned as a successful read, with no warning and no list of empty page ranges, and there is no OCR anywhere in the repo. Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: slides (.pptx), spreadsheets (.xlsx) and the other converter formats are not read, and no Office skills are bundled. The drop-a-file-in entry point belongs to the chat-attachment row.
