reviews.summary: Nerva has no ACP editor-agent surface. No handler for session/new, load, resume or fork exists anywhere under agents/, and the editor-surface row H542 is itself still missing, so nothing can accept an mcpServers array from an editor. The only outbound MCP registry is the process-wide MCPManager (agents/core/mcp/client.py:728-730), which holds a single servers dict. It is filled by the admin-guarded POST /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:174-175) and the persisted global config. There is no per-session server scope, no per-session mcp-<name> toolset, no bounded discovery join and no late refresh of the tool registry. tests/test_mcp_client.py and tests/test_mcp_admin.py exercise only the global registry.
reviews.remaining: Every accepted part is missing: (1) an ACP session entry point (session/new, load, resume, fork) that accepts an mcpServers array; this depends on H542. (2) A session-scoped MCP registry layered over the global MCPManager, so that a server registered for one session is invisible to every other session and is torn down when the session ends. (3) Off-loop registration (asyncio.to_thread) with a bounded discovery join (default 1.5 s), so a dead server cannot block session creation. (4) A scheduled late refresh that re-reads the session's tool list after slow discovery finishes. (5) Governance: session-supplied servers pass through the same outbound MCP authorization gate as configured servers (H554, still partial), and their trust tier is capped at no wider than a configured server's.

reviews.summary: Filtrele allow/deny pe nume și glob (`tools_allow`/`tools_deny`, potrivite cu `fnmatchcase` pe numele original al uneltei) restrâng atât listarea, cât și apelarea uneltelor MCP; deny prevalează (`tool_visible`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:603-610). `_list_tools` nu oferă o unealtă ascunsă (:596-601), iar `MCPServer.call_tool` răspunde `tool_filtered` înainte să plece vreun frame (:616-617), deci scoaterea unei unelte din filtru o revocă imediat, și la apel, nu doar la înregistrare. Un filtru malformat îngustează, nu lărgește: un allow care nu e listă devine `[]` (`_clean_tool_patterns`, :124-135). Limitele (64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere, :120-121) sunt fail-closed. Ruta de add (`admin_mcp_add`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:200-209) refuză cu 400 `{"error": "invalid_tool_filter", "field": ...}` un `tools_allow` sau `tools_deny` peste limite, în loc să-l taie (`tool_patterns_over_bounds`, client.py:138-154), la fel ca pe o valoare care nu e listă sau pe o intrare goală. Un deny care nu poate fi păstrat (peste 64 de pattern-uri, un pattern peste 128 de caractere, sau care nu e listă) venit dintr-un config editat manual prin `load_from_config` îngustează serverul la nimic (`tools_allow = []`) și loghează un avertisment (:407-418), pentru că un deny tăiat ar face din nou vizibilă unealta pe care o numea. Filtrele fac round-trip prin `to_config`/`load_from_config` (:808-809, :852-853). Teste (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py, 13/13 verzi): listare și deny prevalează (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:47-57), unealtă filtrată refuzată la apel pe nume (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:60-70), filtru malformat → nimic și round-trip de config (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:73-84), ruta primește filtre și refuză formele malformate (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:98-109), ruta refuză 129 de caractere / 65 de intrări pe ambele câmpuri (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:121-129) și acceptă un filtru exact la limită (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:132-138), un deny imposibil de păstrat ascunde toate uneltele cu avertisment (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:141-147), iar un config editat manual cu deny peste limite se încarcă fail-closed fără să atingă serverul vecin (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:150-159). Resursele/prompts sunt urmărite separat în H552.

Trust tiers și readOnlyHint limitează doar apelurile MCP, nu oferta. Tier-ul (`read-only` implicit, `full` explicit; alias-uri + `normalize_trust`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:105-117; `MCPServer.__init__` ridică ValueError pe o ortografie necunoscută, :397-400; `load_from_config` tratează tier-ul lipsă ca full-cu-avertisment și unul necunoscut ca read-only, :825-842; ruta de add validează tier-ul, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:194-197) și `MCPTool.read_only` (adevărat doar când `annotations.readOnlyHint is True`, :401-403) sunt consultate exclusiv în `_trust_denial` (:636-649), pe care `call_tool` îl rulează înaintea contractului de formă și înainte ca vreun frame să plece (:618-624): pe un server read-only orice tool nemarcat sau nelistat e refuzat pe nume cu `trust_denied` (`readOnlyHint_required` / `unlisted_tool`); `full` lasă totul la contractul de formă. Oferta (listarea) e îngustată numai de `tools_allow`/`tools_deny` (`_list_tools`/`tool_visible`, :584-610 — mecanismul H-4c pe care îl fixează tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py; un deny care nu încape în limitele de 64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere îngustează serverul la nimic tot prin `tools_allow`, :407-418); tier-ul și hint-ul nu ascund nimic: un server read-only își listează și tool-urile de scriere (`get_tools` :742-746 neîngustat; tests/test_mcp_trust.py:61-68; ruta admin le afișează cu `read_only: false`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:106-112).
reviews.remaining: Rămâne reconcilierea fiecărei căi de autorizare outbound față de contractul complet: nu există hop de aprobare (`kernel|authorize|approval|elicitation|retry` apare în agents/core/mcp/client.py doar în comentariul de la linia 103; `request_elicitation_consent` nu există în Nerva), tier-ul read-only refuză scrierile în loc să le ruteze la consimțământ, dict-ul de refuz (liniile 643-649) nu îi spune modelului să nu reîncerce, `_tool_call_blocked` (:651-670) evaluează doar forma `kind/server/tool/transport/args_keys`, iar apelul outbound nu scrie niciun rând de audit — singura cale outbound guvernată (kernel + audit) rămâne agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py, construită manual pentru un singur server `full`. Dovada pentru mecanismul trust/readOnlyHint e în tests/test_mcp_trust.py (necitat); tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py fixează doar filtrele: serverele pe care le apelează sunt construite cu `trust="full"` (helper-ul `_server`, tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:33-44), iar celelalte (inclusiv cazurile fail-closed pentru limite, tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:141-159) rămân pe tier-ul implicit fără să aserteze ceva despre el.

reviews.summary:
H557 is PARTIAL, not missing and not equivalent. The 2026-09-07 verdict is stale on one half and still correct on the other; the overnight triage's "already equivalent" is wrong. Re-read 2026-09-22 after #1179 (cda4e19d): that PR touched agents/core/mcp/client.py only in the stdio env-baseline disclosure — the scope paragraph of the module docstring (client.py:17-36), `from pathlib import Path` (:58), the `_CWD_SECRET_FILES` comment block + constant + `cwd_secret_files()` (:211-242) and the "withholding is undercut" warning block in `MCPServer._merged_env` (:560-571) — none of which this row relies on; `MCPTool`, `_list_tools`, `MCPManager.get_tools`/`_resolve`/`find_tool`/`call_tool` are byte-identical to the pre-#1179 file, and the six other evidence files are unchanged. Only line numbers moved (they had already drifted 94 lines at #1174 and were 151 off after #1179). Re-read again 2026-09-23 after the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1): it added `tool_patterns_over_bounds` after `_clean_tool_patterns` (client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in `MCPServer.__init__` (:407-418), a bounds refusal in `admin_mcp_add` (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:202-208) and bounds tests at the end of tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:112-159); none of it touches a schema, a tool name or the resolver, so client.py pointers moved another +19 (the `MCPTool` block) or +31 (from `MCPServer.__init__` on) and routers/mcp.py pointers past the filter check moved +4. Every pointer below is at HEAD. One fact did change between the 2026-09-07 stamping and HEAD, by #1152 (0ef4002f, 2026-09-15) rather than #1179: a fifth provider serialization path now exists (see NOT SHIPPED).

SHIPPED (the row's rationale half). The name-collision correctness bug is fixed and tested: agents/core/mcp/client.py:748-777 `MCPManager._resolve` accepts a bare tool name only when exactly one server offers it and otherwise returns `{"error": "ambiguous_tool", "servers": [...]}` (:772-776); `server/tool` or an explicit `server=` pins the server (:756-767); `find_tool` (client.py:779) and `call_tool` (client.py:788) both route through it; `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:367-370) is the `server/tool` form. tests/test_mcp_hardening.py:41-74 proves first-wins is gone (3 tests, passing; file 6/6 at HEAD). This is a genuine different-spelling equivalent of Hermes' disambiguation property, so `missing` under-reports the row.

NOT SHIPPED (the row's headline half). There is no `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` equivalent. agents/core/mcp/client.py:584-601 `_list_tools` still stores `t.get("inputSchema", {})` verbatim (client.py:592) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (client.py:357) with zero repair — the 2026-09-07 evidence sentence is still literally true. Nerva repairs at the dialect boundary instead, and on only ONE of five provider serialization paths: agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-438 `gemini_schema` covers Hermes' `required`-pruning (:424-428) and missing-`type` coercion (:421), and :441-451 `gemini_function_declarations` avoids the empty-OBJECT 400 (:447-449); its output feeds only gemini.py:351-353. The other four paths pass `input_schema` through byte-for-byte: Anthropic (tool_dialects.py:147-151 `anthropic_tools`, :149, via anthropic.py:197), OpenAI chat-completions (tool_protocol.py:19-27 `ToolSpec.as_openai`, :25 — shared by base.py:556, the Ollama path base.py:841 and openrouter.py:96), OpenAI Responses (responses.py:73-82, :78) and xAI Responses (xai.py:79-80 — `XAIBackend._payload` at xai.py:55 overrides `ResponsesBackend._payload` at responses.py:60, so the responses.py builder never runs for xAI; this path landed in #1152 on 2026-09-15, after the original verdict counted four). Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path: re-run at HEAD, `gemini_schema({"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}],"default":null})` → `{"default": null, "anyOf": [{"type":"string"}, {}]}` (the Pydantic null branch is not collapsed; on the Gemini path it degenerates to an empty schema, and the Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI paths ship the raw nullable union untouched — reproduced through `anthropic_tools` and `as_openai` on a ToolSpec carrying that property), and `{"definitions":{"Node":…},"properties":{"node":{"$ref":"#/definitions/Node"}}}` → `{"type":"object","properties":{"node":{}}}` (draft-07 `definitions`/`$ref` are not promoted to `$defs`, the referenced shape is silently deleted). No name sanitization exists anywhere: `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` is empty, and `qualified_name`'s `/` is not a legal provider function-name character.

ON REACHABILITY. The triage is right that this is currently unreachable from a model: `MCPManager.get_tools()` (client.py:742-746) has zero callers in the whole repo, `MCPTool.input_schema` is read nowhere outside its constructor (`grep -rn "MCPTool" agents/` hits only client.py; `grep -rn "\.input_schema" agents/` outside agents/core/llm/ hits only client.py:357 and the hub's own MCP-server side in route_tools.py), the only `MCPManager` instances are `orch.mcp` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:632, reached from agents/web.py:1790 and agents/web.py:1830 and routers/mcp.py for config and HUD only) and worldview_write.py:77, and agents/core/routers/mcp.py:105-112 and :269-270 expose only name/description/read_only to the HUD, never the schema. But the triage's grep was scoped wrong and missed a real production consumer of the dispatch path: agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:163 calls `self.mcp.call_tool(tool, mcp_args)` by bare name (it lives inside agents/core/mcp/, which their grep excluded). So `_resolve` is not dead code, and its bare-name path is live today.

Unreachability is a reason the remaining work is small and belongs inside the bridge PR — it is not a reason to record the row as done. Six of Hermes' nine clauses are unsatisfied or satisfied on only one of five provider paths, and no test anywhere exercises repair of a third-party `inputSchema`. Recording `equivalent` would put a false claim on a public status page; `partial` with a named remainder is the honest row. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. reviews.remaining: No provider-agnostic repair of a third-party MCP server's JSON Schema exists (re-verified at HEAD 2026-09-22, line numbers re-mapped 2026-09-23 after the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change, which touches none of this path; #1179 changed nothing on this path either — its client.py hunks are the stdio `cwd_secret_files` disclosure at :17-36, :58, :211-242 and :560-571; the only change since the 2026-09-07 stamping that bears on this row is #1152 adding a fifth unrepaired provider path, below). (1) `agents/core/mcp/client.py:584-601` `_list_tools` still stores `inputSchema` verbatim (`:592`) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (`:357`); add a `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` applied at registration. (2) Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path, verified by running the code: draft-07 `definitions`/`#/definitions/...` are never promoted to `$defs`/`#/$defs/...` (and `gemini_schema` silently reduces a `$ref` property to `{}`, deleting the shape), and a Pydantic nullable union `anyOf:[{...},{"type":"null"}], default:null` is never collapsed to its non-null branch (`gemini_schema` yields `anyOf:[{"type":"string"},{}]` with `default:null` retained on the Gemini path; the other four paths ship the raw nullable union untouched). (3) The three repairs that do exist (`required` pruned to declared names `:424-428`, missing `type` coerced `:421`, empty-OBJECT avoided `:447-449`) live only in `agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:369-451` and therefore apply to Gemini alone; the other four serialization paths pass `input_schema` through unrepaired: `anthropic_tools` (tool_dialects.py:147-151), `ToolSpec.as_openai` (tool_protocol.py:19-27; used by base.py:556, the Ollama path base.py:841 and openrouter.py:96), the OpenAI Responses payload (responses.py:73-82) and the xAI Responses payload (xai.py:79-80, whose `_payload` overrides responses.py's, added by #1152 on 2026-09-15). (4) No name sanitization or provider-legal prefixing: `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:367-370) is `server/tool`, whose `/` is outside the `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` function-name charset both Anthropic and OpenAI enforce, and nothing replaces characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`; `grep -rn "mcp__" agents/` returns nothing. (5) The row's security property — a third-party tool shadowing a built-in governed tool name — is unaddressed: `_resolve` (client.py:748-777) disambiguates only among `self.servers` (:768), never against the agent tool registry. (6) No test covers any of this; `grep -rln "gemini_schema" tests/` returns only tests/test_cloud_tool_turns.py, and neither test that constructs `MCPTool` (tests/test_mcp_hardening.py, tests/test_mcp_trust.py) asserts on `input_schema`. All of the above is currently unreachable by a model because no MCP-client -> tool-registry bridge exists (`MCPManager.get_tools()`, client.py:742-746, has zero callers repo-wide), so the normalizer plus its tests should land inside whichever PR first offers MCP client tools to the model, not as a standalone pure function — and that normalizer must sit at registration, ahead of all five dialect serializers, not inside `gemini_schema`.

reviews.summary: The model can read a document mid-turn through a tool call. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as its extracted text, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte).
reviews.remaining: Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: no .ipynb, .xlsx, .doc, .ppt, .odt, .rtf or .epub, and the text comes back plain rather than converted to Markdown. There is no size refusal for documents (Hermes refuses over 50 MB): the whole file is parsed again on every page request, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned. There is no scanned-page coverage warning naming the page ranges that yielded no text, which the row calls the clever half. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. A missing parser is named (`parser_missing`) rather than installed lazily.

reviews.summary: The owner's own chat attaches @file:path, @file:path#L10-40 and @file:"a b.md" for the turn. agents/core/context_refs.py holds the rules. expand (agents/core/context_refs.py:209) finds a reference that starts a word or follows an opening bracket, quote or backtick, and not one inside a word or a path (x@file:, a/@file:, @@file:) (_REF_RE, agents/core/context_refs.py:49); a double-quoted path may hold spaces, #L7 is one line and #L2-L3 a range, and trailing punctuation or a closing quote is not part of it. The routes keep the owner's message as typed: commands, skills, LLM-backend control, the router and memory see only it. The "--- Attached Context ---" section is bound to the turn (bind_attached, agents/core/context_refs.py:251; agents/web.py:1245 on /chat, and inside the stream task at agents/web.py:1312) and appended after the message only in the model prompt (attached_block, agents/core/context_refs.py:266; Orchestrator._build_agent_turn_text, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3331), so the file text is never stored as the owner's words, replayed in a later turn's history or embedded. Hermes keeps the expanded message in the user turn; Nerva shows the attachment to the model for the attaching (tainted) turn only. Each file's text is in a fence longer than any backtick run in it, so no line of it can close the fence (_fence, agents/core/context_refs.py:194), under a header that names the file as typed and the lines actually attached, `(line 7)` or `(lines 2-3)`, as attached file content, not instructions; injection patterns and a forged Attached Context marker are flagged in that header (`flagged: …`, _flags, agents/core/context_refs.py:180), not withheld. Each path is resolved through the same FileScope as file_read (_attach_one, agents/core/context_refs.py:133), so outside the file roots, .. traversal, a symlink escape and a secret-looking path such as .env are refused. A missing file, a directory, a binary file (a NUL in its first 8 KB), a bad line range, a range past the end, an unreadable file, an over-long name, a denied stat and an unknown ~user each become a one-line warning in the same section instead of failing the message. With JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS unset, the file tools' default root <data home>/workspace is used; only an unusable JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS makes the section say nothing was attached. The limits are 8 distinct references per message, 64 KB per reference and 128 KB in all, counted in bytes. A cut reference says so, and a repeated one is attached once. A line range skips the lines before it a 64K-character chunk at a time, up to 64M characters into the file (MAX_SCAN_CHARS; past it, the warning "line N is too far into the file"), keeps at most the byte budget and never reads a line whole (_read_lines, agents/core/context_refs.py:105); invalid UTF-8 is read with replacement characters. The expansion runs on /chat and /chat/stream (agents/web.py:1234, agents/web.py:1399), off the event loop, so both the HUD and nerva chat get it. It never runs for a channel message, as Hermes' gateway does not expand either. A turn that attached anything is tainted: handle_input and handle_input_stream call _taint_attached_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:357, :1966, :2169), which raises the turn's action origin to recall:untrusted. An action planned from attached content therefore escalates GRANT to QUEUE at the kernel, while an inbound turn keeps its more specific origin. complete (agents/core/context_refs.py:272) lists in-scope completions for what follows @file:, with directories ending in / and a path with a space quoted (a name no reference could name is left out). It shows dot files only when asked and never secret paths or links out of the roots, is bounded to 50 entries, and returns nothing for a prefix over 1,024 characters. GET /api/context-refs (agents/core/routers/commands.py:63, user-guarded, read-only) serves it and the reference types, and answers 503 file_roots_unusable when the roots cannot be used. The HUD composer (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:228, :283, frontend/src/context-refs.tsx) offers the reference types while `@` or `@fi` is typed (Tab takes `@file:`), then the in-scope paths; a list is shown only for the text it was fetched for. tests/test_h579_context_refs.py (70 cases) covers the bounds, parsing, whole files, line ranges (single, L-form, past the end), every refusal and warning, a symlink, punctuation, word starts, dedupe, the byte cut, the shared budget, the reference limit, an unreadable file, invalid UTF-8, the roots, an explicit scope and the marker; completion (prefixes, dot files, secrets, roots, a long prefix, a file or missing folder, the bound); both routes, the completion route, the turn taint on both paths, and an inbound turn. The review round added attached text never read as the owner's command (a slash command, a skill, a backend switch) and never stored or carried to a later turn, through the real routes; a file that cannot close its fence; injection and a forged marker flagged; a range in one huge line bounded in memory and a range of many short lines linear; a range too far into a file; quoted paths and their completion; references after brackets and quotes and not inside words; the distinct-reference limit; the header's path and lines; paths the system refuses to look at; and the roots. frontend/src/test/context-refs.test.tsx has 6 cases. The row's 53 mutants predate this code; the review round's 34: 28 caught at once, five after five cases were added, and one equivalent (a kept read stops at the budget either way, since readline(0) answers ""). OpenRouter provider routing ships, and the owner's changes reach the live backend on the next request. Six llm rows are seeded right after compatible_provider (agents/core/settings_db.py:171-176): openrouter_sort, openrouter_only, openrouter_ignore, openrouter_order, openrouter_require_parameters, and openrouter_data_collection, seeded deny. The HUD PUT /api/admin/settings/llm and `nerva config set` both validate through settings_db.validate_category, and the three slug lists share one slug check (agents/core/settings_db.py:842 -> agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:97). build_provider_block (agents/core/llm/provider_routing.py:110) turns the knobs into OpenRouter's `provider` object. It lower-cases and de-duplicates slugs, caps each list at 32, sends require_parameters only as a literal true, omits empty knobs, and raises on an invalid value instead of dropping it. HybridRouter.detect hands OpenRouterBackend a reader over the rows, not a snapshot (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:396). Before every text or tool-turn request the backend re-reads and re-validates them off the event loop (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:95, called at agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:168 and agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:207) and puts the object in the body (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:129). A HUD change, or a `nerva config set` run from another process against the same settings DB, therefore governs the next request, so the CLI's '(a running hub picks it up within 30 s)' holds for these rows. The object goes only to the openrouter profile, never to openai-compatible (agents/core/llm/openrouter.py:71). Nerva reads a project's convention files into the turn, as Hermes reads its context files and subdirectory hints. agents/core/project_context.py walks from the nearest git root (never above the file root) down to the working directory (llm.project_dir when it is a folder inside the roots, H218; else the first JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS root), and reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc in each directory in that order (CONVENTION_NAMES, candidates). A directory that the model's file_read, file_list or file_search touches is noted for the session (note_tool_path, bounded to 8 directories and 256 sessions); its chain is read on every later turn, and the tool's own result carries the files the turn had not seen yet, marked tainted so the loop fences it (attach; agents/core/file_tools.py _with_project_context). A script's file call (execute_code, no tool turn) brings none. A local terminal_run runs only after approval, from the queue and outside any turn: ToolRPCServer.handle records the queuing session (note_task, agents/core/tool_rpc.py), and when the approved command ran locally, note_terminal notes its cwd for that session, so its next turn reads the chain (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py _rpc_terminal_run). The command's own result goes to the task row, not to the model. A project SOUL.md, HEARTBEAT.md or IDENTITY.md is never read, not even through a symlink (HUB_FILES, _admit). Every file is resolved through FileScope (outside the roots, symlink escape and secret paths refused), must be a regular file (a FIFO is never opened), and is bounded to 20 KB, with 40 KB and 12 files a turn and 8 rules a directory, shared by parallel tool calls under the turn's lock; a cut says how much was shown, a file past the budget is named, and files past a count cap are counted (load_file, collect, render). Each file's text and name are scanned with detect_injection_normalized, plus Unicode TAG characters (decoded and scanned) and the fence's markers. A flagged file becomes a [BLOCKED ...] line naming the rules (injection_flag_names) with none of its text, and a flagged name is withheld; other names have non-printable characters escaped and undecodable bytes replaced. The caveated block, which holds the files in the untrusted-data fence, sits after the core-memory block in _build_agent_turn_text; _begin_project_context builds it off the event loop at turn start in both turn paths and marks the turn recall-tainted when any file was given, so an action planned from it escalates GRANT to QUEUE. A noted directory's files are in every later turn of the session, so those turns are tainted too: web_search, web_extract and memory writes refuse until the setting is off or the hub restarts. A guest's turn is given none of them. It is off with llm.project_context_files and in safe mode (layer project_context, named on the HUD banner). tests/test_h594_project_context.py: 66 cases. The original build's 51 mutants were all killed; the review round's fixes each come with a case that fails without them. reviews.summary: The three external intakes now honour an Idempotency-Key, so a retried request returns the original run instead of starting a second one. agents/core/idempotency.py holds the rules. parse_key (agents/core/idempotency.py:79) accepts 1-255 visible ASCII characters and refuses anything else with HTTP 400 invalid_idempotency_key. check_header (agents/core/idempotency.py:322) runs before the body is read. On POST /api/webhooks/{id} (after the hub's 503 not-initialized check) and on POST /api/a2a/task it also runs before the token, signature or peer is checked; POST /api/actions/request authenticates the caller first (user_guard), then checks the key. IdempotencyStore (agents/core/idempotency.py:105) keeps a SQLite row whose primary key is (scope, key), in the data folder (idempotency.db). reserve (agents/core/idempotency.py:147) runs inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so two workers or processes on the same file cannot both win (8 racing threads get exactly one reservation), and a reservation survives a restart. A row holds only the fingerprint (SHA-256 of method, path and body, each length-prefixed; agents/core/idempotency.py:88) and the public reference of what the request started, capped at 2 KB. It never holds the body, a reply or a credential. A retry with the same fingerprint returns that reference with Idempotent-Replayed: true, and nothing runs again. The same key with a different request gets 409 idempotency_key_reused. A retry while the first attempt is still running gets 409 idempotency_in_progress with Retry-After. A first attempt that raised or answered 5xx releases the key, so its retry runs. So does a webhook delivery whose agent turn produced no answer: an error or timeout marker from the hook's own target agent, a backend failure reply, the no-model line, a data-handling refusal or a refused turn, which the orchestrator answers as text instead of raising (is_failed_turn_reply, agents/core/orchestrator.py:110; _attempt_failed, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:583); and a deliver-only delivery whose push failed. The marker must name the hook's target exactly, and the target is not validated. A hook whose target is not a loaded agent id (a typo, "Jarvis", a removed agent) runs a routed turn, where the routed agent's "[jarvis timeout]" or "[jarvis error: …]" is not recognised. That delivery keeps its key, and a retry replays the failed turn. A turn that answered keeps its key even when its push failed. Each reservation carries a random attempt id, and complete, release and touch require it. A webhook delivery refreshes its row every 60 s while it runs (Claim.kept_alive, agents/core/idempotency.py:288); a row nothing refreshed for 600 s (its process died) is taken over under a new attempt id, so the first attempt can no longer finish or release it. A wall-clock jump larger than the window can still cause a take-over between heartbeats. Rows expire after 24 h, swept one bounded batch of 500 per reservation on a created_at index; a key's own expired row is dropped when that key is reserved. There is no per-scope row cap. The routes call the store through asyncio.to_thread, never on the event loop (a release on the exception path excepted). When the store cannot be written, a keyed request is refused with 503 idempotency_unavailable rather than run without its guarantee. That covers the reservation: an outcome that cannot be recorded afterwards is tried three times, then logged, and the row stays pending until it goes stale, after which a retry runs the request again. durable (agents/core/idempotency.py:129) says whether the store is a file rather than :memory:. The scope is the authenticated caller, and the key is reserved only after authentication and before anything is queued or run, so a duplicate never becomes a second approval item, kernel task or audit row. POST /api/actions/request (agents/core/routers/actions.py:76) reserves in the owner's action scope after the body is validated. A replay returns the queued action, or its id if the queue no longer holds it. POST /api/a2a/task (agents/core/routers/a2a.py:73-74) reserves in the scope a2a:<peer> only after the peer's signature verifies. A forged retry is refused with 401 and never reads the peer's receipt, and a refused task releases its key. The stored receipt is id, status and accepted. POST /api/webhooks/{id} (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:552) reserves in the scope webhook:<id> after the token or signature, the receiver switch and the enabled check, and before the delivery is counted, run or sent. _run_delivery (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:609) is the previous delivery body, unchanged. _public_outcome (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:603) keeps only ok, target, skipped and error; a replay answers those with the original status code, never the reply, steps or delivery. tests/test_h659_idempotency.py (90 cases) covers the key grammar, the fingerprint, and every store state: TTL, stale take-over, restart, two workers, a thread race, an in-memory store, the reference cap, an unreadable reference, and rollback on a file and in memory. It also covers the begin/claim mapping and all three routes: replay, conflict, no key, a malformed key checked first, an invalid body or unauthenticated caller not burning a key, a failed attempt released, scopes per hook and per peer, a skipped delivery replayed, and a forged A2A retry. The review round added fencing, the heartbeat, the bounded sweep and its index, per-key expiry, the migration of a file from before attempts, the outcome's retries, begin and done off the loop in all three routes, and the failed-turn and failed-push release rules. There are 57 mutants, all killed; the review round's 20 mutants: 19 killed (3 by tests added after a first pass) and 1 equivalent (PURGE_BATCH 500 to 5: the sweep test is written against the constant). reviews.summary: Oversized output is paged back from its spill file instead of being re-run. execute_code stdout/stderr are spooled to disk as they arrive (agents/core/code_tools.py:480, agents/core/tool_result_store.py:431) under <data root>/workspace/tool_results. Each stream is capped at DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES = 5,000,000 (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:130): StreamSpill.write stops writing at the cap but keeps counting (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:600), close appends one '[... spill capped at N bytes: M more bytes ...]' marker (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:642), and the result carries <stream>_spill_capped and <stream>_kept_bytes (agents/core/code_tools.py:274-275). Head and tail stay inline with omitted-byte accounting (agents/core/environments/output_limits.py:42, tests/test_environment_output_limits.py:38). A whole result the loop spills (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1421) keeps both ends in its preview (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:705-706, tests/test_tool_loop_result_spill.py:139), and file_read itself is never spilled (tests/test_tool_loop_result_spill.py:287). Every notice carries the exact call from page_recipe (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:145): file_read(path="<resolved path>", offset=0, max_bytes=N). The same arguments are returned as <stream>_read_with (agents/core/code_tools.py:272) and read_with (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:736), and stream recipes propose pages of at most 8,000 bytes (agents/core/code_tools.py:226). file_read takes an integer offset from 0 to MAX_OFFSET = 2**53-1 (agents/core/file_tools.py:123, agents/core/file_tools.py:1517). Anything else is refused as bad_offset, both in the preflight and in a direct call (agents/core/file_tools.py:1436, agents/core/file_tools.py:742). An offset at or past the end is an empty final page, answered without seeking (agents/core/file_tools.py:760). A page that stops early returns next_offset (agents/core/file_tools.py:1291) and never ends inside a UTF-8 character (agents/core/file_tools.py:1243). A .pdf/.docx pages through its extracted text (agents/core/file_tools.py:1295). The named call is one file_read answers in every live setup, including the three the review found broken. The recipe path is resolved (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:207). A spill is never named like a secret (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:190). file_read alone gets a read-only door for exact spill-file names in the coordinator's spill directory (agents/core/file_tools.py:650, agents/core/file_tools.py:687, agents/core/file_tools.py:1208), wired at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1011. So JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS pointing elsewhere, a symlinked JARVIS_HOME or a bridged tool with a secret-looking name no longer strands the file (tests/test_spill_paging.py:507, tests/test_spill_paging.py:535); the door's limits are pinned by tests/test_spill_paging.py:414. The recipe is named only where that call is answered. ToolResultStore.readable(path) (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:361) asks the coordinator probe (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1015). The probe requires four things: file_read registered, allowed by the job toolset, in this turn's profile offer (noted at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1169), and able to open this very path (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1027, agents/core/file_tools.py:715). execute_code also requires file_read in its own run's offer (agents/core/code_tools.py:462, agents/core/code_tools.py:559). Otherwise the notice says the file is kept for the owner and cannot be paged from this turn (tests/test_spill_paging.py:545, tests/test_spill_paging.py:589, tests/test_code_tools.py:866), and concurrent turns each see their own offer (tests/test_spill_paging.py:627). A failed spill just omits the path (agents/core/code_tools.py:258-259, tests/test_code_tools.py:698). Retention is unchanged (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:490, tests/test_tool_result_store.py:214, tests/test_tool_result_store.py:353). End to end, a real AgentToolRuntime follows read_with and then next_offset through the real file_read and rebuilds the spilled result byte for byte, while the producing tool runs once (tests/test_spill_paging.py:719). execute_code stdout does the same on the one-shot and session paths (tests/test_code_tools.py:824), and a runaway stream stops at its ceiling with one marker (tests/test_code_tools.py:877, tests/test_spill_paging.py:233). Adaptations: offsets are bytes, not Hermes' lines. The 5,000,000-byte cap covers streamed spills, which is Hermes' execute_code scope; whole-result JSON spills stay bounded by the 256 MB retention sweep. A spill stays third-party when it comes back: every file directly in a spill directory counts as one (agents/core/file_tools.py:701), a file_read page of it and a file_search whose matches reach it declare tainted (agents/core/file_tools.py:767, agents/core/file_tools.py:919), and the loop fences the result as DATA and raises the turn's recall taint, in the turn that spilled it or any later one (tests/test_spill_paging.py:761, tests/test_spill_paging.py:812, tests/test_spill_paging.py:834, tests/test_spill_paging.py:856). A trusted tool's spill counts too, because a spill's file name cannot say reliably which tool wrote it.

Built in #1207 and fixed after one adversarial review (review-H666: no major; five minors and eight nits, all fixed). Hermes nests the agent's subtasks with one optional parent on each todo item (the id of another item) instead of a nested array, so merge-by-id keeps working, and draws the list through one defensive tree builder. Nerva now does both, for the todo tool's items and for mission plan steps.

The tree builder:
- agents/core/todo_tree.py tree() (agents/core/todo_tree.py:48) returns (item, depth) pairs in depth-first order, children in list order under their parent, with every item exactly once. It is stdlib only, because the CLI imports it.
- Depth is capped at MAX_DEPTH = 4 (agents/core/todo_tree.py:30); a deeper item is drawn at depth 4, under its parent.
- An item whose parent is missing, itself, or not an id at all is drawn at depth 0 in its place (agents/core/todo_tree.py:65). ref() accepts only text or whole numbers as ids; a bool, a fractional float, a list or a dict is no id, and a whole-valued float is its number, as JSON's 1.0 is 1 to the HUD (agents/core/todo_tree.py:33). When two items share an id, the first holds it. Anything that is not a list is an empty tree.
- Cycle members, and anything under them, are reached from no root, so they are appended flat at depth 0 in list order (agents/core/todo_tree.py:78). A getter that raises counts as no parent. The walk uses an explicit stack, so a 5,000-item chain costs no recursion.
- The HUD's twin is frontend/src/todo-tree.ts todoTree() (frontend/src/todo-tree.ts:28), with the same rules. Both suites read one shared file of 47 cases, frontend/src/test/todo-tree-cases.json (hand-written shapes plus seeded random ones over text, number, whole and fractional float, bool, null, list and dict ids and parents), and assert the same drawn order and depths. The review's fuzz had found the twins differing on whole-valued floats; that is fixed and pinned.

The todo tool:
- An item may carry parent: the id of the item it sits under. It is an allowed item field (agents/core/todo_tool.py:84) and is in the schema as a string of at most MAX_ID (agents/core/todo_tool.py:102); the description tells the model how to nest and un-nest.
- _clean_parent (agents/core/todo_tool.py:197) cleans it like an id. Empty or whitespace-only text means no parent, as Hermes clears it. Anything else that is not an id is refused as todo_bad_parent, with a sentence the model can act on, and changes nothing.
- A parent need not name an item in the list: a dangling, self or cyclic parent is stored and drawn at the top, never refused and never lost.
- On a merge, parent null means not sent (as for content and status), and "" clears it. A changed parent counts as a write, so the plan cap applies. A parent moved by an untrusted turn taints the item, as a status does. Re-sending the same parent changes nothing: no taint, and the plan's labels stay (agents/core/todo_tool.py:400).
- model_items answers the parent only when it is set (agents/core/todo_tool.py:227), so a flat list answers exactly as before and plan_bytes counts a parent's bytes.

Mission plan steps:
- MissionStore.create (agents/core/autonomy/missions.py:203) gives every step a nullable parent. _plan_step (agents/core/autonomy/missions.py:390) reads each entry.
  - A title, or any other value, is a top-level step with its own text, as before; a mapping without title or parent is still stringified.
  - {title, parent?} may sit under an earlier step: parent is that step's index, and only an earlier one. A plan is therefore a forest by construction.
  - Anything else is refused as bad_plan_step: a self, later, out-of-range, negative, bool, text or float parent, a missing or blank title, or an unknown key.
- POST /api/missions (agents/core/routers/missions.py:50) accepts such a plan. A bad step answers 400 with one fixed sentence and code bad_plan_step (agents/core/routers/missions.py:73); no request data reaches the body.
- The build-queue plan kept out-of-range and self parents on mission steps and let the tree degrade them. The store refuses them instead: a mission plan is written once, by its creator, so a bad parent there is a caller's mistake worth a 400. The tree still degrades any step the store did not check, such as a row written before this change, which has no parent key. A legacy entry {title, <other key>} is now refused too; nothing in the repo sends one.
- finish_step budget charging and the completion gates are unchanged. A child step is charged like any step, closing a child does not close its parent, and exhausting the budget still auto-fails the mission.

Rendering:

Code execution no longer keeps its files on the system temp root. Where a Sandbox built without an explicit work_dir makes its run directory, first match wins: JARVIS_EXEC_TEMP_DIR in the process environment, then the owner's security.sandbox_temp_dir setting, then the managed cache <data root>/cache/exec (resolve_root, agents/core/exec_cache.py:149). A value that is not an absolute path, or cannot be read as one (a relative path, ~nosuchuser, a NUL byte), is skipped with a warning (_as_root, agents/core/exec_cache.py:117), and the setting refuses such a value on write, as it refuses an age outside 1-8760 hours (agents/core/settings_db.py:796); a choice that names the managed cache, however spelled (through a link or a '..'), is the managed cache, compared by identity (_same_dir, agents/core/exec_cache.py:138). Each run directory is an absolute private mkdtemp (mode 0700, named nerva-sandbox-*) under a root made 0700 when this user owns it; a root that cannot be used gives the system temp directory for that run, with a warning, unmanaged and never pruned (new_work_dir, agents/core/exec_cache.py:177). The Sandbox takes it at construction (agents/core/sandbox.py:85); the orchestrator's one production sandbox (agents/core/orchestrator.py:644) passes no work_dir, so it gets the managed cache. A run directory removed under a live sandbox, or there without its lock or wider than 0700, is made again 0700 and its lock taken again before the next run, and the tool-RPC runtime asks for that before it makes its mailbox inside the directory (agents/core/tool_rpc_runtime.py:381) (ensure_work_dir, agents/core/sandbox.py:100). Docker bind-mounts it with --mount, CSV-quoted, so a ':', ',', '"' or line break in the data root is data (_bind_mount, agents/core/sandbox.py:29). A managed run directory's lock lives outside it, in <root>/.locks/<name>.lock, where code run in the directory cannot remove, replace or forge it: an flock held for the sandbox's lifetime, recording host, pid, whether the flock was taken, the kernel's boot id and the pid's start time, written under a private temporary name and renamed into place so it is never seen empty and a link planted at its name is never written through, in a .locks directory that is private and not a link, and released (closed, then removed, as Windows needs) when the sandbox is gone (release, agents/core/exec_cache.py:312; hold, agents/core/exec_cache.py:257). Each run directory is aged as one group: the newest date anywhere inside it, links never followed, dates the whole directory (_newest, agents/core/exec_cache.py:327), a file being dated by the older of its mtime and ctime so a date set in the future never keeps it forever (_date, agents/core/exec_cache.py:323). Both refreshes from Hermes's row exist (`agents/core/session_refresh.py`, the parked mechanism commit 89b53e85 cherry-picked unchanged; its module docstring has since gained a note on where each half is wired) and are wired at Nerva's two compaction boundaries, each failing in its own direction. **Nerva is turn-based, so most of the row was already true between turns and is pinned as such**: `Orchestrator._prompt_context` reads the skills catalog per turn, the plugin block is rendered per turn, and `AgentToolRuntime._run_loop` resolves ToolRPC → capability registry → tool profile at the top of every run (`test_between_turns_the_offer_was_already_live`). Two things were not live. **(1) The system prompt.** `Agent._load_soul` ran once in `__init__` and `orchestrator.py` sent `agent.soul["content"]` for the life of the process, so a persona edited or quarantined mid-session needed a restart. `Agent._read_soul` is the one builder (same file resolution, same H387 scan, same cap) behind both `_load_soul` and `Agent.refresh_soul`, and `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` (orchestrator.py, a module function so the bare-stub tests of that path keep working) calls it for every agent from `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` — after the clock CAS, never before it, and pinned as such: a refused `commit_clock` migrates nothing, an accepted one is followed by the refresh in that order. In front of the builder sits an `os.stat` probe (`_soul_signature`: resolved path, inode, size, mtime, ctime and the body cap), because once a session is over budget the conversation-level commit happens on **every** turn — `ContextCompressor.compact()` recomputes from the raw turns each call — and the walk is process-wide: an unchanged persona costs one stat, and only a file whose kernel signature moved reaches the builder (measured over the 18 shipped SOULs, 76 KB: 59.0 ms → 0.55 ms per boundary, 18 → 0 reads and scans). A file written within the last two seconds has no trusted signature (git's racy rule: a same-size edit in the same timestamp tick would be invisible to a stat) and is read and compared by bytes until it ages. Past the probe the keep path is byte equality of the builder's whole output — body *and* front-matter, so a tier or trait edit with the same body is adopted and the HUD's `soul["meta"]` follows — never a dirty flag; a builder that throws keeps the last-good bytes (fails OPEN); a file absent for the instant of an editor's save-by-rename keeps them with a plain warning, and an agent that had no persona and still has none is unchanged, not failed. A scan verdict is not a failure — a persona that is now mostly injection is dropped exactly as a restart would drop it — and it is announced exactly as a restart announces it: `_announce_soul_verdict` is the one place both moments log, so a quarantine at the boundary is the H387 ERROR line, not an INFO line. **(2) The tool set inside one turn.** A loop of up to `llm.tool_loop_max_iterations` model turns kept the list it resolved at the top. `_run_loop` treats a committed fold (`_compact_context` grew `compacted`) as the boundary and re-resolves through `_resolve_offer` (the same three steps, minus the turn-start side effects) via `session_refresh.refresh_tools`, which fails CLOSED: a resolver that raises withdraws every tool, an empty resolution is a revocation, and either ends the loop with `_TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY` after a `tool_loop_withdrawn` event rather than asking a provider a turn on a stale or empty list. The offer and the executor move together (`_specs_for` rebuilds the specs, the gate map the executor checks `offered` against, and the untrusted set) — pinned by a tool withdrawn through the *profile* while still registered in ToolRPC, the one shape that can tell the executor's `tool_not_allowed` from the RPC's own (keeping the stale gate map runs the handler, and that test goes red). Between folds the registry is not consulted at all, so the set stays stable between two folds; Nerva's fold happens inside one user turn, so Hermes's "mid-turn tool sets stay stable" reads here as *between folds*. A `tool_offer_refreshed` event (added/removed/reason) is written only when something moved. 17 mechanism tests (`tests/test_session_refresh.py`, red-proofed by mutation in the parked commit) plus 26 wiring tests (`tests/test_h672_compaction_refresh.py`). An independent review of the first cut found 14 items (4 major, 6 minor, 4 nits: the per-turn, process-wide re-read cost; the H387 verdict suppressed at the boundary; the overclaim that `ToolRPC.handle` refuses profile revocations; the unpinned gate map and CAS order; the front-matter blind spot; the traceback for a persona-less agent; the docstrings); 13 are addressed here and each code fix was neutered once and shown red (8 mutations, 11 distinct tests red). reviews.remaining: **The boundaries are opt-in, so on a shipped default nothing migrates**: the conversation-level commit exists only with `memory.context_compression` on (default off) and the in-turn fold only with `llm.tool_loop_enabled` on (default off) — a default install still needs a restart for a persona edit, exactly as before. **Profile revocations are not enforced on the execution path**: `ToolRPCServer.handle` checks the job toolset, registration and the gate, never the tool profile, and the executor's gate map is rebuilt only at a fold — so in a loop that never folds (small results, the common shape) a tool the profile withdrew mid-turn stays offered *and* executes until the loop ends; pre-existing, unchanged by this slice, pinned as a limit by `test_between_folds_a_profile_revocation_is_not_enforced_by_the_executor_either`. **The persona migration is process-wide**: `orchestrator.agents` is every agent and `agent.soul` is the one dict every session's system prompt reads, so the session that commits migrates the persona for all sessions (the boundary log line says so); refreshing only the routed agents would need the route at `_history_for_prompt`, which it does not have. **On the staged shared-route path the turn's budget is computed against the persona in force before the commit** (`_shared_route_plan` → `build()` measures `agent.soul` while planning; the refresh runs in `accept()` → `publish()`), so a persona that grew is sent that turn with a budget computed for the old size — bounded by `_soul_max_chars`, self-correcting next turn; the H363 cached prefix and the H673 usage anchor under-count for one turn after a rebuild the same way. The probe trusts the kernel's signature; what the builder reads outside the file (the scan patterns) is code and needs a restart. The prompt half covers the SOUL only: Nerva's plugin and skills sections live in the user prompt and were already per-turn, so there is no plugin section in the system prompt to fail open — the fail-open is exercised on the SOUL builder. The in-turn boundary does not rebuild `messages[0]`: a persona change reaches the *next* turn, not the loop in flight. "A newly configured MCP server appears without a restart" is only as true as the MCP manager's registration into ToolRPC is hot, which this slice did not verify. The lineage row stays at `nerva.context-compaction.v1`; the boundary note is a log line plus the runtime event, not a field on the row. `refresh_tools` compares names, so a tool whose schema changed under the same name is adopted only because the fresh list is taken whenever the set moved, never on its own. The stale comment at `agents/core/file_tools.py` saying `_load_soul` runs no injection scan predates H387 and is left for a hygiene commit (it would drift five unrelated rows). Nine ledger rows cite `agent.py`, `agent_runtime.py` or `orchestrator.py` and were drifted by this branch (and by #1188 on main: its registry path in `orchestrator.py`, and the pairing kwarg, refusal branch and lifespan hand-over in `telegram.py` and `web.py`, which H146, H449, H364 and H671 also cite and were read against — the pairing store is not their subject); each was re-read against the diff on its cited paths before its hashes moved. Six keep their text and take fresh stamps — H146, H298, H363, H364, H449, H679: the in-turn re-resolution runs through `_profiled`, which still applies the job toolset on both sides of the profile, and the result-spill, cache, reasoning and job-pin mechanism those rows cite is untouched. Three are rewritten — H387: the ERROR line now comes from `_announce_soul_verdict` behind the `_read_soul` builder, for boot and boundary alike; H671 and H673: `publish()` re-reads the personas after the clock CAS, and the staged-route budget limit above is now on H673's own row. The 16 other needs_review rows on main (H060, H061, H068, H071, H104, H108, H130, H135, H139, H398, H477, H510, H523, H683 from #1188's edits to `orchestrator.py`, `web.py` and `telegram.py`; H288 and H684 from #1187's `heartbeat.py` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`) are main's own drift, not this branch's, and are left untouched here; #1187's five-line comment in `orchestrator.py` re-drifted the nine rows above once more, and they were re-read against it and re-stamped.

Ollama and LM Studio structured tool turns now retain the provider-reported input/output token counts. Strict count normalization preserves valid answers when usage metadata is absent or malformed. Tool-loop usage accumulates for metering while context anchors replace with the latest request count; unavailable input does not erase a prior anchor. Gemini structured turns now retain inclusive prompt counts and disjoint candidate/thought output counts; explicitly OpenAI-compatible profiles retain standard prompt/completion totals without adding nested breakdowns. Complete context anchors now include Anthropic disjoint input/cache-read/cache-write counts, including cache-only requests, while totals-only mappings count the full prompt once. Billing semantics remain unchanged. Complete non-stream text replies now publish provider usage through closed request-local observers. Non-stream agent gathers retain per-agent measurements and complete-prefix anchors; ToolRuntime remains the single structured-turn reporter. Retries publish only accepted response usage; cancellation and inherited late tasks cannot outlive the observer. Public string/stream signatures and guardrails are unchanged. OpenRouter inherited streaming reports its single complete text request once. Ollama, LM Studio and Anthropic actual streams now publish one measurement only after confirmed completion: literal done=true, usage-only snapshot plus [DONE], or valid start/final cumulative message_delta usage plus message_stop respectively. Errors, interruption, malformed frames/containers and missing final usage do not reuse intermediate counts. Retry state resets, disjoint cache categories and text callbacks remain intact. Gemini streams now retain a terminal response's own validated prompt/candidate/thought counts after clean HTTP exhaustion and response close. Known single-candidate completion or explicit blocked-prompt semantics are required; errors, raw trailers, cancellation, conflicting response identities and nonzero/malformed candidate indices invalidate the whole attempt. Retries remain isolated and answer callbacks are unchanged. Pinned ask jobs now resolve and freeze their model/window before history construction, cap completion, and omit an unrelated prior usage anchor; unchanged default models retain their existing estimate. Ordinary tool turns now also use immutable configured/cached backend capacity forwarded before guardrails; known limits include completion, initial/later transcript, schemas and structured tool-call arguments. Unknown capacity remains estimated rather than discovered. Reasoning integration was reviewed against previously-current grid33165622 evidence: request-shaping refusals/empty controls do not change this row's cache, session or context/usage semantics. Existing focused regressions are retained. Responses completed text/tool turns and validated terminal streams now retain reported input/output usage. Inclusive input totals split cached_tokens once into disjoint uncached input and cache_read; output reasoning detail is not added to output totals. Missing/malformed metadata does not invent counts. Stream errors, incomplete/contradictory terminal items, cancellation or failed close do not publish usage; request-local sinks preserve existing single-publication semantics. The xAI Responses dialect inherits the same strict reported input/output/cache split and complete terminal accounting, while its own completed-response acceptance rechecks reasoning/replay lifetimes. Reasoning token detail is not added twice to output totals. Opaque function replay preserves main-loop provider usage without introducing ciphertext persistence, per-vendor prices or cache discount assumptions. Shared history compression now preplans each actual governed specialist route and its finite or dynamic completion reserve instead of borrowing the router default model. The strictest input budget stages one shared summary; final prompts/routes are revalidated through at most three monotonically tightening passes before a single accepted clock/history publication. Prepared text/SSE dispatch preserves backend/model/session/lifetime identity, policy gates and known-versus-estimated context metadata. Selected Ollama resolves its own context. Usage anchors require matching backend/model, session generation and retained-history digest; unmanaged old anchors are not promoted to exact managed measurements. Existing disabled-compression behavior and direct local auto output remain unchanged. Since H672 the accepted clock/history publication is followed by the persona re-read (`_refresh_souls_at_boundary`, after the CAS): it changes nothing in how pressure is measured or anchored, but on the staged shared-route path `_shared_route_plan` measured `agent.soul` while planning and the refresh runs in `accept()` → `publish()`, so a persona that grew at that boundary is sent that turn with a budget planned for the old size — bounded by `_soul_max_chars`, and the next response's usage anchor measures the real prompt. #1188's edit to `orchestrator.py` is the pairing store's registry path, nothing on this row. reviews.summary: A compaction summary no longer holds the owner's turn past a short bound, and a silent summarizer is cut. Hermes keeps two clocks: how long the summary may make the user wait, and how long the summarizer may go quiet. Nerva awaited the strict-local summarizer inline with neither. Its only limit was the httpx read timeout (120 s for Ollama), a total-duration wait on a non-streaming call, and nothing told the owner. (1) Bounded hold. ContextCompressor takes a gate (agents/core/context_compressor.py:325, used at :596). The orchestrator builds it per turn (_summary_gate, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3841, passed at :3975) around SummaryHold (agents/core/compaction_hold.py:136). SummaryHold.wait (:146) waits at most memory.compression_max_turn_hold_seconds for the LLM summary (settings_db.py:276; default 10 s, 0 = never wait, clamped 0..120 by hold_seconds, compaction_hold.py:63). One summary per session is written at a time: a turn that finds one still in flight neither waits on it again nor starts a second. Past the hold the turn goes on without the summary, and compress marks the result summary_deferred (context_compressor.py:621). compact (:524) then sends the turns verbatim, their old images dropped, when they still fit the window under the owner's memory.compression_max_tokens; otherwise it sends the deterministic digest. The summary keeps being written. When it lands it seeds this session's iterative-merge prior (_ctx_summary_cache), but only if no newer turn has replaced the prior this turn started from, and never through the compaction-clock CAS: publish commits only what the prompt was built from, and never writes the digest over the pending summary (orchestrator.py:4064). A turn cancelled while it waits (Stop, a client gone) still leaves its summary for the next turn. A summary that fails later seeds nothing and is logged by name. aclose stops what is still being written within the task budget (orchestrator.py:4762; SummaryHold.aclose, compaction_hold.py:185). (2) The owner is told. record_turn_notice (agents/core/turn_notices.py:35; a per-turn sink collected like turn_approvals, one notice per code) carries DEFERRED_NOTICE (compaction_hold.py:38) out as notices on /chat (ChatResponse.notices, agents/web.py:1102, TurnNotice :1085) and on every /chat/stream end event, the failed one included (:1363, :1369). The HUD shows each notice as a system line under the reply (frontend/src/turn-notices.ts, app.tsx:352). The hub log says the summary was deferred and, later, that it landed. (3) Inactivity deadline. The summarizer now streams (stream_summary, compaction_hold.py:88, called at agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:136). It is cut after memory.compression_summary_idle_seconds with nothing received (settings_db.py:277; default 60 s, up to 600, no "off": idle_seconds, compaction_hold.py:71). Any chunk counts as life: a visible token, and a reasoning chunk that shows no text, through the new on_activity callback on the Ollama and LM Studio streams (agents/core/llm/base.py:677, :907). A slow stream that keeps talking is never cut. A cut stream is cancelled and given CLOSE_GRACE (1 s) to close its HTTP response. A backend with no stream is awaited whole. A degraded reply ("⚠️ …", "[backend error …]") or an empty one is now a failure, and so the digest is used. Before, the non-streaming generate could hand an error text over as the summary. Tests: tests/test_h674_compaction_hold.py (52) covers both settings, the idle deadline (silent, slow-but-talking, token-only, thinking, degraded, no stream), the hold (in time, at the bound, single flight, zero, cancelled wait, late failure, failure within the hold, aclose), the compressor's deferral (digest, verbatim when it fits, owner's budget, covered with a prior), and the orchestrator: the turn going on at the hold, the late summary seeding the next turn, a newer prior never overwritten, no clock commit for the deferred summary, the idle setting reaching the summarizer, aclose. It also covers the notice on /chat and every stream end event, the collector unbound after /chat, and on_activity on both local streams. frontend src/test/turn-notices.test.ts covers the HUD. 72 mutants: 70 caught after nine survivors got cases. Two were equivalent. m23 (busy ignoring done()) is equivalent because the done callback always pops the flight first. The other was a redundant typeof check in the HUD helper, which was removed. The phase-2, H20.3 and compaction-policy suites pass unchanged. The AUD-7 and H677 end-event and reply pins gain the notices key. reviews.summary: Boot now waits for the local model before it accepts work, and every shutdown wait has a short explicit budget. (1) Warm-up gate. load_agents still starts LLMRouter.warm_up as a background task (agents/core/orchestrator.py:961). The web lifespan now waits for it before orch.start_channels(): gate_warmup (agents/core/lifecycle_budget.py:102, called at agents/web.py:631). The wait is bounded by system.startup_warmup_timeout_seconds (settings_db.py:392; default 20 s, 0 = do not wait, clamped to 0..300 by warmup_timeout, lifecycle_budget.py:37; a bad value keeps the default). The HTTP app is not served before the lifespan yields, so /chat waits too. On expiry the gate logs the setting's name, opens anyway, and the warm-up finishes in the background; the gate never cancels it. WARMUP (WarmupState, :51, :99) holds off / warming / ready / cold (warm_up answered False: nothing local to warm) / failed (raised or cancelled), the gate_expired flag, and the seconds it took (frozen when it ends). GET /api/status (routers/status.py:120) and /readyz (routers/ops.py:143) report it; it is never a reason to be not-ready. A turn served while it is still warming is marked: ChatResponse.warming (web.py:1099, :1254), every end event of the stream, the failed turn's included (:1363, :1369), and a log line for channel turns (orchestrator.py:1654). (2) Shutdown budgets. bounded (lifecycle_budget.py:128) runs one step for at most its budget, logs an overrun or an error by name and moves on; a step that ignores cancellation is abandoned, never awaited. wait_task (:147) cancels a background task and waits at most its budget. ChannelManager.stop_all bounds each channel's stop at 3 s (channels/manager.py:126). _cancel_task bounds each cancelled task at 2 s (orchestrator.py:1452). stop_channels bounds the Oracle watcher and plugin close_all (:1472, :1475). aclose bounds the checkpoint flush, each context-cache task, the warm-up task, the LLM router, the Ollama client, MCP, the context cache, the plugin HTTP clients and each channel's aclose (:4718-4767). So one wedged step costs its budget, not the service manager's stop budget. The budgets are per step; there is no total deadline, so several wedged steps still add up. (3) Per-chat lanes. ChatLanes (agents/core/channels/chat_lanes.py:24) runs a chat's turns in order and different chats side by side, at most 8 turns at once. A failed turn never stalls its lane. drain (:66) gives the lanes a bounded time at stop, cancels what is left and names how many it abandoned. Telegram's poll loop creates the lanes (channels/telegram.py:533) and hands each batched turn (_deliver_turn, :833), each button tap (:586), each observed group line (:769) and each reply that may answer a decision-reason prompt (:639) to its chat's lane through _in_chat (:839). Work with no chat waits for every lane first (settle), so H117's order holds: what a chat said before a tap is handled first. The loop goes straight back to reading, so one slow answer, or a 180 s lease wait, no longer holds other chats. stop() and the loop's exit drain the lanes within 2 s (LANE_DRAIN_BUDGET, :59). The voice-reply mark (H071 "voice for voice") is taken when a note is read, while the chat's previous turn may still be running; the note's turn now carries it into its lane (_voice_pending, :323, :1011; _deliver_turn; _run_turn, :852) and sets it only when it runs, so the earlier, typed, reply is never the one spoken. Tests: tests/test_h677_boot_and_shutdown.py (51) covers the setting, every gate phase, the lifespan order, status/readyz, the /chat and stream marks, the channel-turn log, bounded and wait_task, a hung channel stop, a stubborn task, a hung aclose step, a source pin that no teardown await is bare, lane order, concurrency, failures, bound, drain and settle, Telegram reading the next update while a chat is answered, and a voice note read while its chat is busy keeping its own spoken reply. The H117 batching and Telegram suites pass unchanged. 84 mutants, all caught after cases were added (a cancelled or None-returning warm-up, the frozen duration, a zero budget, cold vs failed, an abandoned step's cancel and late error, lane order after an earlier turn ends, drain cancelling, the poll loop's own lanes, a tap in another chat, cache-task cleanup, the warm-up cancelled at close, the budgets nesting); one was equivalent (asyncio.shield around asyncio.wait, which never cancels) and the shield was removed. Building the lanes exposed a regression they would have introduced (the voice mark taken by the busy chat's earlier reply), fixed red-first. reviews.summary: Re-read on main at 55d625f4. Telegram has the partial-then-edit mechanism: TelegramDraft (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:116) sends the first token as a message, then edits it in place through _edit_message (telegram.py:459) at most once per STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL (telegram.py:57, 1.2 s) and only when the visible text changed; finish() (telegram.py:189) settles the final text in the streamed message, sends overflow as new messages, retries markup Telegram rejects as plain text and falls back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. The adapter declares supports_edit=True (telegram.py:232) and exposes begin_stream (telegram.py:475). The real caller is Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1659), invoked for every non-observed channel turn (orchestrator.py:1535): it opens a draft only when the adapter has begin_stream, its descriptor says supports_edit, the owner setting channels.streaming_replies is on (orchestrator.py:1667) and the delivery router would send to this source; the turn then runs through handle_input_stream with on_token=draft.push (orchestrator.py:1656) and draft.finish (orchestrator.py:1580) replaces the whole-reply send. The conservative default is declarative rather than a stub: ChannelDescriptor.supports_edit defaults to False (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:36), so an adapter that declares nothing gets the whole reply. Slack and Discord are deliberately excluded from streaming (orchestrator.py:1664) because their replies go through the governed channel.reply approval queue (_queue_workspace_reply, orchestrator.py:1589-1590); test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens pins that an editable transport alone cannot publish tokens before that approval. Tests: 82 passed, 1 skipped (tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py needs slack_sdk, absent on this box) across tests/test_telegram_streaming.py, tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py and tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py. #1188's change to telegram.py (the process's shared SenderPairing handed in at construction, deeplink pairing refused when none is wired) does not touch the draft, edit or send paths. Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability.
reviews.remaining: (1) No edit or delete in the base contract: ChannelAdapter (agents/core/channels/base.py:14) still declares only abstract start/stop/send plus receive, and no adapter implements a delete operation (no delete_message or deleteMessage anywhere in agents/), so a sealed streamed preview cannot be removed and there is no base method that fails loudly for a channel that cannot edit; the fallback to a whole reply is silent. (2) Slack and Discord do not stream: both descriptors declare supports_edit=True (agents/core/channels/slack.py:102, agents/core/channels/discord.py:32) but neither adapter implements begin_stream or an edit call (Slack's send posts via chat_postMessage only, slack.py:335), and _begin_channel_draft refuses both because a streamed draft would publish tokens before the channel.reply approval; streaming there needs an approval contract that covers output not yet generated. (3) No acknowledgement at ingest: Telegram sends a typing chat action only while reading an inbound attachment (telegram.py:998) and a record_voice action before a spoken reply, so an ordinary text message gets no receipt signal until the first streamed token or the whole reply; Slack and Discord send none (the Slack Socket Mode envelope ack is a transport ack to Slack, not a signal the sender sees).
